## v2 forensics (V2_ADAPTER_FORENSICS.md) -- CORRECTS my earlier same-day diagnoses. 2026-10-11
A full read-only investigation of ALL 5 adapter traces + 5 matching v6 no-adapter traces (not the one-grep
diagnoses I logged above) overturns my earlier conclusions. CORRECTED findings:
- ANCHOR-MISMATCH is NOT the failure. Of 17 edit_file calls, exactly 1 was anchor-mismatch, and it self-
  corrected next call. The harness edit_file has an "unescaped" fallback that AUTO-UNESCAPES literal \n, so the
  exact byte-faithfulness skill the whole LoRA targets is SILENTLY TOLERATED by the scorer. My "edit-anchor wall
  survives" verdict (logged above) was wrong -- generalized from a single grepped call.
- REAL failure #1: SEARCH-DEATH on 3/5 tasks (4079, 4076, 3469) -- zero edit attempts, burned 15 calls on
  grep/pytest/read, empty patches. The adapter DEGRADED the agent's convergence/commit-to-edit ability. On
  rich_4079 it reached rich/markdown.py (the file v6 edits to resolve) and never edited it = REGRESSION.
- REAL failure #2: MALFORMED-TOOLCALL serialization bug on rich_4070 -- 11+ identical broken edit_file calls
  where old_string collapses into a JSON key with a stray `,old_string: suffix. Specific to edit_file's two-
  string payload (run_command is never corrupted). Inferred cause: training-data tool-call TEMPLATE shape makes
  the model run the two strings together. NOT measured against the training set yet.
- rich_4077 ("our 1/5 win") resolved IN SPITE of the adapter; v6 resolves it identically with no adapter. NO
  task the adapter resolved that v6 didn't; NO sub-step better; every delta neutral or negative. Adapter is
  purely subtractive (1/5 vs v6 2/5 on shared tasks).
IMPLICATION: all my proposed next steps (retrain cooler, add negatives, sweep alpha) targeted the ANCHOR SKILL,
which is not broken. Correct targets per evidence: (1) the edit_file serialization template in the training
data; (2) the convergence/search-death regression. Also: the FREE gate CANNOT cleanly test the anchor skill
because the harness auto-unescapes \n -- need a raw-old_string-match observation to test it at all.
PROCESS NOTE (user-flagged): stop diagnosing from one grep of one trace. This forensic pass is the standard now.


## Literature pull (2026-10-11) -- confirms the v2 forensic + names the v3 fix. Rephrased; sources linked.
Searched LLM/agent tuning lit for the TWO forensic-named failures (tool-call format corruption; commitment).
Findings (not image-domain -- directly agentic/tool-call):
- FORMAT CORRUPTION is a known data-centric problem: data-centric SFT cut tool-call parse failures 87%->~1%
  (arXiv 2603.16901). Training on a BADLY FORMATTED tool dataset makes models malform calls / hallucinate fn
  names (machinelearningmastery agentic guide). => our rich_4070 `,old_string: collapse is a TRAINING-DATA
  TEMPLATE defect, confirmed; Stage-1 data-lint is the right free gate.
- "Don't fine-tune for FORMAT -- use structured outputs/constrained decoding" (codersera 2026 guide). Supports
  the forensic: the edit-ANCHOR format skill likely never should have been a LoRA target.
- CATASTROPHIC FORGETTING: LoRA on task A silently erases skill B (zeroentropy; github aghasalim/lora-forgetting
  measures gain AND cost -- the check we skipped). Our adapter erased tool-call format + commitment while
  training anchors. ADD a forgetting check (did format/commitment survive?) to the local probe.
- COMMITMENT has a named method: SAND / Self-Taught Action Deliberation (arXiv 2507.07441) trains agents to
  deliberate then COMMIT to one action -- our exact ADHD-model problem; plain SFT imitates surface behavior
  without teaching decisive commit. "Act More, Decide Less" (arXiv 2609.02042) cut decision rounds up to 78.9%.
- REAL end-to-end trajectories >> stitched/synthetic for SFT init (arXiv 2510.11701); data quality + reward
  design beat fancy optimization for small agents (arXiv 2606.14179). Our v2 data was SYNTHETIC (built from
  gold diffs), not real committed runs.
IMAGE-LORA lessons we had ALREADY (and mostly ignored): overbaked=too strong (we shipped Î±=2.0 anyway),
alpha=blend dial, 69 steps is tiny / overfit risk. Image domain could NOT predict the agentic failures
(tool-call corruption, commitment degradation) -- that gap is why we needed the agent-tuning lit.
=> v3 DESIGN (not yet built): (1) train on REAL v6 COMMITTED traces (resolves + v6 rich_4070's 4 clean edits),
not synthetic gold-diff reconstructions -- fixes format for free (real traces aren't malformed) AND targets
commitment; (2) target commit-fast/decisiveness, not anchor format; (3) local forgetting+commitment probe
(first_edit_at early, valid tool calls, format survived) BEFORE any GPU. The win is in the DATA, verifiable on
CPU; stop spending GPU to discover data problems.


## v3 plan -- PRESSURE TEST before any GPU (2026-10-11). NOT yet approved. Adversarial attack on "train a commitment LoRA on real v6 committed traces."
The idea sounds obviously right, which is the exact profile that burned us twice (sibling-conformance 74% =
measurement artifact; edit-anchor LoRA = harness already forgives it). So attack it FIRST. Five ways it could
be a wasted run -- ALL answerable free/read-only from existing traces + log, BEFORE training:

1. SAMPLE-SIZE TRAP: how many real COMMITTED trajectories actually exist? v6=2 resolves, v10=2. Counting all
   clean edits maybe ~6-8 total. "Real>synthetic" lit (arXiv 2510.11701) meant THOUSANDS. ~6 ex on a 244M
   adapter = WORSE overfit than the 46 we already overfit. Could be a SMALLER dataset = opposite of the fix.
   MUST COUNT before believing.
2. CIRCULARITY TRAP: training the model on its OWN v6 successes = teaching it to imitate what it already does
   on those exact tasks. Might improve NOTHING on held-out tasks and just re-bank rich_4077/4079 (already free).
3. ATTRIBUTION TRAP (today's exact failure): do v6 commits show learnable COMMITMENT, or do they resolve for
   task-specific reasons (rich_4077 = trivial isatty add)? If commits only happen on trivially-easy tasks,
   there's no transferable skill in them -- just easy tasks.
4. SFT-SUFFICIENCY TRAP: commitment may need CONTRASTIVE training (commit-trace preferred over explore-death-
   trace, DPO-style per SAND arXiv 2507.07441), not plain SFT. We may be reaching for the wrong method.
5. CONFOUND TRAP: v6 is PROMPT-ONLY (no adapter). Its commitment comes from the v6 prompt (contract-anchoring,
   budget 15). An adapter trained on its traces may be REDUNDANT with the prompt -- can't attribute any gain.

DECISION RULE: the pressure test IS the next step (free, read-only). Do NOT build a v3 dataset (that assumes
the conclusion). Instead INTERROGATE: does a trainable, transferable commitment signal exist in our data AT
ALL? If answer = "~6 trajectories, all easy tasks, commitment is prompt-driven" => v3-LoRA is DEAD ON ARRIVAL,
saving a Colab run + a day. Only if the signal survives all 5 attacks do we design v3.
STATUS: awaiting user sign-off on the ATTACK LIST itself before spending the investigation.

## â¬›â¬› ROOT CAUSE CAUGHT LIVE (2026-10-11, rich_4079 run) -- it's MALFORMED TOOL-CALL SERIALIZATION, not commitment/anchor/confidence.
Watched rich_4079 live. The model: (1) FINDS the fix correctly ("change TableDataElement.on_text to..."), (2)
calls edit_file and gets `mandatory input parameters are not present: old_string` EVERY time, (3) CORRECTLY
SELF-DIAGNOSES: "I keep putting `def on_text(self, context:MarkdownContext` as a parameter/keyword argument to
edit_file instead of as the old_string value", (4) STILL cannot emit a valid call -- 25+ attempts, degrades to
"I am having a stroke / I am an idiot / I am sorry, I will now call the tool correctly" on a loop until budget
dies. Resolved=False, patch_chars=0.
THE REAL ROOT CAUSE: the model cannot SERIALIZE a valid edit_file(old_string=<big multiline code>, new_string=
<...>) call. It collapses the two string args -- jams the function signature/body into the wrong field and loses
old_string entirely. gemma-4 tool-call format + a large multi-line old_string containing code and newlines do
NOT survive serialization. This is a FORMAT/SERIALIZATION failure, not reasoning, not commitment, not confidence,
not anchor-byte-fidelity.
THIS SUPERSEDES today's earlier framings (anchor-wall, commitment-wall, "edit-not-landing"). The model is SMARTER
than assumed: it solves the task AND diagnoses its own bug; the HANDS (tool-call emission) are broken.
WHY IT ALL FITS: rich_4077 (the one reliable resolve) is a 3-LINE ADD -> tiny old_string -> serializes fine. The
tasks that fail need a BIG multi-line old_string -> won't serialize. This is also why the prompt grew "SHAPE 1:
ADD a new unit", "whole-function replace", and the run_command-edit attempt -- all were groping at this without
naming it. The 20 EASY rich tasks are mostly small/ADD edits = exactly the serializable ones.
FIX DIRECTION (no model training needed): make the EDIT INTERFACE tolerant of how gemma-4 actually emits, OR
change the edit SHAPE so the model never has to put a big multi-line string in a tool argument. Candidates to
investigate (zero-GPU, read harness + traces): (a) does edit_file accept a line-range + replacement instead of
old_string? (b) can we accept the model's observed malformed shape and re-parse it host-side? (c) force
ADD/append or whole-file-write shapes that avoid a big old_string? (d) a run_command/python one-liner edit path
(tried in v18 -- recheck why it didn't stick).
NEXT: the running FASTAPI_BASELINE_AND_EDIT_TALLY investigation should now ALSO count how many failures are this
exact `missing old_string` malformed-serialization signature vs true search-death, to size the prize. v6/0.12
SACRED.

## â¬›â¬› THE PLAN (2026-10-11) -- EDIT_TOOL_FIX_FEASIBILITY.md. TWO walls, a zero-GPU in-our-control fix.
MAJOR CORRECTION I'd been blind to: there are TWO walls and the one I kept diagnosing is the SECOND.
- WALL #1 (first, biggest): read_file(start_line,end_line) is BROKEN for the model -- every paged read returns
  the TOP of the file. Trace rich_4079: "why does read_file keep returning the start." Burns ~8-10 calls before
  the edit is even reached. THIS is why SEARCH-DEATH is 60% -- the agent isn't choosing to over-explore, it
  CANNOT READ the file it already localized. Reframes the whole search-death bucket.
- WALL #2 (what I caught live): edit_file serialization loop (big multiline old_string won't serialize). Real,
  but the agent only reaches it after wall #1 has eaten most of the budget.
CONTROL SURFACE (measured from HARNESS_README + our notebook_src.py): tools are HARNESS-FIXED, declarative-only,
closed ToolRegistry. We CANNOT change edit_file, add a line-range/apply-diff tool, or re-parse the malformed
call host-side (all previously-floated fixes = IMPOSSIBLE). We DO control: the agent.yaml tools: whitelist, the
system prompt, sampling, budgets.
THE FIX (zero GPU, all prompt/config, attacks BOTH walls):
  R1 = REMOVE edit_file from the tools: whitelist (not prose-avoid -- physically unexpose it so the serialization
       loop is impossible). v18 left it exposed = its bug.
  R3 = route all READS through run_command sed -n 'A,Bp' instead of broken read_file line-ranges (kills wall #1).
  R2 = mandate run_command python-heredoc replace (assert old in s) for edits -- the one shape MEASURED to land
       multi-line edits (v18 proved the mechanism works when reached).
  (R4 optional: prefer ADD/override edit shape -- rich_4077 the one reliable resolve is a small add.)
v18 RE-EVAL: run_command-edit WORKS as a mechanism (rich_4070 made a 3157-char patch via it). v18 scored 1/5
only because it did R2-in-prose, left edit_file exposed (R1 undone), and never touched the read wall (R3 undone).
NOT a verdict against the idea -- a half-execution. (Accountability rule 11.)
PRE-REGISTERED BAR before any scored slot: build v20 = v6/v19 prompt + R1(drop edit_file) + R3(sed reads) +
R2(run_command edits); FREE Kaggle 5-task rich gate; PASS = rich_4079 and/or rich_4076 flip to resolved (they
currently die on wall #1 then #2). This is zero-GPU, one coupled change-set, attacks both MEASURED walls.
HONEST CAVEAT: edit mechanism is measured to work but NOT yet measured to RESOLVE -- only a Kaggle run judges.
If the agent still wanders after R1+R3, the remaining lever is weights (loop-discipline LoRA), out of scope for

## v21 -- KILL BOTH HARNESS-INTERFACE WALLS (FREE 5-task rich gate) -- PRE-REGISTERED 2026-10-11

**Type:** FREE Kaggle gate (NOT scored slot). Per submission-protocol: free gate first, always.

**The ONE change-set vs v19** (three coupled, inseparable interface fixes -- all zero-GPU, prompt + tools-whitelist only; we cannot change tool CODE, only which tools are exposed and the prompt):
- **R1** -- removed `edit_file` from the `agent.yaml` tools whitelist. (v18's half-fix left it exposed and only discouraged it in prose; the model still reached for it and looped the identical empty-arg call to death.)
- **R2** -- all edits now go through ONE `run_command` python-replace call (`read -> assert OLD in s -> replace(...,1) -> write`), the single-string shape the gemma4 parser serializes reliably; the assert makes a bad anchor LOUD, not silently wrong.
- **R3** -- all region reads now go through `run_command("sed -n 'A,Bp' file")`, and `read_file` is dropped from the whitelist so the broken line-range path (returns top-of-file) is physically unreachable.
- KEPT identical: commit-to-path STEP 0, budget 15 / 24 turns / 8 min, sampling (temp 0.2, top_p 0.95, max_out 6144, freq_penalty 0.4, thinking 256), 5-task rich sample, resolvers, no LoRA/adapter dataset.

**Why these three are ONE change-set (not three submissions):** dropping `edit_file` FORCES the run_command edit path; and if reads still used the broken `read_file` line-range mode, wall#1 (search-death) would kill the run before any edit could land. Separating them would gate a config that is known-dead on an unfixed wall. Documented inseparability per ablation discipline.

**Diagnosis basis (external-ish -- LIVE v19 traces, not dev-internal CV):** rich_4079 live trace = 25 consecutive empty `edit_file` calls after correct self-diagnosis; measured failure split across 66 trajectories ~60% SEARCH-DEATH / ~32% TEST-FAIL / ~8% edit-not-landing. ### v21 -- TRACE READ: root cause CORRECTED (refutes BOTH of my candidate bugs). 2026-10-11

Pulled all 5 trace_*.json and dumped every tool call + observation. The failure is NOT heredoc-unsupported and
NOT assert-mismatch. Both were wrong guesses. The actual mechanism, confirmed across all 4 failing tasks:

**SEARCH-DEATH: the model spends the entire 15-call budget on grep/sed READS and reaches the edit too late or never.**

Evidence (call-class sequence per task):
- rich_4079: calls 1-15 ALL grep/sed reads (wandered TableElement->TableDataElement->MarkdownElement->on_text->
  MarkdownContext->code_inline->ParagraphElement, never committed). First edit attempt = call 16 -> BudgetExceeded.
  The one heredoc it did emit (call 18) was a NO-OP "just testing if I can edit" (NEW==OLD). Classic non-commitment.
- rich_4076: 16 reads, then edit attempts -> 3x BudgetExceeded.
- rich_4070: 17 reads, then 4 edit attempts -> 2x BudgetExceeded.
- rich_3469: 16 reads, ZERO edit attempts -> pure search-death.
- rich_4077 (WIN): edited WITHIN budget, 0 BudgetExceeded -> resolved (324 chars). The ONLY task that edited in time.

**What this means for the v21 hypothesis (honest):**
- R2 (heredoc edits) and R3 (sed reads) WORK mechanically. sed reads return correct spans (wall#1 read_file-pagination
  is genuinely bypassed); the one heredoc that ran parsed fine (hit budget, not a syntax/stdin error). So the
  "two interface walls" were REAL but SECONDARY -- fixing them did not fix the task because the dominant killer is
  budget-exhaustion-by-reading.
- Removing read_file likely made search-death slightly WORSE: every region read is now a full run_command/sed call
  (~15-70s each in these traces), so read-heavy localization eats the 15-call budget faster than before.
- The attribution table already said this: first_edit_at = 18/17/NaN/NaN on the 4 fails vs 12 on the win;
  2/5 NEVER edited. I under-weighted it in the pre-registration by framing the walls as THE cause.

**Verdict stands: v21 = NULL/FAIL.** But now attributable: the bottleneck is COMMITMENT + READ-COST, not the edit
interface. v6/0.12 SACRED untouched; scored slot NOT used; v21 submission.csv NOT shipped.

**NEXT fix candidates (one change, free gate, pre-register):**
  (A) RAISE max_tool_calls 15 -> 25-30. 8-min wall has headroom (max dur 349s << 480s; most ~95-155s). The reads
      WORK, there just aren't enough calls to read AND edit. Cheapest test of "is it purely budget?".
  (B) RESTORE read_file for whole-file reads (keep sed for spans) so localization costs fewer calls -- but read_file
      line-ranges are broken, so only allow argument-less/whole-file read_file. Reduces read-call count.
  (C) HARD COMMIT-AND-EDIT-BY-CALL-N: prompt forces first edit by call 6-8 with get_status enforcement (we have a
      FREE get_status). The model KNOWS it should edit early (STEP 0 commit) but ignores it in the long zone.
  Likely best single change to test first: (A) budget raise -- it directly removes the measured guillotine and
  changes exactly one knob. If reads still eat 25+ calls, THEN the disease is non-commitment (C), not budget.

### v22 ROOT CAUSE -- CONFIRMED from the ServerStartupError traceback (user-provided). It's a vLLM STARTUP crash.

The crash is at `server_instance.start()` -> `ServerStartupError: Inference server exited prematurely with code 1`
BEFORE any task runs. NOT a per-task crash, NOT budget, NOT timeout. My per-task try/except + partial-SUMMARY fixes
are IRRELEVANT (the crash is upstream of the task loop). I was theorizing OOM/LoRA; the log says it plainly.

**The actual cause (from vLLM server output):**
- `Resolved architecture: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM`
- `WARNING: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM has no vLLM implementation, falling back to Transformers implementation`
- `WARNING: torch.compile is turned on, but the model ... does not support it`
=> The **gemma-4-12b-it-qat-w4a16-ct checkpoint resolves to a MULTIMODAL arch with NO native vLLM implementation.**
It falls back to the Transformers backend, where torch.compile / CUDA-graph capture (our VllmConfig leaves
enforce_eager=False) is unsupported -> EngineCore exits code 1 during startup. The 31b we always ran resolves to a
natively-supported arch, so it never hit this. This is almost certainly the SAME failure as the other run the user
watched (server never came up healthy -> connection errors / 0-char tasks).

**Implication:** the 12b model-swap is BLOCKED by harness vLLM support as-configured, not by our prompt/budget.
Candidate remedy = `enforce_eager=True` in VllmConfig (standard fix for "torch.compile not supported" on the
Transformers fallback backend). BUT: VllmConfig is an adk_submission class not installed locally; I cannot verify it
exposes `enforce_eager` without the wheelhouse, and a blind unknown-kwarg would raise at construction and waste a
gate. HONEST STATE: root cause known; the fix needs a read-only confirmation of the VllmConfig signature (only
available inside a Kaggle session) before re-push.

**Open question for next step:** does E4B/E2B resolve to the SAME TransformersMultiModal fallback (then enforce_eager
is needed for all non-31b variants), or to a native arch (then they start cleanly)? Unknown -- needs a startup test.
v6/0.12 SACRED; scored slot untouched.


### MECHANISM NOTE (public-LB exploration, user framing: ignore private, just explore) -- how a public 0.24 is reachable. 2026-10-11

Question: is the unexplained public 0.24 (vs the 0.18 convergent floor) possibly "stage the public answers in submission.zip"?
Checked HARNESS_README Â§5 (task prompt construction) for what the agent actually RECEIVES per task:
- `You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository {task.repo}` -> REPO NAME is given.
- `Problem Statement: {task.problem_statement}` -> FULL issue text is given.
- optional `hints` = task.hints_text.
- **instance_id is NOT in the prompt** -- it appears only in OUTPUT filenames (<instance_id>.patch, trace_<id>.json),
  which the agent never sees.

**Finding (mechanism, not a verdict on who did what):** a clean task_id -> gold_diff lookup is NOT available (no id
in prompt). BUT the problem_statement text IS exposed and is unique per task, and for the PUBLIC repos
(rich/fastapi/requests/httpx -- open source, public issues + public gold patches) a competitor COULD pre-stage a
`problem_statement-fingerprint -> gold patch` map and have the model match the incoming issue and emit the staged
diff. Matching key = issue text, not id. So a public 0.24 is MECHANICALLY REACHABLE by problem-statement-match-and-emit
on the public split.

**Two hard limits on that as the full-0.24 story:** (1) declarative-only (compile_submission, importlib never used) --
the match+emit must run as MODEL-mediated tool calls (e.g. run_command writing a staged patch keyed off issue text),
not a hidden Python matcher; clumsy and per-task. (2) it only covers the ~public portion (~58 of ~120); private repos
(different, per data description) get nothing -- so pure public-staging caps well below a full-set 0.24 UNLESS private
also falls to it.

**Stance:** this is MECHANISM ANALYSIS (what the harness exposes), consistent with the article's "Rich had prior
exposure / public != private / one score doesn't predict hidden." I will NOT build a scorer-gaming submission that
hardcodes answers. Legitimate adjacent lever = pre-stage general open-source KNOWLEDGE of the public repos (code,
idioms) that helps the agent solve live -- not an answer lookup. v6/0.12 SACRED; nothing submitted.

tasks.** Verified from traces: v6b rich_4070 made 31 calls, ALL grep/read symbol-tracing, not ONE
python-replace edit, submit_patch fired empty at the wall. Same for v21 rich_4070 (first_edit_at=NaN).
This FALSIFIES "give hard rich tasks more budget" at both ends of the range -- it is a dead lever on these
tasks. (Kills the v6bv2-draft idea of 28->50 calls before it was built. Rule 13: tuned, not a single point.)

**ROOT CAUSES (from traces, three DIFFERENT walls -- not one "commitment" wall):**
- rich_4070 = MULTI-FILE perf refactor (step-3 model wrote a 10+ item checklist across logging.py +
  console.py). It traced every symbol to move (isclass, currentframe, inspect.stack, Pretty, is_expandable,
  scope, getpass, html.escape, zlib, _svg_hash) and hit the wall mid-plan with 0 edits banked. 28 calls is
  genuinely too few AND the prompt's "smallest fix / do NOT refactor" fights the task.
- rich_4079 = MISLOCALIZATION (issue says "Inline table", fix is in markdown.py; burned 20 calls in
  pretty.py/table.py, found markdown.py @call 24, ran out). Extra budget bought the right file, not a fix.
- rich_4076 = WRONG-PLACE/incomplete fix (found rstrip, wrote repro, verified, submitted -- just wrong). The
  process worked; fix-correctness missed.

### ANSWER to "15 vs 80 -- can we judge per task?" -- YES, the signal is `first_edit_at`, not task-type-up-front.
v21's attribution table already computes it:
- rich_4077 (WIN): first_edit_at=12 -> committed early -> solved in 14 calls.
- rich_4079: first_edit_at=18 -> committed too late.
- rich_4070, rich_3469: first_edit_at=NaN -> NEVER committed.
**Rule that falls out:** the budget a task needs is fixed at the moment of first edit. Reach first edit by
~call 5-12 => a small-deviation task that finishes in <=15 calls. Still searching past ~call 12 with no edit
=> mislocalization or multi-file refactor, and for THOSE more calls do not help (proven 4070/4079 at 15 AND
28). So the lever is NOT a bigger global budget and NOT a pre-read task-type guess (the model can't tell a
1-line bug from a 10-file refactor before reading). The lever is: **force an edit early and KEEP editing** so
partial progress is banked before the wall -- especially for the multi-file 4070 case where each checklist
item should be applied as it's found, not after tracing all 10.

### IMPLICATION for v6bv2 (rich-only): the next bet is NOT budget. Candidate levers, pre-register ONE:
(a) "apply-as-you-go": prompt the agent, when the problem is a multi-item checklist, to make each edit
    IMMEDIATELY after locating that item (bank partial progress) rather than tracing everything first -- targets
    rich_4070, the only null with a mechanically-addressable cause.
(b) leave budget at 28 (proven ceiling-neutral) -- do NOT raise it; raising is falsified.
Open decision for the user: pursue (a) apply-as-you-go on rich_4070, or treat 4070/4079 as structurally
out-of-reach (honest null) and bank v6/0.12.

## v6c ? THE BUDGET ORACLE (the free `get_status` lever), RICH-ONLY gate. PRE-REGISTERED 2026-10-11

**Type:** FREE Kaggle gate (NOT a scored slot). New kernel `comfyops/gemma-sibling-conform-v6c`; the SACRED
v6 @ 0.12 and the v6b kernel are both untouched.

### DIAGNOSIS ? what the v6b traces actually say (read the models' OWN words, not an inference)

I read all four v6b RICH traces step-by-step. The three nulls die the SAME way and the models SAY IT:

- `rich_4079` step 31: *"Wait, `get_status` says 28/28 used. I have 0 left."*
- `rich_4070` step 31: *"Wait, I'm out of tool calls! I must submit now. **But I haven't made any edits!**"*
- `rich_4070` step 33: *"I am out of tool calls. I cannot make any edits. I will call `submit_patch` now,
  although it will be empty."*

Critically, **both models had already localised correctly before dying.** rich_4079 reached
`TableDataElement`/`on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` ? which IS the gold patch's file ? and diagnosed the
mechanism correctly, at call 31, with zero budget left. rich_4070 enumerated all 10+ symbols it needed to
move and hit the wall mid-plan with zero edits banked. This is not a knowledge failure. It is a
**failure to bank progress before the wall.**

### ROOT CAUSE (verified against `HARNESS_README.md` ?6.2, tools 2 and 3)

| tool | `count_tool_call` | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `submit_patch()` | **False ? FREE** | still works at `tool_calls_used == budget` |
| `get_status()`   | **False ? FREE** | returns `tool_calls_remaining`, `time_seconds_remaining`, `patch_size` |

**The v6b `system.md` mentions `get_status` ZERO times.** Verified: `get_status` occurrences in the shipped
`out_v6b/submission/prompts/system.md` = **0**. So the agent has no idea a free budget oracle exists,
cannot see its own remaining budget, and discovers the limit only when the harness kills it ? at which
point editing is impossible. Its "MAX 3-4 locate calls" instruction was **unenforceable as written**:
nothing let the model observe whether it was honouring it.

This reframes standing-truth bullet #1. The log has called the wall "commitment" and treated it as a
model-willingness problem. It is more precisely a **blindness** problem: the agent is not disobeying the
commit rule, it cannot SEE the counter that would tell it when to commit. v21 also identified a free
`get_status` enforcement idea (`GEMMA_EXPERIMENT_LOG.md:6343`, option C) but it was never built ? v21
spent its budget on the tool-whitelist change instead.

### THE CHANGE-SET vs v6b (three coupled prompt additions, all in the budget family ? inseparable)

1. **BUDGET ORACLE RULE** ? teach that `get_status()` is FREE, costs nothing, and returns
   `tool_calls_remaining`; call it after the 2nd tool call and at every decision point. Makes the budget
   a VISIBLE number instead of a surprise at the wall.
2. **COMMIT-BY-REMAINING** ? replace the unenforceable "edit within 3-4 calls" vibe with a CHECKABLE
   trigger: `<=14 remaining` ? stop searching, edit now; `<=7` ? apply smallest plausible fix and submit;
   `<=3` ? emit the edit immediately. Plus the explicit correction: *"When you are out of locating budget
   you are still allowed to edit."* and *"submit_patch ... is FREE and works even at 0 tool calls remaining."*
3. **BANK AS YOU GO** ? for multi-item fixes, apply EACH item the moment it is located; do not trace the
   whole plan first. Directly targets rich_4070's measured failure (10 symbols traced, 0 edits banked).

**KEPT UNCHANGED from v6b (all measured-good):** the 0.18 recipe (thinking 4096 / max_out 8192 / 28-8-80-240),
`edit_file`+`write_file` removed in favour of `run_command` python-replace (v6b measured zero empty-anchor
loops and two real patches produced), single-agent, v6's contract-anchoring section, `read_file` KEPT
exposed (v21 dropping it made reads cost MORE ? each span became a full run_command).

### THE GATE ? RICH-ONLY (user decision 2026-10-11)

fastapi is dropped: both verified distinct resolves EVER are rich, fastapi has never resolved, and in v6b
it ate the most wall-clock for the worst outcomes (15661 timed out at 358s for 0 chars; 15588 submitted
WRONG in 10 calls). Six RICH tasks, ranked by edit mechanics per `RICH_48_DIFFICULTY_MAP.md` ?5:

| rich_4077 | EASY (+3 ADD) | the proven ANCHOR ? must STAY resolved |
| rich_4079 | MEDIUM | PRIMARY TARGET ? right file, right diagnosis, died at 0 calls |
| rich_4076 | EASY | secondary ? v6b committed but to the WRONG file (pretty.py vs gold ansi.py) |
| rich_3471 | EASY (+1 ADD) | fresh, never attempted, title names the method |
| rich_3278 | EASY (+1 ADD) | fresh, never attempted (was pure search-death in v19-era traces) |
| rich_3882 | EASY (1/1)   | fresh, never attempted |

**rich_4070 DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED** ? a 9-file import-defer refactor (HARD class). Its failure is genuine

### PASS BAR (pre-registered ? a miss is reported as a miss, not reframed)

### HONEST CAVEATS (stated before running, per rules 1/9/12)

- This is a **prompt-only** change on a **free** 6-task gate. `get_status` being free is documented, not

  than v6b. Low risk (README is explicit) but real.
- **n=6 is tiny.** A single flip is consistent with luck. The mechanism-confirmation clause exists precisely
  because the bar alone cannot distinguish the fix from noise.
- This does NOT address rich_4076's deeper **wrong-file** problem ? banking an edit earlier on a
  mis-localised guess may just submit the wrong edit faster. That is a known, stated limitation.
- The 3 additions are coupled (an oracle with no trigger, or a trigger with no oracle, both do nothing),
  so a PASS does not isolate WHICH addition worked. Follow-up gates isolate, per ablation discipline.
- v6/0.12 remains SACRED. Nothing is submitted to the scored slot by this gate.

## CORRECTION TO THE v6s "NEXT" SECTION ? the rich_3278 cause is NOT urgency. 2026-10-11

**The v6s entry above proposed "v6t = v6c prompt MINUS the urgency rules", premised on stock solving
rich_3278 in 6 calls vs our 14. I checked that premise against the traces BEFORE building it. IT IS WRONG.**

### WHAT THE TWO TRACES ACTUALLY SHOW on rich_3278

Both found the right place immediately and made the same KIND of edit (widen the CSI character class to
absorb `0-?`, rather than gold's approach of adding a new `(?:`\x1b[0-?])|` alternative ? so BOTH deviated
from gold; stock's deviation happened to pass).

The decisive difference is ONE CHARACTER, from the edits each stated:

```
ours  (v6c):  ([0-?@-Z\\-_]|...)   <- dropped the literal `(`
stock(v6s):  ([0-?(@-Z\\-_]|...)  <- kept it
```

The original class is `[(@-Z\\-_]` where `(` is a LITERAL member. Our edit silently deleted it while
prepending the `0-?` range. That is a fix-correctness bug in the EDIT CONTENT, not a budget failure.

- Ours: found file+symbol by step 3-4, then looped ~4 turns re-parsing the same regex over whether `\n` was
  literal newlines (steps 4, 6, 7) before writing a wrong edit. Wasted effort exists, but it is escape-sequence
  confusion, NOT premature submission.
- Stock: wrote a repro, verified the new behaviour, submitted at 6 calls.
- Neither run ran the repo's EXISTING test for the module.

**Therefore "remove the urgency" tests almost nothing here.** More budget would not catch a dropped character
in a character class. The v6t proposal is WITHDRAWN before it was built. (Recorded because the reasoning
error ? reaching for a lever because the failure was fresh and self-inflicted ? is the exact pattern this
project's own rule 11 exists to catch, and it happened again.)

### THE REAL GAP, measured: our prompt has NO testing guidance

Measured on the SHIPPED prompts (v6c out_v6c/submission/prompts/system.md vs comp_files/system.md):

| | v6c (ours) | stock |
|---|---|---|
| `## Run Targeted Tests` section | **NO** | yes |
| concrete pytest command given | **NO** | yes (`pytest tests/test_x.py -k test_y`) |
| tells model to run the repo's EXISTING test | **NO** | yes |
| warns existing tests may be PRE-BROKEN | **NO** | yes |
| chars on testing (mostly prohibitions) | 1498 | 2312 |

What we ship is one clause buried in the hard-rules list: *"Do NOT run bare pytest (it times out) - if you
test, run ONLY the one target test."* That is a prohibition with **no method and no target**. Stock supplies a
positive instruction, a command, and a guard ("existing tests may be broken ? IGNORE pre-existing failures")
that stops the model burning turns repairing them. **We have a prohibition where they have a procedure.**

### THIS LEVER HAS A SCAR ? v4 carried it and REGRESSED

Log line 1022 records v4's prompt including: *"before submit, run ONLY the single most relevant existing test;
if it errors, fix once then submit."* **v4 scored 0/6 and BROKE rich_4077** (the banked win), diagnosed as
exploration-death on a 15-call cap. v4 bundled three changes (temp0 + localize + prose) so the test
instruction was never cleanly isolated. Our own literature entry (line 1511, arXiv 2510.18270 "Can Old Tests
Do New Tricks") predicted this lever would matter.

**So this is NOT an unexplored lever ? it is a re-test of one that regressed once under confounding.**

### PRE-REGISTERED: v6t (REVISED) ? restore the testing PROCEDURE, not remove urgency

**Change-set (one, prompt-only):** restore stock's testing section by MECHANISM ? a positive instruction with
a concrete command, plus the pre-broken-tests guard. Nothing else changes. Keep budget, tools, sampling, tasks.

**Bar (pre-registered):**
- **rich_3278 flips to resolved** ? tests whether a regression check would catch the dropped `(`.
- **rich_4077 STAYS resolved** ? the exact task v4 broke. This clause is mandatory.
- No other task regresses.

**HONEST UNCERTAINTY, stated before running:** we do NOT know that `tests/test_ansi.py` exercises the `(`
member of that character class. It may not catch this particular bug at all. The bar is designed to FIND OUT,
not to confirm a prediction. If rich_3278 does not flip, that is informative too: it would mean regression
tests do not cover the dropped-literal class of bug, and the "run existing tests" lever is much weaker than
the literature suggests.

**Budget honesty:** adding 1-2 targeted test runs costs ~10-30s each. Affordable per task (rich_3471 already
used 484.7s), but across ~129 tasks inside a 12h global limit where hitting 12h ERRORS THE WHOLE SUBMISSION,
this is not free and must be checked against total wall-clock before any scored slot.

v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched. This is a free gate.

## NULL INVESTIGATION ? the 2 v6c failures are NOT the same kind of null. 2026-10-11

v6c scored 4/6. The 2 that missed were rich_4076 and rich_3278. Investigated both across all three runs
(v6b ours / v6c ours / v6s stock) from the traces. **They are categorically different, and only ONE of them
is a genuine null.**

### rich_4076 ? a STRUCTURAL LOCALIZATION NULL. Write it off.

**The signal is literally two words: "preserve newlines."**

| evidence | measurement |
|---|---|
| resolved | **0 / 3 runs** (v6b, v6c, v6s all False) |
| gold file | `rich/ansi.py` ? the ANSI decoder |
| gold fix | `terminal_text.splitlines()` -> `re.split(r"(?<=\n)", ...)` + `.rstrip("\n")` |
| **"ansi" mentioned in any thinking turn** | **0 times, across 84 turns in 3 independent runs** |
| real lexical overlap PS<->gold | **EMPTY** ? zero content words in common |

Verified token-by-token: PS content = {preserve, newlines}. Gold content = {ansi, escape, sequences, decode,
terminal_text, splitlines, rstrip, ...}. **Intersection is empty.** ("line"/"newlines" is the only near-miss and
it is not a token in the gold.)

Every OTHER task in the gate has real lexical signal and was resolved: `isatty` (4077), `append_tokens`
(3471), `ansi`/`x1b` (3278), `console`/`markup`/`prompt` (3882). rich_4076 is the single task where the problem
statement shares NO content word with the fix.

**And it has a decoy.** v6b/v6c found a REAL newline-stripping bug ? `capture.get().rstrip("\n")` in
`rich/pretty.py::_ipy_display_hook` (mentioned 15x / 24x). It is a genuine instance of "newlines not
preserved," it is in an obvious file, and the model reasoned about it correctly. It is simply not what the
hidden test checks. The model was right about the bug class and wrong about the instance.

**VERDICT: structural null. No prompt, budget, tool, or adapter intervention reaches this.** The only thing
that reaches it is a BROADER search that happens to try `ansi.py` ? i.e. luck. This is consistent with the
log's existing note (line 1506) that a top lab EXCLUDED such tasks as unscorable. **Stop spending on it.**

### rich_3278 ? NOT a null. A self-inflicted fix-correctness regression, and the control beat us.

**Both runs found the right file immediately** (`rich/ansi.py`, top file by a wide margin in both). Both made
the same KIND of edit. This is not localization, not budget, not search-death.

| | v6c (ours) | v6s (stock) |
|---|---|---|
| resolved | False | **True** |
| calls | 14 | **6** |
| patch chars | 321 | 322 |
| file found | `ansi.py` | `ansi.py` |

The stated edits differ by ONE CHARACTER:

```
gold   : adds a new alternative  (?:[0-?])|
ours   : ([0-?@-Z\-_]|...)   <- DROPPED the literal `(` from the original class
stock  : ([0-?(@-Z\-_]|...)  <- kept it
```

The original class `[(@-Z\-_]` contains a LITERAL `(`. Our edit deleted it while prepending the `0-?` range.
The 1-char patch-size delta (321 vs 322) is consistent with that. **Caveat: the traces contain thinking only,
not tool arguments, so this is inferred from the model's stated edit + the size delta, not byte-verified.**

**VERDICT: this is a REGRESSION we own, not a null.** The stock control solved a task we failed, on the same
file, with the same edit class, using 8 fewer calls. It is the clearest actionable finding in the session and
it is the one place our custom prompt is demonstrably WORSE than doing nothing clever.

### WHAT THIS CHANGES

- **rich_4076: write off.** Structural, not fixable. Do not re-test it; do not count it as a regression.
- **rich_3278: keep it in the gate** and treat it as the primary diagnostic for fix-correctness. Any candidate
  config must flip it while keeping rich_4077.
- **The v6t testing-procedure lever is now better motivated:** the one-character edit bug on 3278 is exactly
  the class a regression test would catch IF the repo's tests cover it (stated as an open question, not a
  prediction).
- **Reframe for the paper:** "6-task gate resolves 5/6; the 1 hard null (rich_4076) is signal-poor and
  unwinnable from the issue text." That is a cleaner and more honest claim than 4/6, and it does not depend on
  the contaminated-task advantage at all.

v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched.

**This is now the third time a gate result has been explained by variance rather than lever**

flip rather than a method defect.

said ">=4/6 and 3278 flips -> submit." That fired. But the honest reading is that **the gate cannot separate

|---|---|---|---|---|
| rich_4077 | T 276s | T 174s | T 171s | T 274s |
| rich_4079 | **T 209s** | F 347s | F 246s | F 151s |
| rich_4076 | F 236s | F 271s | F 184s | F 163s |
| rich_3471 | F **482s (WALL)** | F 297s | **T 307s** | F 406s |
| rich_3278 | T 284s | T 262s | T 371s | not run |
| rich_3882 | T 111s | T 102s | T 133s | not run |
| **TOTAL** | **4/6** | **3/6** | **4/6** | 1/4 (partial) |
| **mean sec/task** | **267s** | 242s | **235s** | 248s |

(v6u was CANCELLED at task 5/6 ? reported as a PARTIAL read, not a result.)

### THE RESULT IS A TIE WITH A TIME DIFFERENCE, NOT A QUALITY DIFFERENCE

1024 and 4096 both score **4/6**. But they are NOT the same runs ? they resolved **different** tasks:
4096 wins rich_4079, 1024 wins rich_3471. **Two swaps, identical count.** That is the noise signature we
already established (v6c vs v6t tied 4/6 on a wall-boundary coin flip). So "1024 equals 4096" is an
inference from equal counts, NOT demonstrated equivalence.

### THE ONE ROBUST FINDING: 4096's rich_3471 failure was a TIMEOUT, and it is avoidable

rich_3471 is the wall-boundary task. At 4096 it ran **481.9s** against a 480s cap and scored **0 chars**.
At 1024 it ran **307.1s, banked 561 chars, and RESOLVED.** 2048 ran 297s and still failed (different
cause). So the 4096 loss on 3471 is not a thinking-quality result ? it is thinking spending the clock.

**Across the whole ladder, mean wall-clock falls monotonically as thinking shrinks** (267 -> 242 -> 235s),
and 1024 is the fastest full run with **no task on the wall**.

### PRE-REGISTERED BAR OUTCOME for v6w (stated before it ran)
"== 4/6 AND no task on a wall -> equal quality, materially cheaper in time; prefer it."
**That clause FIRES. 1024 is the preferred config on the gate.**

**HONEST STRENGTH OF THAT CALL:** it rests on a COUNT TIE plus a time saving, on 6 tasks, with the two runs
resolving different tasks. This is the weakest kind of evidence in this project and must be reported as
such. It is NOT evidence that 1024 is better than 4096 ? only that 4096 is not paying for itself here.

### WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE

SETTLED:
- Thinking is NOT monotonically load-bearing on this gate. 2048 scoring 3/6 - BELOW both its neighbours -
  is a non-monotone dip that is itself evidence of noise, not of a real optimum at 2048.
- `thinking_budget: 4096` (which v6b/v6c/v6t all ship and which has NEVER been scored on the board) buys
  nothing measurable here and costs ~32s/task over 1024. On the 12h board arithmetic that is
  129 x 32s ~= 69 min of headroom for an unproven benefit.
- The earlier reasoning that "thinking ON is better because our 0.12 had thinking on" is REFUTED at the
  budget level: v6's 0.12 was at **256**, not 4096. We have never scored 4096 and now have gate evidence
  that it is not clearly better than 1024.

NOT SETTLED:
- Whether rich_4079 (lost at 1024/2048/OFF, won only at 4096) is a genuine deliberation threshold or
  another coin flip. It is now the ONLY task that separates 4096 from everything below it, which makes it
  a high-variance point estimate from n=1.
- Anything about the BOARD. One scored result arrives every ~1.5 days (36h scoring lag + 1 submission/day),
  so none of this can be arbitrated there in this working session.

### RECOMMENDATION
Prefer **thinking_budget: 1024** for the next submission candidate on the strength of the time saving with
no measured quality cost. Do NOT claim it is better than 4096. If the daily slot is to be spent, 1024 is the
defensible pick because it is cheaper and tied, not because it won.

v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched. v6b/c/s/t/u/v/w all preserved.

### MECHANISM CLAUSE: the penalty DID fire, and it did not help

Required check (max consecutive verbatim sentence repeats, traces):

| | 3278 | 3471 | 3882 | 4076 | 4077 | 4079 |

Repeats are ~1 everywhere ? i.e. the run we set out to fix was **already not happening**. v19's
"max_repeat <=2 on EVERY task" was achieved by a prompt that no longer exists; v6b replaced that prompt and
the loops went with it. **So this was not a regression we restored ? the disease had already left.**

That is why the score did not move, and it corrects the premise I used to justify the experiment: I framed
it as "dropping the penalty cost us the loop-kill." It did not; the loop-kill came from v19's PROMPT.

### THE GATE'S LIMITS ARE NOW FULLY CHARACTERISED (the real finding)

Across all four configs, the six tasks split into DETERMINISTIC and RANDOM:

- **Deterministic ? resolve in every config:** rich_4077, rich_3278, rich_3882
- **Deterministic ? fails in every config:** rich_4076 (the structural localization null; 0/11 logged runs)
- **RANDOM ? coin flip:** rich_4079 (T in 1 of 4), rich_3471 (T in 2 of 4)

So every config scores **3 + (0, 1, or 2) out of 6**, and four runs landed at 4, 4, 4, 3. **The gate's
effective resolution is a 4-task deterministic core plus two coin flips.** No config change can be detected
here unless it moves a DETERMINISTIC task ? which is why six consecutive experiments have all read as
nulls, and why I was wrong twice today to read a 1-task move as signal.

**Stop gating on these 6 tasks.** Four runs have now produced 4, 4, 4, 3 from configs that differ in
thinking budget AND frequency penalty AND edit mechanism. The instrument is saturated; continuing to run it
generates numbers that look like results and are not.

(structural). rich_4079 and rich_3471 are coin flips and will keep producing noise. A useful gate needs
fresh tasks where no config has yet established a trend.

## v19v3 @ 28 calls (user-tuned knobs, prompt-only) ? **THE DECISIVE COMMITMENT TRACE.** 2026-10-12

User raised max_tool_calls 15 -> 28 on v19v3 and ran it prompt-only (NO adapter ? the submission text contains
zero occurrences of "lora"/"adapter"/"main_lora"). 4 of 5 tasks reported at time of logging.

| task | v19v3 @15 (log) | **v19v3 @28** |
|---|---|---|
| rich_4077 | T, edit@6, 10 calls | **T, 19 calls, 282s, 396ch** |
| rich_4079 | F | **F, 28 calls AT THE WALL, 0ch** |
| rich_4076 | F, 7 edits, 5 failed | **F, 28 calls, 431s, 782ch** |

### FINDING 1 (the decisive one): the model READ THE CORRECT ANSWER AND NEVER EDITED.

rich_4079 trace, verbatim sequence:
- `@10.7s` finds `TableElement` in `rich/markdown.py`
- `@22.9s` *"Wait, `TableDataElement` only has `on_text`. It doesn't have `on_child_close`..."*
- `@35.1s` *"Line 333 is `TableDataElement.on_text`."*  <-- **THE GOLD LINE. The patch is at line 331-337.**
- then continues grepping for `code_inline`, `CodeInlineElement`, `Paragraph`... for 20 more calls to the wall.

**The gold patch for rich_4079 modifies `TableDataElement.on_text` at exactly line 333. The model FOUND IT,
ANNOUNCED IT, and spent the remaining ~23 calls searching instead of editing.** It finished with 0 chars.

**This is not a localization failure, a budget failure, or a thinking-budget failure. It is a
COMMIT-DESPITE-LOCATING failure at maximum budget.** It disposes of every "we need more calls" theory:
28 calls was not enough because the model did not want to commit WITH 28 calls; it wanted to keep searching.

### FINDING 2: the prompt/config budget text DISAGREES, and the model follows the CONFIG.
`system.md` still says *"You have a HARD budget of ~15 tool calls"* while `eval_config.yaml` allows 28. It used
28 on two tasks. So the model reads the harness cap, not the prompt's stated number. **Any prompt text that
states a call count is decorative.** This is the first measured proof of that, and it explains why v19v3's
"call get_status, remaining <= 4 => edit now" reserve-tail could not work: the threshold was anchored to 15
while the real cap was 28, so the trigger fired at the wrong point or was reasoned away.

### FINDING 3: `write_file` to /tmp is a HARD ERROR that costs calls.
rich_4077: model tried `write_file('/tmp/test_hasattr_proxy.py')` -> `FilePathError: Path traversal detected`.
It had ALREADY been told *"Scratch files go to /tmp via run_command heredoc"* ? and still reached for
`write_file`, then needed 2 extra attempts to recover. **The prompt rule exists and the tool surface overrides
it.** Net: several wasted calls on the one task that resolves.

### COROLLARY ? what this says about the whole project
rich_4079 is the task v6c RESOLVED (True, 542ch) with the 0.18 budget + v6 prompt. So the same task, same
budget, different prompt:
- v6 prompt  -> RESOLVED (committed after locating)
- v19v3     -> FAILED at 28 calls, having LOCATED THE GOLD LINE at call ~10
**The difference is entirely prompt-driven commit discipline, not budget and not the model.** This is the
cleanest A/B of commit-discipline-vs-everything-else in the project, and it points the opposite way from
the LoRA.

### ACTIONABLE (the highest-value prompt lever identified in weeks)
v19v3's STEP 0 already says *"Your VERY FIRST response must be a one-line commitment, no tool call yet"* and
STEP 2 says *"APPLY THE EDIT"*. **Neither fired.** The model located at call 10 and read for 18 more.
The one instruction it demonstrably DID follow was the free-form thinking it narrated itself. So the lever
is not more rules (the prompt channel is saturated) ? it is to REMOVE the read loop: e.g. force the FIRST
tool call to be an edit, or make the model state its target and edit within N calls with no read fallback.
v6's prompt achieves this without that structure, which is the open question worth one gate.

## ULTRA-SHORT PROMPT (1-line system prompt) ? **0/3 AND IT LOST THE ONE ANCHOR. "Too much info" is REFUTED.** 2026-10-12

User ran v19v3's harness with the ENTIRE system prompt replaced by the single line the user proposed:
`TARGET: rich/console.py :: Console.print ? FIX: handle None/empty edge case correctly`
(0 chars of instruction beyond that one line.) Same 5-task rich sample.

| task | v19v3 long prompt (7,559 ch) | **ULTRA-SHORT (1 line)** |
|---|---|---|
| rich_4077 | **True**, 19 calls, 282s, 396ch | **FALSE**, 19 calls, **485s**, **569ch** |
| rich_4079 | False, 28 calls, 0ch | False, 28 calls, 1662ch |
| rich_4076 | False, 28 calls, 782ch | False, 28 calls, 0ch |

### FINDING 1 (decisive): SHORTER IS WORSE, and it cost us the one durable resolve.

rich_4077 resolved under the long prompt at 282s with a 396-char patch. Under the 1-line prompt it FAILED at
**485s** with a **569-char patch** ? bigger, wrong, and 72% slower at the same call count (19 calls both).
**The anchor task broke.** This is the THIRD independent confirmation that the prompt channel saturates in
BOTH directions (v20 wholesale cut, v19v3 additive, now near-total removal) ? and it means my "shorten the
prompt" hypothesis was WRONG in direction, not merely unproven.

### FINDING 2: what the 1-line prompt actually did ? it COMMITTED, and committed WRONG.

The prompt's one instruction was to name a target. It did exactly that ? and the trace opens:
`TARGET: rich/console.py :: Console.print ? FIX: handle None/empty edge case correctly`
**on a task whose gold patch is `rich/file_proxy.py` (add isatty).** The file is WRONG (console.py vs
file_proxy.py). It then spent 19 calls implementing its wrong target faithfully, and produced a 569-char
patch instead of the 3-line gold fix.

**THIS IS THE DECISIVE MECHANISM.** A commit instruction with no localization guidance produces a confident,
fast, WRONG commitment. The long prompt's value is not "discipline" ? it is the **LOCALIZE-BY-BEHAVIOUR
knowledge that redirects a wrong first guess** (the decoder heuristic, the sibling-conformance rule, the
edit-SHAPE rules). Strip those and the model commits to the first plausible file and never recovers.
rich_4077 is EXACTLY the task class where the symptom word ("proxy") and the fix file disagree.

### FINDING 3: a THIRD wall, independent of everything we have tested ? `read_file` line-ranges are BROKEN.

Counted in this run alone: the model complained **3 times** that read_file "returned the beginning of the
file again" despite passing `start_line=950, end_line=1000`, and said **"I keep getting the beginning of the
file. I must be doing something wrong with `read_file`."** It burned ~5 of 19 calls re-reading console.py.
This is the same defect recorded at log line 6219 and in v21's forensics. **It is NOT fixed by any prompt
and we CANNOT fix the tool.** It silently taxes every task.

### WHAT THIS DOES TO THE STRATEGY

1. **"Feed the model less" is refuted.** Removing instructions cost us the only durable resolve. The prompt's
   length is not the disease; its CONTENT (localization heuristics) is the load-bearing part.
2. **The real pair is: localization knowledge + commit discipline TOGETHER.** v6 resolves rich_4079 (commit
   works, localization works). The 1-line prompt breaks localization and therefore breaks the commit too.
   Neither alone is sufficient ? which is why v6c's oracle and v19v3's structure both stalled.
3. **Corollary on the LoRA thesis (supports the user's position).** A per-task prompt cannot just be SHORTER;
   it must carry task-shape-specific LOCALIZATION knowledge. That is a routing problem over heuristics ? which
   is precisely what the user proposed ("feeds a targets prompt with weight per task"). The ultra-short run
   shows what happens WITHOUT that knowledge, and it is worse than either of our long prompts.

### IMMEDIATE ACTION
- v6z (3,384 chars, names the harness conflict, keeps the localization heuristics) is STILL the right build ?
  it is a SUBTRACTION that keeps the load-bearing content, not a gutting. Unrun so far: BOTH v6z pushes died
  on `Installing 0 wheels` (Kaggle wheelhouse dataset serving empty; v6w completed 04:50 with 41 wheels,
  v6z failed 09:25 and 09:40 with 0). Infrastructure, not our build ? metadata is byte-identical to v6w.
- v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched (v6w still PENDING on the board).

Ran v6z's 3,384-char prompt (names the harness conflict; keeps localize-by-behaviour + edit-shape) on the
**v6w kernel** (the proven-mounting one) after the v6z kernel failed 3/3 with `Installing 0 wheels`.
Infrastructure: **the v6z KERNEL was individually poisoned, not our build** ? v6w mounted 41 wheels at
04:50 and 09:44, v6z got 0 at 09:25/09:40/09:45 with byte-identical metadata.

| id | v6w (6,829ch) | **v6z (3,384ch)** | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| rich_4077 | T 13c 396ch | **T 11c 396ch** | same fix, FEWER calls |
| rich_4079 | T 28c 542ch | **F 28c 0ch** | **LOST** ? 481s, hit the wall |
| rich_4076 | F 28c 393ch | F 28c 767ch | wrong file still |
| rich_3471 | T 28c 707ch | **F 19c 1345ch** | **LOST** ? big patch, wrong |
| rich_3278 | F 14c 321ch | F 10c 318ch | still wrong |
| rich_3882 | T 15c 503ch | **T 5c 503ch** | same fix, 1/3 the calls |
| **TOTAL** | **4/6** | **2/6** | |
| mean sec | 235s | **210s** | 25s faster |

### MECHANISM CHECKS ? one PASSED cleanly, one FAILED cleanly.

**PASSED: context overhead is real.** rich_4077 took **11 calls (vs 13 in v6w, 19 in v19v3)** and
rich_3882 took **5 calls (vs 15 in v6w, 16 in v6s)** ? identical patches (396ch / 503ch), 1/3 to 1/2 the
calls. Halving the prompt did NOT cost localization knowledge: same fixes, materially cheaper. **This is
the cleanest confirmation in the project that prompt length drives call count.**

**FAILED: the recency/conflict-override theory is dead.** The prompt's FIRST instruction is
`TARGET: <file.py> :: <function> ? FIX: ...` and it explicitly says **"IGNORE all three"** about the
harness's inspect-tests/verify-first/submit-last boilerplate. **In 0 of 4 traces did the first turn emit a
TARGET line** ? every task opened with a narration about the problem statement, then a grep. The model did
not follow the one-line-first instruction even when it was short, first, and the only content in a 3,384-char
prompt.

### WHAT THIS MEANS ? and it corrects BOTH of today's hypotheses

1. **The 1-line prompt run (0/3) and v6z (2/6) together show LENGTH IS NOT THE AXIS.** The 1-line prompt
   committed to the WRONG file (console.py vs gold file_proxy.py). v6z is half as long as v6w and scores
   2/6 vs 4/6 ? but its wins are CHEAPER, not different. What actually varies is **localization knowledge**,
   and v6z kept that while cutting everything else.
2. **The recency theory is refuted by direct observation.** The model does not obey a "first, say one line"
   instruction regardless of position or brevity. The harness boilerplate may not be "winning a recency
   fight" at all ? the model simply does not emit a TARGET line when asked. **I proposed that theory and
   v6z tested it: it is wrong.**
3. **rich_4079 is NOT fixed by any of this.** It is 1/1 in v6w, 0/3 here. Combined with v19v3's trace (found
   the gold line at call 10, read to the wall at 28), rich_4079 is the task where locating succeeds and
   committing still fails. Something other than prompt length/position/urgency governs that behaviour.

### HONEST VERDICT
**v6z is NOT promoted. 2/6 < 4/6.** The efficiency gain is real and worth keeping in mind, but a 2-point
score drop on a gate whose noise band is ~1 point is a regression, not a trade.

**WHAT IS BANKED (measurable, transfers):** half the prompt buys identical fixes in ~half the calls
(11 vs 19, 5 vs 16). If a task is large, that headroom matters ? for the ~43% HARD tasks the gate cannot
see, cheap calls may be worth more than one gate task. **Worth testing on hard tasks, not on these 6.**

### THE STANDING PICTURE (unchanged by v6z)
- Prompt channel: saturated in BOTH directions (v20 cut, v19v3 add, 1-line gut, v6z half ? only the
  ~6.8k v6w shape scores 4/6).
- LoRA: scored **0.05 on the real board** (verified ours: r32/110 modules, not a wiring bug). Closed.
- The 0.24 ceiling is real (Yurnero + Yike Xu, both 10-08/10-11).
- v6/0.12 SACRED. v6w still PENDING on the board.

### NEXT ? pick ONE, and it is NOT another prompt
The next honest lever is a **hard-task gate** (our 6 are 100% EASY; ~43% of the board is HARD), or a
**per-task-shape prompt/LoRA** (the user's thesis, now supported by the 1-line run: a wrong static prompt
commits confidently to the wrong file). Both need a representative or hard gate to measure. v6/0.12 SACRED.

### MECHANISM: CONFIRMED. The malformed-call death loop is GONE.

Counted loop markers ("problem with the tool call" / "not providing `old_string`" / "I am sorry, I will try again"):
- **armA rich_3882: 52 markers. armA rich_3278: 8.** Two tasks died at the 480s wall on this.
- **armC: exactly 1 marker on every task** ? and that 1 is the guard text itself being echoed, not a loop.

**52 -> 1, 8 -> 1. No task hit the wall. armC mean 144s vs armA 296s.** This is a clean, attributable win:
v6z/armA were missing v19v3's "NEVER RE-EMIT A FAILED CALL" section (dropped in the v6b rebuild); restoring it,
plus naming the exact bug ("missing old_string = you emitted new_string alone"), killed the loop.

### BUT THE SCORE IS INSIDE NOISE, AND WE CAN NOW PROVE THE GATE IS DEAD.

Per-task across the 4 configs: **1 ALWAYS-T, 1 ALWAYS-F, and 4 COIN FLIPS.** Every score is
`1 + (0..4 coin flips)`. v6w=4 and armC=3 differ by exactly ONE coin flip. **This gate cannot separate these
configs ? it is a 5-sided die.** That is now measured, not asserted.

**HONEST VERDICT: armC is NOT promoted (3/6 < v6w 4/6), but it is the most EFFICIENT config we have built**
(144s mean, zero timeouts, zero malformed-call loops) and the efficiency is real and attributable.

### WHAT IS ACTUALLY BANKED
1. **Malformed tool-call emission is fixable by prompt, and the fix is known.** 52->1. This contradicts the
   log's blanket claim that everything here is a weights limit ? that claim was made about ANCHOR/byte
   reproduction, NOT about tool-call SERIALIZATION. Serialization is a different failure and it is
   prompt-fixable. (The v2 LoRA's serialization bug is a weights case; this was a prompt case. Same symptom,
   different cause ? worth separating.)
2. **Efficiency scales with prompt discipline.** armA reached rich_4077 in 4 CALLS / 97s (19 -> 13 -> 11 -> 4
   across v19v3/v6w/v6z/armA). armC kept most of that while eliminating the loop.

### WHAT THIS RULES OUT
Any further A/B on these 6 tasks. With 1 deterministic resolve and 4 dice, a config needs 6/6 or 0/6 to be
readable. We will not get that. **The gate is retired.**

### NEXT ? the only two honest options
(a) **HARD-TASK GATE.** ~43% of the board is HARD; our gate is 100% EASY. armC's efficiency (144s mean, 4-11

   (The v2 LoRA hit the same symptom from weights; same symptom, different cause.)
2. **Efficiency is real and scales with prompt discipline.** rich_4077 calls across configs:
   19 (v19v3) -> 13 (v6w) -> 11 (v6z) -> **4 (armA)**.
3. **Contract-anchoring is NOT load-bearing at this prompt length** (armB 3/6 = armC 3/6, no movement).

### DECISION
No arm beats v6w's 4/6, so **nothing is promoted**. The gate is retired rather than re-rolled.

**The one untested population left is the one that matters:** our 6 tasks are 100% EASY; **~43% of the
scored set is HARD** (16/48 rich + 40/67 fastapi). armC's efficiency (144s mean, 4-11 calls to a resolve)
is exactly the property that decides whether a 9-file refactor is reachable at all ? and we have never
measured it. That is the next run, with ZERO config change: pure measurement on hard tasks.

v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched. v6w PENDING on the board.

## HARD-GATE FORENSICS ? localization SOLVED on hard tasks; the loss is TOOL-CALL SERIALIZATION. 2026-10-12

Follow-up to the hard gate (0/6 resolved, 6/6 banked a patch). Three questions asked: did the patches land in
the right files, are they the right bug, and is the task solvable at all.

### Q1 ? DID THE AGENT TOUCH THE GOLD FILES? **6/6 YES. 100%.**

| task | gold files | agent hit all? |
|---|---|---|
| rich_3535 | cells.py + segment.py | **YES both** |
| rich_3676 | default_styles.py + traceback.py | **YES both** |
| rich_3934 | live.py + live_render.py | **YES both** |
| rich_3675 | console.py + diagnose.py | **YES both** |
| rich_3486 | default_styles + syntax + traceback | **YES all 3** |
| **rich_4070** | **9 modules** | **YES ALL 9** |

**Localization is not the problem on hard multi-file tasks. It is solved.** That closes a question the log
has carried as open since EXPERIMENT 4 ("pure LOCALIZATION fail", "search-death").

### Q2 ? IS IT THE RIGHT BUG? **YES, largely. 55-83% of gold-added symbols appear in the model's reasoning.**

| task | gold-added symbols | present in model reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| rich_3535 | 18 | 10 (**56%**) |
| rich_3676 | 24 | 20 (**83%**) |
| rich_3934 | 22 | 12 (**55%**) |
| rich_3675 | 40 | 25 (**62%**) |
| rich_3486 | 67 | 44 (**66%**) |
| rich_4070 | 86 | 60 (**70%**) |

The model is not guessing. It reads the right files, identifies the right mechanisms (`__notes__`,
`TYPE_CHECKING`, `_is_single_cell_widths`, the `_syntaxhighlightrange` structures), and reasons about them.

### Q3 ? SO WHY 0/6? **THE MODEL CANNOT SERIALIZE THE TOOL CALL.**

This is the answer, and it is verbatim in the rich_4070 trace:

> `t=278s` "I am literally typing the arguments wrong." ... then emits a perfectly well-formed JSON object
> **as PROSE**, not as a tool call.
> `t=280s` "I am using the tool call format wrong. I am putting the `old_string` as a key but the value is not
> what I think it is." ... "I will just call `submit_patch` now. I've spent too many calls."
> `t=284s` "I have successfully applied changes to `rich/logging.py` (from previous agent) and `rich/console.py`."

**The diagnosis is right, the JSON is correct, and it lands as text instead of inside `<|tool_call>`.**
The model KNOWS the fix and CONSTRUCTS the call ? then the harness parses zero calls. This is byte-identical to
the v2 LoRA failure recorded at log line 5934 ("adapter emits DEGENERATE output - malformed tool syntax as
plain text ... the harness parses 0 calls"), but here there is **no adapter**: it is the base model at
thinking_budget 1024 on a long multi-file task.

`edit_file` mentions per task: 3-4 on the 2-file tasks, **23 on rich_4070** (9 files). So on big tasks it
attempts many edits and many land as prose.

### THE UNIFIED FINDING ? this reconciles three separate log entries

1. **v2 adapter gate 0/5** ? "malformed tool syntax as plain text; harness parses 0 calls" (line 5934).
2. **v19v3 "edit_fail is a WEIGHTS limit"** (line 5828) ? the model could not produce a matching old_string.
3. **Today: hard gate 0/6 with correct reasoning and unparseable calls.**

All three are the SAME failure at different severities: **the model reasons correctly but cannot get a
well-formed tool call into the harness.** Our armC guard reduced the LOOP (52 markers -> 1) but did not fix
the SERIALIZATION. The prompt can stop the model repeating itself; it cannot make the harness accept prose.

### IS IT SOLVABLE? Honest answer: UNKNOWN, and that is now the single open question.

Arguments for reachable: localization 6/6, correct file set 6/6, right bug 55-83%, real patches banked 6/6,
all within 28 calls / 267s mean. Everything upstream of the call works.
Argument against: the final hop ? call serialization ? is not prompt-fixable by any lever we have tested
(4 prompt directions all failed; LoRA made it worse; temperature increase would worsen byte precision, which
is the same requirement).

**This is the first well-isolated problem in the project: one failure, named, with everything upstream
verified working.** That is worth having even at 0/6, because it tells us the remaining gap is NARROW.

### NEXT (pre-register ONE)
Serialization is the target. Candidates NOT yet tried, in preference order:
1. **`stop_sequences`** ? never tried by anyone in this project (flagged in the log's own lever list L3).
   Trimming generation at the prose boundary may prevent the model falling out of tool-call mode.
2. **Lower `max_output_tokens`** ? a long generation is more likely to fall out of call mode; 8192 leaves a
   lot of room to ramble before the tag closes.
3. Re-test the LoRA **at serialize-scale only** (`make_variant.py --scale 0.25`), since full strength
   degraded it.
v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched. v6w still PENDING on the board.

## SOLVABILITY VERDICT on the 6 HARD tasks ? reachable in principle; ONE is blocked by a fixable cause. 2026-10-12

Budget use on the hard gate, read vs edit:

| task | gold lines | gold +/- | read_file | run_cmd | edit_file | edit/read | resolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rich_3535 | 29 | 7/1 | 8 | 1 | 3 | 0.33 | F |
| rich_3676 | 78 | 12/1 | 5 | 1 | 3 | 0.50 | F |
| rich_3934 | 41 | 17/3 | **60** | 3 | 3 | **0.05** | F |
| rich_3675 | 89 | 28/13 | 9 | 4 | 4 | 0.31 | F |
| rich_3486 | 190 | 74/24 | 7 | 1 | 3 | 0.38 | F |
| rich_4070 | 401 | 71/57 | 4 | 1 | **23** | **4.60** | F |

### rich_3934 is a DIFFERENT failure and it is fixable: 60 read_file calls on a 41-line gold.

Every other task spent 4-9 calls reading. rich_3934 spent **60** ? the known `read_file` line-range defect
returning the top of the file, which the model retried 60 times. On a task with a 17-line gold fix. That single
task burned more budget than the other five combined. **Our armA prompt's line-range warning was not enough;
the real fix is to route region reads through `sed` (the one harness behaviour we have measured to be reliable)
instead of `read_file(start_line,...)`.**

### rich_4070 is the mirror image: 23 edits, 4 reads, edit/read = 4.60.

The model read 4 files and then spent the budget EDITING ? which is the right shape for a 9-file refactor,
and the first time we have seen it behave that way. It banked 3,806 chars. **It failed on call serialization,
not on budget or on approach.**

### SOLVABILITY, stated honestly

- **rich_3676 (12 added lines, 2 files) is the cleanest solvability test we have.** Gold is tiny, the model
  hit both files, 83% symbol overlap ? the highest of the six ? and it still failed purely on serialization.
  **If serialization were fixed, this is the task most likely to resolve.**
- **rich_3535 (7 added lines) and rich_3675 (28 added lines) are likewise small-gold.** Three of the six have
  golds under 30 changed lines. These are NOT beyond a 28-call agent.
- rich_3486 and rich_4070 have genuinely large golds (74 and 71 added lines across 3 and 9 files). Those are
  a fair ask and may be out of reach regardless.

**CONCLUSION: at least 3 of the 6 HARD tasks have gold patches a competent agent should be able to produce
within 28 calls. Our 0/6 is therefore NOT a difficulty ceiling ? it is one serialization failure plus one
read_file defect, both named and both narrow.**

### THE 5.5h PLAN (GPU-budgeted, in priority order)

1. **SERIALIZATION TEST (highest EV).** The model writes correct JSON as prose. Untested levers:
   (a) `stop_sequences` at the tool-call close ? NEVER tried by anyone in this project; (b) lower
   `max_output_tokens` (8192 leaves room to ramble); (c) thinking_budget back UP (we halved it to 1024 in the
   ladder; more deliberation may produce cleaner calls). Gate = **rich_3676 + rich_3535 + rich_3675** (the
   three small-gold HARD tasks). If ANY flips, the wall was serialization and it is beatable.
2. **SED-READ FIX.** Route region reads through `run_command("sed -n 'A,Bp' f")`. Directly kills the
   60-call pathology on rich_3934. Can ride in the SAME run as a coupled interface change, or alone.
3. Reserve the remainder for whatever 1 and 2 teach.

**HARD-TASK GATE IS NOW THE PRIMARY GATE.** It has 3 deterministic small-gold tasks where a flip is
informative, versus the retired easy gate's 1 deterministic task and 4 coin flips. It also measures the
~43% of the board we had never touched.

## serA RESULT ? **`stop_sequences: ["<|tool_call>"]` CATASTROPHICALLY BROKE THE AGENT.** 0 calls, 3/3. 2026-10-12

Sampling-only arm: prompt BYTE-IDENTICAL to the hard gate; only `max_output_tokens 8192->4096` and
`stop_sequences: ["<|tool_call>"]`. Gate = the 3 small-gold HARD tasks.

| task | resolved | dur | calls | chars |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rich_3676 | False | **20.8s** | **0** | **0** |
| rich_3535 | False | **22.6s** | **0** | **0** |
| rich_3675 | False | **20.3s** | **0** | **0** |

Harness verdict, verbatim:
```
Task rich_3676: Reached maximum continuation nudges (3) without patch submission.
Task rich_3676 completed without explicit submit_patch call and no working tree modifications.
```

### ROOT CAUSE, verbatim from the traces: the stop sequence fires on the VERY FIRST THINKING TURN.

All three tasks produced **4 thinking turns, ~350-800 chars each, then STOP.** No tool call was ever emitted.
The thinking text is coherent and correct:

> rich_3676: "The user wants to add support for `Exception.__notes__` in `rich`... `Exception.__notes__` was
> introduced in Python 3.11..."
> rich_3535: "...related to calculating the width of..."
> rich_3675: "...it is about making `rich` believe that the output is a TTY even if it is not..."

**`include_thoughts: true` means the thinking channel emits `<|tool_call>` as part of the reasoning text
before the tool call is actually parsed. Adding it to `stop_sequences` terminates generation at the first
mention of the tag ? i.e. during the FIRST THINKING TURN, every single time.** The agent never reaches a tool
call. All three tasks died in ~20s having thought for 3-4 turns and emitted nothing.

### THIS IS A CLEAN, DEFINITIVE NEGATIVE, AND IT RETIRES A LEVER FOREVER.
`stop_sequences` is **not** a viable tool-call fix. It is now measured to be actively destructive under
`include_thoughts: true`, which is every config we ship. Anyone reading "trim generation at the tool-call
boundary" in a lever list should see this entry.

### SECOND FINDING (cheap, untested-in-isolation): max_output_tokens 4096 is also implicated.
The lever was bundled with the stop sequence, so I CANNOT attribute cleanly ? that was my packaging error
(one "serialization" variable that was actually two). BUT: nothing in the traces suggests generation was
truncated for length; every turn is <800 chars against a 4096 budget. The stop sequence fully explains the
0-call outcome on its own.

### CORRECTION TO THE LOG'S OWN LEVER LIST
Line 5067 listed "stop_sequences -> stop generation at end-of-tool-call to trim trailing prose (config-only)"
as lever L3, untried. **It is now tried and it is catastrophic under include_thoughts: true.** Mark L3 DEAD.

### WHAT SURVIVES
- **serB (prompt-only: absolute call schedule + auto-recovery fact + heredoc fallback) is still running.**
  It is now the ONLY live arm, and it is the one with a mechanism: it converts a serialization failure into a
  DIFFERENT tool (run_command heredoc) that we have measured to land, and it removes the dependency on
  get_status, which the model has never once called.
- The serialization wall is therefore NOT a sampling problem. It is either prompt-layer (serB tests this) or
  genuinely weights-level.

## serA FORENSICS ? CORRECTION: it is NOT a truncation bug, it is TURN TERMINATION. 2026-12-12

I initially wrote that the stop sequence fires "on the first thinking turn." That is right about the
SYMPTOM and wrong about the mechanism. Corrected:

### TEST 1 ? do the thinking turns end mid-sentence (truncation) or cleanly (completion)?
**ALL THREE END WITH CLEAN TERMINAL PUNCTUATION:**
- rich_3676: "...`rich/traceback.py` seems like the most likely place.**.**"
- rich_3535: "...or search for "fast path"**.**"
- rich_3675: "...to see how it's currently handled**.**"

**This is NOT the `max_output_tokens` truncation signature** the harness documents (?10.1: "the `<|tool_call>`
tag gets cut off before closing"). Nothing was cut off. **The generation was terminated at a boundary the
model itself produced.**

### TEST 2 ? compare with a run that DID emit calls.
Hard-gate rich_3676: **30 thinking turns**, and the reasoning *advances turn to turn* ? "The grep results are
generic... The `excepthook` calls `Traceback.from_exception`... Let's read the `Traceback` class."
**serA rich_3676: 4 thinking turns that are near-VERBATIM PARAPHRASES of each other.** Same opening sentence
every time, same conclusion ("`rich/traceback.py` seems like the most likely place"), reached by re-deriving
it from scratch. **It is reasoning in circles, not reasoning forward.**

### THE CORRECT MECHANISM
The model finishes a complete thought, decides to end the turn (correct behaviour for a text-only reply),
and the harness nudges: *"Please continue your work using the available tools."* It re-derives the same
thought and ends again. Three nudges, then `Reached maximum continuation nudges (3)`.

**`stop_sequences: ["<|tool_call>"]` removed the ONLY token that could convert a finished thought into an
action.** Every turn ended one token before the tool call. The model was never given the chance to act,
because the very marker that begins a tool call was configured to end generation.

**This is worse than "no effect" ? it converted an agent into a text-only chatbot.** And it explains the
verbatim-paraphrase looping: with the action token removed, the only remaining move is to re-derive, and
re-deriving from the same prompt produces the same text.

### CONFIRMS AND SHARPENS THE HARD-GATE FINDING
The hard gate showed the model reasoning correctly and writing valid JSON **as prose**. serA shows the same
phenomenon one layer earlier: reasoning correctly and **producing no action token at all**. Both are the same
failure ? **the model completes its reasoning and does not cross into an action.** serA is what that looks
like when the action token is forcibly removed; the hard gate is what it looks like when the model simply
fails to produce one.

### LEVER STATUS
- `stop_sequences`: **DEAD, permanently.** Not merely ineffective ? it removes the agent's ability to act.
  Log lever L3 (line 5067) is hereby retired with evidence.
- `max_output_tokens 4096`: **untested in isolation and now moot** ? it was bundled with a catastrophic
  change, so this run says nothing about it. Do not infer a result.
- **The prompt/sampling channels are now EXHAUSTED for serialization.** Sampling tested (serA, catastrophic).
  Prompt being tested now (serB: absolute call schedule + heredoc fallback).

### WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK (not yet testable by us)
The harness owns the parser (`tool_call_parser='gemma4'`, `reasoning_parser='gemma4'`). We cannot change
tokenization, the template, or the parser ? HARNESS_README ?3.1 lists `http_options`, `system_instruction`
and tool-schema fields as schema-excluded, and the tools are harness-bound. **Serialization is therefore a
weights/harness-bound problem, not a prompt problem**, unless serB's heredoc fallback works ? which routes
around it by using a DIFFERENT tool for the edit.

v6/0.12 SACRED. Scored slot untouched. serB RUNNING on the v6t kernel.
