## serB RESULT ? 0/3 but LARGER patches; the call schedule fired and did NOT convert. 2026-10-12

serB = hard-gate prompt + absolute CALL SCHEDULE (edit at call 5, no polling) + the auto-recovery fact
("graded as it is", verbatim from HARNESS_README 8.1) + "pure reading cannot score" + a heredoc fallback
("if edit_file will not serialise, write the edit with run_command"). Sampling IDENTICAL to the hard gate.
Gate = the 3 small-gold HARD tasks. Verified shipped: 6,181 chars, all three additions present.

| task | resolved | dur | calls | chars | hard-gate chars (same task) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rich_3676 | False | 235.6s | 22 | **1187** | 1252 |
| rich_3535 | False | 192.1s | 15 | **465** | 479 |
| rich_3675 | False | 97.0s | 12 | **723** | 810 |
| **TOTAL** | **0/3** | 175s mean | | 3/3 banked | 3/3 banked |

### MECHANISM: the schedule FIRED (edit_file mentions 3->5) and did not convert a single task.

Same 0/3 as the hard gate. Patch sizes are the same order of magnitude. **The added rules produced no
resolution.** Specifically:
- **The absolute call schedule was obeyed in FORM** (the model discusses editing more, edit_file mentions rose
  3 -> 5 on all three tasks) **and that changed nothing.**
- **The heredoc fallback was NOT used** (`pathlib`/`write_text`/`read_text` = 0 occurrences on all three).
  The instruction to fall back was present in the prompt and ignored. Same pattern as `get_status`: a rule
  depending on a tool the model will not reach is inert.
- rich_3675 finished in **97.0s** - the fastest hard-task run in the project - and still failed.

### THE VERDICT ON SERIALIZATION, stated plainly and for the last time in this direction

Three independent attacks, all from inside our control, all now measured:
1. **serA (sampling): stop_sequences on `<|tool_call>`** -> CATASTROPHIC. 0 calls, 3/3. It removes the agent's
   ability to act entirely (see the forensics entry).
2. **serB (prompt): absolute call schedule + auto-recovery + heredoc fallback** -> 0/3, no change. The
   fallback instruction was ignored.
3. **The prompt channel generally**: saturated in BOTH directions, measured 4 ways (v20 cut, v19v3 add,
   1-line gut, v6z halve), and the easy gate is a 5-sided die that cannot rank anything.

**Everything we control has now been tried against this failure.** The model reasons correctly (55-83% gold
symbol overlap), localizes correctly (6/6 correct file sets including all 9 files of rich_4070), and fails at
the final hop: producing a tool call the harness will parse. That hop is owned by
`tool_call_parser='gemma4'` / `reasoning_parser='gemma4'`, which HARNESS_README 3.1 places outside
declarative submissions entirely (no `http_options`, no schema-overridable tool definitions, tools bound by
`SwegemmaContext.create_tools`).

**CONCLUSION: the serialization wall is NOT prompt-addressable and NOT config-addressable.** It is either
weights-level (the W4A16 model cannot reliably emit the gemma4 tool-call format - consistent with the v2
adapter's identical documented failure at log line 5934) or harness-level. Either way it is not ours.

### WHAT IS LEFT, honestly
- The edit-discipline LoRA scored **0.05 on the real board** - the adapter route is closed on external evidence.
- **serve-time scale dial (`make_variant.py --scale 0.25`) has NEVER been run.** That is the one weights lever
  still untried, it needs no retrain, and the log itself names it as the cheapest test of whether
  over-application caused the v2/v19 adapter failures. If W4A16 + a hot LoRA is what breaks serialization,
  a cool adapter is the natural candidate.
- **rich_3676 with 1187 chars banked against a 12-line gold is the clearest single artifact of the session:**
  the mechanism upstream is fine and the last hop is not. That is a weights problem wearing a prompt costume.

## SCOPE CHANGE (2026-10-12, today) ? SMALLER GEMMA 4 VARIANTS ARE NOW LEGAL SUBMISSION MODELS. 2026-10-12

**This arrived TODAY. The log was NOT stale - it was complete as of when it was written.** Recording it so no
future session treats "single base model" as a permanent law.

**The change (Kaggle announcement, ~2 days old; staff replies within 10h):** submissions may now declare any of
- `gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`  (what we have always used)
- `gemma-4-12b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`
- `gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`
- `gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`
One variant per submission; every agent AND subagent must match; different LoRA adapters are allowed per agent.
**Unquantized variants are published too** (staff: "The unquantized variants are on the same page: Gemma 4").

**Ryan Holbrook (staff) confirmed the rest is unchanged:** "Yes, everything is the same." Same 4xL4, same 12h
global limit, same eval_config per-task budgets. So a smaller model is a real trade, not a free win.

### THREE CONSEQUENCES THAT INVALIDATE STANDING ASSUMPTIONS IN THIS LOG

1. **"Single Base Model Per Submission" (?3.1 of HARNESS_README) IS NOW WRONG IN PRACTICE.**
   Every LoRA dead-end recorded here was justified partly by "we must serve the frozen 31b, so we cannot fix
   the weights." That premise is gone. **v6t/v6z/armA/B/C and the whole v19-based prompt line were built under a
   constraint that no longer exists.**

2. **12B IS NOT CLOSED.** Our log says "VERDICT: 12B CLOSED" (v22 v4 entry). That was a wheelhouse-version
   wall (`KeyError: vision_embedder.patch_dense.weight`). **Ryan: "Fixed in the most recent wheelhouse."**
   Our own note said "RETRY TOMORROW: ... the wheelhouse refresh" - that refresh has now landed.
   Also: 12B needs `extra_args=('--hf-overrides', '{"architectures":["Gemma4ForCausalLM"],"model_type":"gemma4"}')`
   and `VllmConfig(extra_args=...)`, which VllmConfig DOES accept (staff-shown).

3. **TRAINING/INFERENCE ITERATION SPEED CHANGES THE SEARCH SPACE.** A competitor reports **12B ~67 tok/s vs
   31B ~35 tok/s on the same 4xL4** - roughly 2x the reasoning per task at the same wall-clock. Staff also
   advertise L4x4 notebooks for adapter training and consumer-hardware LoRA. **LoRA iteration moves from a day
   to minutes**, which is what every dead LoRA in this log actually needed.

### THE HYPOTHESIS THIS OPENS FOR OUR CURRENT WALL
Our serialization failure (model reasons correctly, writes valid JSON, emits as PROSE, harness parses 0 calls)
is a FORMAT-ADHERENCE failure, and adherence is size-sensitive. Two testable consequences:
- **a smaller model may serialize better** (more rigidly bound to its chat template)
- **2x throughput buys recovery attempts** even at identical per-attempt failure rate
NEITHER is established. Both are cheap to test and neither is free.

Our own log records FOUR failed 12B attempts (v22 v1-v4). Staff say it is fixed and one competitor reports it
serving locally at 67 tok/s, but **verify it serves before planning around it** - that is exactly the check we
skipped in v22. Treat the staff fix as a strong prior, not as proof.

- NEXT, gated on lora025: **12B serving test on the 3 small-gold HARD tasks.** If it serves, the whole

The hard gate (all 6 HARD tasks) was **0/6 with 6/6 patches banked**. rich_3676 was one of those, banking
1,252 chars and failing. Here it banks 1,154 chars and **passes**. Same task, same budget, same tool surface;
the difference is that the prompt could SEE the task and branch on it.

### MECHANISM CONFIRMED ? the branch fired, and it changed behaviour measurably.

**1. `git grep` usage, branch vs the static prompt (identical tasks, identical everything else):**

| task | branch | static prompt |

| rich_3535 | 2 | **0** |
| rich_3934 | 1 | **0** |

**Four for four.** The static prompt NEVER ran a `git grep` on these tasks; the branching prompt did, every
time. That is the sibling-search rule taking effect as written - exactly the mechanism we specified.

- rich_3675: 17 -> 14

### WHY THIS IS THE FIRST REAL LEVER IN DAYS
Every previous experiment manipulated the prompt's CONTENT while the prompt stayed IDENTICAL for every task.
This one changes the prompt's BEHAVIOUR per task, using a harness feature documented in HARNESS_README 5.1 and
**never once used by us**. The measured deltas (git-grep 0->4/4, turns -53%, one task flipping to resolved) are
larger than anything in the saturated content levers.

- Underspecification is a real ceiling regardless: Yurnero (#1) reports 12 of 43 failures were "the test wants a

## COMPACTION ARM ? compaction_interval 15 -> 5 (MATCH THE SCORER). **SCORE NULL, MECHANISM INFORMATIVE.** 2026-10-13

**THE MEASUREMENT GAP.** HARNESS_README 7.2 (verified in our copy): swegemma configures
`EventsCompactionConfig(compaction_interval=5, overlap_size=2, token_threshold=14336, event_retention_size=5)`
in `scripts/inference.py`. **OUR KERNELS HAVE USED interval=15 for the entire project.** Every free gate we
have run compacted **3x less often than the scorer does.** All gate results to date were produced under a
different harness than the one that generates our board numbers. This is a validity problem, not a config knob.

Prompt / tools / budget / sampling held BYTE-IDENTICAL to the branch arm. Gate = the same 4 tasks.

| task | iv15 res | iv15 chars | iv5 res | iv5 dur | iv5 calls | iv5 chars |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rich_3675 | F | 829 | F | 230s | 24 | 723 |
| **rich_3676** | **T** | 1154 | **F** | 148s | 11 | 1301 |
| rich_3535 | F | 465 | F | 265s | 22 | 479 |
| rich_3934 | F | 533 | F | 426s | 23 | 727 |
| **TOTAL** | **1/4** | 4/4 banked | **0/4** | | | 4/4 banked |

### SCORE: 1/4 -> 0/4. ONE TASK. THIS IS NOT A RESULT.
rich_3676 is the single task we have ever seen flip on the branch prompt, and our own log (line 5207) records
that **15% of tasks flip between two IDENTICAL passes**. One task moving is inside that band by a wide
margin. **Do not read "compaction 5 broke it."** The only honest statement is: 4/4 still banked a patch at
interval 5, i.e. **the compaction defect did NOT destroy edit generation.**

### MECHANISM: what DID change, and it is the useful part

| | interval 15 | interval 5 |
|---|---|---|
| total `read_file` calls | **26** | **16** |
| total prompt tokens | 637,145 | **856,043** (+34%) |
| total repeat-loop markers | 4 | 4 |

**Fewer reads, MORE tokens, same loops.** Compacting more often means each surviving read stays in context
longer and gets re-sent more times - so context grows *faster* per unit of work (+34% tokens for 38% fewer
reads). **Aggressive compaction is not a context saver here; it is a context tax.**

And critically: **rich_3934's pathology is GONE.** It was the task that burned **60 `read_file` calls** in
the hard gate. Here it used **4**. rich_3675 also dropped 6 -> 4. **More frequent compaction DID reduce
read-amplification.**

### SO THE REAL FINDING IS A TENSION, NOT A VERDICT
- Compacting more often **reduces redundant re-reading** (60 -> 4 on rich_3934) - good
- Compacting more often **inflates per-task context cost** (+34% tokens) - bad
- and it did **not** cause the repeat-loop defect to appear or worsen (4 markers either way)

**Correction to my own framing before the run:** I predicted "more 0-char / repeat-loop outcomes if the defect
is live." **That prediction did not come true** - 4/4 banked patches, loops unchanged. The known
"compaction loses tool results" defect is NOT visibly active at interval 5 in this sample. Either it was
fixed in a later wheelhouse, or it needs longer trajectories than these four tasks to manifest.

### WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE 0.15 GAP
We are 5 points below a 0.20 cluster that predates the small-model unlock. Compaction is **scorer-side and
cannot be changed by a submission** (four YAML files, no compaction field) - same class as
`tool_call_parser='gemma4'`. So this arm is DIAGNOSTIC only. But it does tell us something actionable:
**if the board compacts every 5 events, then our free gate at 15 has been flattering long tasks.** Future
gates should run at 5 to be honest, even though it costs 34% more tokens per task.

### NEXT
1. **STOP using interval=15 on every future gate.** It does not match the scorer. This is a standing
   correction to how we measure, and it may partly explain why gate and board have disagreed all project.
2. Branch submission still PENDING vs 0.15.
3. t4096 (thinking_budget 4096 vs 1024) is built and staged, ready for the next slot.

v6/0.12 SACRED (superseded by v6w @ 0.15 as live-best). Scored slot untouched.

## OFFICIAL HARNESS DOWNLOADED (2026-10-13) ? **SECTION 5.3 EXPLAINS OUR SERIALIZATION WALL.** 2026-10-13

Our `comp_files/HARNESS_README.md` was a **10-day-old copy (49,097 chars)**. The competition file downloaded
today is **55,675 chars** and contains an entire section our copy lacks: **5.3 Multi-Turn Loop, Tool Error
Recovery, Continuation Nudges & Termination.** This is the single most important document read today.

### 5.3 CONFIRMS THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS NOT WHAT WE THOUGHT

The harness detects **THREE distinct termination conditions** and injects a targeted nudge for each:

| detected condition | injected message |
|---|---|
| **Unclosed `<\|tool_call>` tag** in last_assistant_text | "Your previous response reached the token limit **before the tool call finished closing (`<\|tool_call>` was cut off)**. Do NOT repeat your prior reasoning in thought?emit your next tool call immediately, and if calling edit_file or write_file, **split the change into smaller incremental edits.**" |
| `finish_reason` contains MAX_TOKENS or LENGTH | "reached the token limit **while thinking** before a tool call was completed. Do NOT repeat your analysis in thought?keep reasoning under a few sentences..." |
| normal stop without submit_patch | "Please continue your work using the available tools..." |

**THE HARNESS ALREADY KNOWS ABOUT UNCLOSED TOOL CALLS AND NUDGES THE MODEL TO SPLIT EDITS.** Our
"serialization wall" ? valid JSON written as prose, 0 calls parsed ? is a failure mode the harness
EXPLICITLY detects and tries to recover from. What we observed in v6b/v6c/hard-gate traces:
- rich_4070 @26 calls: "I am literally typing the arguments wrong" (x3), then it gave up
- rich_3882 @~24 calls: "I am not providing `old_string` in the tool call" (x3)
- armA rich_3882: 52 identical-retry markers
**That is exactly `consecutive_nudges > 3 -> terminate`.** We were watching a NUDGE EXHAUSTION, not an
unwilling model. We have been trying to fix it with PROMPT text for ~20 versions.

### THE FIX IS MECHANICAL AND WE HAVE ALWAYS KNOWN IT
The nudge the harness itself prescribes is **"split the change into smaller incremental edits."** We only
added that to the prompt in the LAST session (v6t/armC SHAPE-2). The nudge exists regardless of what our
prompt says.

**THE REAL LEVER IS `max_output_tokens`.** An unclosed tool call means generation hit the cap mid-call.
- our `max_output_tokens` = **8192**
- HARNESS_README 5.1 warns prompt+max_output must fit 32,768
- rich_4070 is a 9-file refactor: its edit_file new_string is LARGE, so 8192 is marginal
- **The "serialization" failures we spent 3 days on are plausibly just LONG EDIT CALLS TRUNCATING.**
We measured this correlation early and did not act: log line 5619 says "max_output_tokens 4096->6144 so a
whole-function edit does not truncate the `<|tool_call>` tag (gotcha #1)". We knew. **We went DOWN to 4096
in serA.** That arm's 0-calls was partly my error, not only stop_sequences.

### TWO HARD CORRECTIONS TO TONIGHT'S LOG
1. **compaction_interval is 15, not 5.** The official file says `compaction_interval = 15`,
   `token_threshold = 14,336`. **OUR KERNELS WERE CORRECT ALL ALONG.** The compact5 arm and its whole
   "measurement validity crisis" framing were based on a STALE FORUM QUOTE and are RETRACTED.
2. **Model permissions confirmed**: all four (31b/12b/e4b/e2b) are in `ALLOWED_MODEL_NAMES`. Our old copy
   was stale here too, but the conclusion was right.

### WHAT WE NOW OWN
`harness_src/x/` contains the REAL harness: `adk_submission/{compiler,server,discovery,resolvers,limits,
schema}.py` and `adk_eval_core/`. **Our hand-rolled `local_eval/run_local.py` (now syntax-broken from my
edits) should be DISCARDED in favour of the real one.** We can read exactly how nudges, termination,
patch recovery and tool errors work instead of guessing from traces.

### THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE EXPERIMENT THIS OPENS
**Raise `max_output_tokens` 8192 -> 16384 on the tasks that die with unclosed calls.**
HARNESS_README explicitly warns 16384 "leaves too little room" for a long investigation (honghanh) ? but
the 32,768 ceiling means prompt+output must fit, and our prompts+context are small early in a run. A
middle value (12288) may fit the whole edit_file call where 8192 truncates it.
**This is a ONE-LINE config change targeting a mechanism the harness names explicitly. It has never been tested.**

## LOCAL HARNESS REPAIRED + A REAL HARNESS BUG FOUND IN IT (2026-10-13, evening)

`local_eval/run_local.py` was left with an IndentationError by tonight's edits and is NOT in git, so there was
no rollback. Rewrote `main()` cleanly; syntax valid; CLI works.

### FIX 1 (mine): the branch prompt was NOT being interpolated locally.
The live prompt relies on ADK injecting `{problem_description}` (HARNESS_README 5.1). Locally it was being
passed through **literally**, so a local run would have measured a prompt the board never sees. Now
interpolated per task from `tasks.jsonl`. **Anyone who ran the branch prompt locally before this was
measuring nothing.**

### FIX 2 (the real bug, and it is in MY compaction code, not the model):
First run of the branch prompt locally on rich_3675 and rich_3676 produced **5 calls, 0 chars, both** -
which looked like a model failure. It was not:

```
[compacted 6 msgs -> 0ch summary]
agent: tool_calls=5 ... patch_chars=0
```

**I compacted on EVENT COUNT alone (`events_since_compaction >= 5`), which destroyed the early localization
of a 28-call run after five calls.** The scorer's interval=5 is a BACKSTOP; the threshold (14,336) is what
normally fires. I had implemented interval as the primary trigger.

Two bugs compounded:
1. compaction fired at call 5 on a ~3k-token context;
2. the model-written summary came back **0 chars**, so compaction deleted information outright.

FIXED: compaction now requires **BOTH** the interval to have elapsed **AND** context past the threshold, and
the summary falls back to a deterministic extraction of tool calls + first lines so compaction is never
net-destructive. **Lesson: a harness bug that mimics a model failure is the most expensive kind - it is
indistinguishable from a null until you read the harness log.**

### THE HARNESS NOW RUNS END TO END (rich_4077, 12B, llama-server):
```
[1] search_code('isatty')  [2] read_file(console.py,960)  [3] read_file(console.py,960-980)
[4] search_code('isatty')
[text/length] '...isatty() can raise AttributeError...'
[text/length] ''
[5] edit_file(old_string='        isatty: Optional[Callable[[], bo', ...)
agent: tool_calls=5 patch_chars=698  NOT RESOLVED
```
**It reproduces the Kaggle failure mode LOCALLY**: `finish_reason=length` twice and a visibly truncated
`old_string` ('...Callable[[], bo'). The local path can therefore be used to investigate truncation without
spending a Kaggle slot - which is the entire point of standing this up.

### ALREADY ANSWERED BY IT: max_output_tokens 8192 -> 16384 (Kaggle v12) was a NULL.
Same 4 tasks: **0/4, 4/4 banked, mean 231s vs 224s, and ZERO length-truncation messages in the log.**
So raising the cap did NOT remove the truncation behaviour - the theory that our "serialization wall" is
output-token truncation is **NOT SUPPORTED at 8192**. rich_3676 moved again (T at 8192, F at 16384, F at
compact5) - now flipping across three configs, i.e. **it is a coin flip, not a measurement.**

**1. THERE IS A 0.073 FLOOR THAT NEEDS NO RICH RESOLVES AT ALL.**
v10 converted **ZERO of five** rich tasks and still scored **0.08**. That is the model solving non-rich
tasks (or partial credit on none-of-ours) with the base 31B. **Our gate has been measuring only the
gate-visible slice of the score, and that slice has a small slope: each +1 rich resolve ~ +0.019.**

**2. THE 0.20 CLUSTER IS NOT REACHABLE BY RICH RESOLVES ALONE.**
Extrapolating our own line: 0.20 needs a gate rate of **111%** (6.6/6). Impossible. So **the 0.20+ teams
are converting a different population than we are** - they are doing something on the tasks our rich-only
gate never shows them (fastapi, or the HARD band, or the 106/129 that do not name their gold file).
**Our gate is blind to whatever is driving the top of the board.** That is now quantified, not asserted.

**3. THE LoRA ARM SCORED BELOW THE FLOOR.**
kjhgiughj = **0.05 = -0.023 vs the 0.073 intercept.** It is the only run we have that scored *worse than
doing nothing at all*. Not "a bit worse" - below the model's own baseline with a broken adapter on top.
That retro-justifies closing the edit-discipline LoRA line on external evidence.

### THE HONEST CAVEAT ON THE FIT
**n=4.** R^2 = 0.891 on four points is suggestive, not established, and the residuals are not random
(v15 is +0.016 off). The two runs that break monotonicity are v10 (0/5 -> 0.08) and v15 (1/5 -> 0.08) -
both flat, which is what makes the intercept look big. **Treat the FORM (big floor, small rich slope) as
well-supported and the COEFFICIENTS as provisional.**

### WHAT IT CHANGES ABOUT STRATEGY
- Optimising our rich gate harder has a **~0.019 per resolve** ceiling. Six perfect rich resolves ~ +0.11 from
  a 0.073 floor. That is most of one place, not a path to 0.24.
- **The headroom is OFF-gate.** Whatever the 0.20 cluster does, our gate cannot see it. The next real
  question is not "which prompt scores best on 6 easy rich tasks" - it is **"what population are we not
  measuring?"** Candidate answers, all supported: fastapi (67/129, never resolved by us in 11+ runs), the
  HARD band (~43%), and the 106/129 whose issue text never names the gold file.
- **This retroactively justifies the rich-only gate being retired earlier as the PRIMARY instrument** - and
  explains why six consecutive rich experiments produced a 0.12 -> 0.15 crawl rather than a step.

## Local 12B, raw single turn, no harness: thinking ON gave empty `content` 3/3, thinking OFF gave a diff 3/3. HYPOTHESIS ONLY (n=3, not reproduced on Kaggle). 2026-10-14

[REWORDED the same day. The first version of this entry called this a "root cause" and said it explained
everything we had chased. That was overclaimed, and part of it contradicts evidence already in this log
(see "WHAT CONTRADICTS IT" below). Read this entry as a lead to test, not a finding.]

User's challenge: "use the model WITHOUT the harness and have it solve the problem - maybe it's a harness
problem?" What follows is what that test did and did not show.

### THE EXPERIMENT (raw llama-server, no tools, no agent loop, single turn, repo source in the prompt)

| task | thinking ON | thinking OFF |
|---|---|---|
| rich_3944 | `finish=length` **0 chars** | `finish=stop` **2543 chars** |
| rich_3296 | `finish=length` **0 chars** | `finish=stop` **1065 chars** |
| rich_3518 | `finish=length` **0 chars** | `finish=stop` **3866 chars** |

What was observed: with thinking ON, `content` came back empty and `finish_reason=length` on 3/3 tasks
(max_tokens 3000 on rich_3944, then 8000 on all three). With thinking OFF, 3/3 returned text containing a
diff. The OFF diffs were NOT applied or verified, and their hunk headers were hand-written, so "complete
diff" overstated it: they are plausible-looking text, not tested patches.

### WHAT I DID NOT CHECK
- I never read `reasoning_content`, so I do not know whether the thinking ON runs were a repetition loop or
  just very long. 8000 tokens with no answer says nothing about which.
- Sampling was temperature 0.2 (our harness default). The GGUF's own defaults are temperature 1.0,
  top_k 64, top_p 0.95, min_p 0.05. Low temperature is a known way to get a model stuck repeating itself
  in a thought, so temperature is a confound I did not separate from the thinking flag.
- No thinking budget was set locally. The board runs with one (1024 in v6w), so this is not the same
  condition as the board.
- The model here is the local 11.9B Q4_K_M blob under llama.cpp `--jinja`, not the 31B w4a16 on vLLM with
  `tool_call_parser='gemma4'` / `reasoning_parser='gemma4'`.

### WHAT CONTRADICTS IT (already in this log, I should have checked first)
- THINKING LADDER (log, 2026-10-11, same 6 tasks, one variable): thinking 4096 = 4/6, 2048 = 3/6,
  1024 = 4/6, **thinking OFF (v6u) = 1/4, cancelled at 4 of 6.** On Kaggle, OFF made calls and did NOT beat
  ON. n is tiny and the OFF arm is partial, so this is weak evidence, but it points the other way.
- serA forensics: the Kaggle thinking turns were 350-800 chars and ended on clean punctuation against a 4096
  budget. That is not budget exhaustion. So "every serialization observation is a thinking-budget symptom"
  (my first version of this entry) is not supported for the board runs.
- Line 5063: g4kit measured thinking OFF 9/12 vs ON 7/12 on a different setup. That is a modest effect,
  not 3/3 vs 0/3.
- The first version also said v6u "was probably helped". The ladder does not say that.

### WHAT IS KNOWN
- On this local setup, in a single turn, thinking ON with an 8000-token cap did not finish; thinking OFF did.
- Nothing about the board follows from that. The test that would speak to the board is a Kaggle A/B,
  v6w byte-identical except thinking off, on the hard gate. I have not run it.

## Local 12B vs the real Kaggle harness: parity audit, raw-oracle ceiling, and what the real traces say about nulls. 2026-10-14 (PART 1)

User's question: why do runs end with no patch / never reach edit_file, and is that the model or the harness?
This entry separates what was MEASURED from what is still a lead. Standing caveat on everything LOCAL:
11.9B Q4_K_M under llama.cpp, not the 31B w4a16 on vLLM, and n is small. Part 2 (parity-gate results) is
appended below when the runs finish.

### A. Corrections to my own earlier local work (each one checked against the real traces / README / harness source)
1. The first 0/12 local runs were INVALID: a `return` bug in the loop, and llama-server started without `-c`
   (about 10x slower).
2. Kaggle DOES nudge (HARNESS_README 5.3: max 3 consecutive; texts for unclosed tool_call / length / normal
   stop; the counter resets on a tool-call turn). My earlier "no nudges" assumption was wrong.
3. Local thinking was unlimited; Kaggle enforces thinking_budget. Checked on the real traces: thinking-step
   length is capped at about budget x 3.7 chars (1024: max 3826 chars in v6w, 3883 in v6y; 2048: max 7745 in
   v6v; 4096: max 14.9k in v6b/c/s/t, 17.4k in v6x). Share of thinking steps sitting at the cap: 1.3-1.5%
   (4096), 2.9% (2048), 4.6% (v6w) / 2.6% (v6y) at 1024. The median thinking step is ~220 chars (~60 tokens).
   So the budget is enforced but rarely binding on the 31B, which is consistent with the thinking ladder
   (4/6, 3/6, 4/6) being noise rather than a budget effect (script: atif_budget_hits.py).
4. Local edit_file was exact-match only. The real engine (harness_src/x/adk_eval_core/editing/edit.py,
   apply_replacement) tries exact, flexible, regex, then JSON-unescape. Over all 329 real Kaggle edit_file
   calls: 153 successes = 103 `exact` + 50 `unescaped` (33%), 0 `flexible`, 0 `regex`; errors = 140
   "mandatory input parameters ... old_string" (malformed call), 22 BudgetExceeded, 10 "old_string not found",
   2 "No changes to apply", 2 "occurs 2 times" (script: atif_edit_scan.py).
5. LOCAL TOOL RESULTS WERE CUT AT 3000 CHARS. Real Kaggle read_file results (n=928): median 2527, p95 6524,
   max 25123 chars, and 45.7% are over 3000 (run_command n=1481: median 160, 2.4% over 3000). So about 46% of
   read_file results were truncated mid-JSON in EVERY earlier local loop run, on top of the exact-only edit
   tool. All earlier local loop results (the old 0/12, k_off, k_on1024, rp1 loops) are CONFOUNDED and must not
   be cited for "model vs harness" (script: _probe_reslen.py).
6. Local run_command ran on cmd.exe; Kaggle runs bash (system.md tells the model to use sed -n). Now routed
   through Git bash (not the WSL bash on PATH).
7. The local first user message lacked the tool-call budget, instructions and the Workspace Layout tree. It is
   now reproduced BYTE-IDENTICAL to the real message for all 12 distinct (task, message) pairs that appear in
   the rich ATIF traces (28-call template). Tree rule, validated byte for byte: hidden items excluded;
   conftest.py and pytest.ini added though untracked; assets/imgs/questions/docs/docs_src/tests/examples/
   benchmarks listed but not descended; glibc-like collation (case-insensitive, punctuation ignored);
   BFS-pick <= 200 entries by (depth, key) then re-sort (scripts: _tree_probe.py, _probe_firstmsg_all.py).
8. Malformed calls (missing mandatory parameter) do NOT consume the 28-call budget on Kaggle (armA rich_3882:
   47 tool observations, 43 missing-parameter errors, no BudgetExceeded); get_status and submit_patch are free
   as well. So a malformed-call loop ends on the 8 minute wall or the 80-turn cap, not on the call budget.
   The real ADK error text has no `status` key (script: _probe_missing_budget.py).
9. Parity now lives in local_eval/run_local.py + gate_run.py: `--tools kaggle --kaggle-prompt --prompt-file
   submit_v6w/.../system.md --nudge kaggle --think-budget N`, real edit engine, bash, uncut results (cap 40000),
   80-turn cap, malformed/unknown calls free.
   STILL NOT AT PARITY: llama.cpp vs vLLM tool-call parsers (the 140 real missing-old_string calls and the
   `start_line"` malformed-key wall probably cannot be reproduced locally); 12B vs 31B; graph tools are the
   deliberately crippled ones (exact dotted id only; graph_tools.py says do not "fix"); tool descriptions are
   paraphrased from the README (real docstrings unavailable); sampling defaults (llama-server min_p 0.05,
   vLLM unknown).

### B. Raw single turn, oracle context, thinking OFF (no agent loop; context = gold-hunk regions +-40 lines)
12 rich tasks (rich_3944 3296 3518 3454 3470 2943 3105 3043 3067 3480 3718 3472), verified by applying the
diff and running the task tests (raw_solve.py, repos/rich_v):
- temp 0.2 x1: 5/12 resolved (3518, 3454, 2943, 3067, 3718).
- temp 1.0 / top_k 64 / top_p 0.95 x3: 14/36 resolved, the SAME five tasks (3518, 3454, 2943, 3067 at 3/3;
  3718 at 2/3). The other 7 tasks are 0/3.
- The 22 failures were 14 wrong non-empty edits + 8 no-op/empty diffs, all finish=stop.
=> Raw outcomes are TASK-determined, not sampling noise. Even with the answer location handed to it, the 12B
resolves 5/12 of these. Post-hoc (n=12, hypothesis only): statements under 100 chars (3944, 3470, 3480, 3472)
went 0/4; statements of 450+ chars went 5/7. Possible reading: terse PR-title statements are
under-determined. NOT tested on the other 36 rich tasks.

### C. rich_3944 ("fix fonts" / "Fixes #3943"; gold = rich/cells.py get_character_cell_size `return 0` -> `return 1`)
- With no oracle, thinking OFF and ON-1024 both edit the WRONG file (rich/_export_format.py, apparently
  because of the word "font").
- With the oracle file hint, the loop reached rich/cells.py but hit a finish=length repetition loop; after the
  Kaggle 'length' nudge the next turn edited successfully. (Nudge vs. wiped thoughts not separated: a later
  user message removes earlier reasoning from the rendered template.)
- Replay of the stall state, n=3 per arm, budget 1024, max_tokens 2500: temp 0.2 -> 3/3 looped;
  temp 1.0 / top_k 64 / top_p 0.95 / min_p 0.05 -> 0/3 looped. n=3: a lead, not a finding.
- Log check before claiming novelty: no Kaggle submission has used temp 1.0 or top_k (all temp 0.2); the
  repetition penalty variants (frequency_penalty 0.4, v6x/v6y) were negative.

### D. What the real Kaggle traces say about nulls (31B, 34 runs in the 28-call regime: v6w/x/y/c/t/b;
###    script atif_null_mechanisms.py, atif_seq.py prints one run's call sequence)
- Only 2 of 34 runs made no edit attempt at all: v6t rich_3471 (21 calls of reading, then submit) and v6w
  rich_4079 (budget exhausted while reading: 16 read_file + 11 run_command + 1 neighbors, many re-reads of

  TableDataElement.on_text should be changed but ran out of calls - the gold patch is exactly that method).
- Call index of the first edit attempt: RESOLVED n=20 median 6 (mean 7.2); wrong patch n=8 median 11 (mean
  11.5); all runs median 6.5, p75 16, max 29. (A run_command write counts through a regex heuristic.)
- Runs that reach the edit stage late (call 19-29) often live or die on the 28-call budget: v6w 3471 @19,
  4076 @23; v6x 4079 @21; v6y 4076 @19; v6t 4079 @21; v6b 4070 and 4079 @29.
- Most gate FAILURES on the board runs are WRONG PATCHES, not nulls. The null mechanisms actually visible in
  the traces: (a) the call budget is spent on exploration (v6w 4079); (b) malformed edit_file calls
  (documented at log lines 7718-7814, "marker death loop"; 140 calls, 88 of them in v6z arm runs);

### F. Local rig faults found and fixed (the q_* and p_* arms are invalid; do not cite them)
1. q_* arms (3 in parallel) all failed at the same instant with HTTP 500. Leading hypothesis (NOT isolated):
   llama-server `-c 65536` with the automatic 4 slots shares one unified KV pool that ran out. Relaunched
   with `-np 3 -c 90112` (3 slots x 30208 ctx) and chat_retry now retries 5x with exponential sleep.
2. VERIFICATION BUG: .train_env is Python 3.12 and has no pytest, so verification silently returned
   resolved=False. Gate runs now use pytest_python() (system Python 3.13.14); reverify_gate.py re-verifies
   any tag. Gold-patch validation under 3.13: all 8 gate8 tasks gold=PASS (rich_4077 4079 3944 3518 3454
   2943 3067 3718).
3. Compaction was re-implemented to match ADK exactly (section G) and checked locally: one run reached
   15,655 prompt tokens at turn 15 and continued at about 4,581.

### G. ADK compaction, exact semantics (google-adk 1.34.0 .. 1.39.1 source; harness pins >=1.34.0,<2.0)
- Config (comp_official/HARNESS_README.md 7.2): compaction_interval=15, overlap_size=2,
  token_threshold=14,336, event_retention_size=5. The older comp_files/HARNESS_README.md says interval 5 and
  is STALE.
- The token-threshold path runs before EVERY llm call. Trigger: prompt_token_count of the most recent event
  that carries usage (the PREVIOUS call's prompt, one-step lag) >= 14,336. The sliding-window path
  effectively never fires.
- Events before the split are summarised; the last ~5 events are kept (the split never lands on a function
  response). A rolling summary is seeded as `model: <previous summary>`.
- The summariser input is TEXT PARTS ONLY (user messages, model text, thought parts); tool calls and tool
  results are NOT in it. Parts are joined by a literal backslash-n. It is a separate non-streaming call with
  no tools, no system prompt and no generation config.
- After compaction the model sees: the system prompt (never compacted), a USER-role message
  "For context:\n[model] said: <summary>", then the retained tail. The original task message and old tool
  results survive only as paraphrase. Real post-compaction prompts are about 3.6k-7.6k tokens.
- RETRACTION of "UNIFYING FINDING (2026-10-05)" (~L5175-5187): it used interval=5 (stale README) and said
  compaction drops thoughts and "explains it all". Thought parts are fed to the summariser as text; what is
  lost is raw tool output and exact wording. The "explains it all" framing is not supported by the data below.
- Real traces (v6b..v6y): 74 of 106 runs cross 14,336 prompt tokens. The crude outcome gap (crossed vs not) is
  difficulty confounding: within-task Mantel-Haenszel z = +0.11. Exact-repeat reads rise from 4% of reads
  before compaction to 13% after (the model re-reads what the summary lost) but there is no detectable
  outcome effect.
- So putting {problem_description} into system.md is NOT data-supported as a compaction fix (the branching
  prompt scored 0.12 vs 0.15 for v6w, inside the unquantified noise).

### H. Real 31B traces: behaviour vs outcome (46 rich runs in the 28-call regime; within-task Mantel-Haenszel;
###    scripts atif_behavior_outcomes.py, atif_read_waste.py)
Per-task [resolved, failed]: 3278 [6,1]; 3471 [3,4]; 3882 [7,0]; 4070 [0,1]; 4076 [0,8]; 4077 [7,1]; 4079 [2,6].
Only 2-4 strata are informative, so every line below is a LEAD, not a finding. A model that already knows the
fix may simply edit early and succeed (reverse causality).
- reads before the first edit >= 8: resolved 0.21 vs 0.91 (z = -2.06, 2 informative strata).
- first edit call <= 8: resolved 0.90 vs 0.24 (z = +1.52); <= 12: 0.79 vs 0.17; > 18 or never: 0.18 vs 0.66.
- edit made through run_command (python-replace / sed / heredoc; 38 runs): 0.61 resolved vs 0.25 for the 8
  runs that did not (OR 15.6, z = +1.6). DO NOT remove the run_command python-replace shape from system.md:
  the model follows it and the edit_file-only runs did worse. Any edit_file error: 0.30 vs 0.61.
- execution after the first edit (25 runs): 0.64 vs 0.43 raw, within-task z = -0.20 (no effect). Execution
  BEFORE the first edit: n = 5, too small to say anything about reproduce-first.
- Read waste: 986 counted calls, 284 reads (28.8%), 76 range-less "head" reads of files over 150 lines
  (7.7%), 66 overlapping re-reads (6.7%) => about 14% of calls are avoidable reads. Within-task association
  with outcome ~0 (z +0.27 / 0.00 / -0.13). Real waste, but no detectable outcome lever.

### I. Failure classes on the real 31B (v6b..v6y + v6z_on_v6w arms; script atif_patch_diversity.py)
The task statements are PR titles only ("X\n\nFixes <issue url>"), so the tasks are under-determined; the model
is not failing to follow instructions.
- rich_4079 ("Inline table code"; gold: markdown.py TextElement.on_text -> self.content.append(text,
  context.current_style) when text is a str): right file in 10 of 11 runs (one touched text.py, one made no
  edit). The failures are DIFFERENT wrong edits inside markdown.py (on_text variants, self.content.append(text),
  on_leave, __rich_console__). Resolved 3/11.
- rich_3471 ("Fixed exception in append_tokens"; gold: content = strip_control_codes(content) in
  Text.append_tokens): all 9 runs that edited are in text.py. Passing runs mirror Text.append /
  strip_control_codes. Failing runs include a try/except wrap (v6z base, armB and armC give the identical wrong
  edit; the word "exception" in the title seems to mislead; armA/B/C were prompt variants, NOT same-prompt
  seeds) and 2 runs with no edit.
- rich_4076 ("preserve newlines"; gold: ansi.py AnsiDecoder.decode using re.split(r"(?<=\n)", ...)): ansi.py
  was touched in only 1 of 12 runs; edits scatter over pretty.py, text.py, containers.py, _wrap.py, panel.py,
  rule.py, markdown.py. A LOCALISATION failure from a very vague title. 0/12 resolved.

### J. Calibrated answer to "nulls: is it the model or the harness?"
- Real 31B: 43 of 46 28-call rich runs called submit_patch; only 2 of 34 runs in the section-D subset made no
  edit attempt at all. Failures are mostly WRONG patches, malformed edit_file calls (24 of 159 traces) or
  exploration; nothing in the harness blocks edits.
- No harness, oracle regions, thinking OFF, local 12B: 5 of 12 tasks (same 5 at temp 0.2 and 1.0). On the
  other 7 the model fails with nothing between it and the answer region = capability at 12B.
- "Never reaches edit" is mostly a LOCAL 12B symptom: identical-call loops of 15-25 calls vs a real 31B
  maximum identical-call streak of 2.
- The 12B is a weak stand-in for the 31B. Local arm results are not evidence about the board.

### K. Candidate board levers (NONE validated; each is a bet)
(a) temp 1.0 / top_k 64 (Google's recommended Gemma sampling; every board run so far used temp 0.2). Weak
    mechanism: the 31B at 0.2 shows no loops, and the coin-flip tasks already fail with DIFFERENT wrong edits.
    Risks: more malformed tool calls, longer thinking.
(b) a prompt-only localisation change for vague titles (4076-type). Conflicts with the commit-early design;
    exec-before-edit n = 5 cannot support reproduce-first.
(c) v6w byte-identical replicate to put a first noise estimate on the board (1 degree of freedom only).
Local arms r_off, r_on1024, r_on1024_t1 (gate8, 12B, no wall-clock cap, -np 3 -c 90112) are running.


## PART 3 (2026-10-14, evening): rig fault, tool mix, board candidate staged (NOT submitted)

### L. Rig fault found while the arms ran (llama-server vs vLLM semantics)
- r_off rich_2943 ended chat_error:HTTPError after 13 calls (334 s). llama-server answered HTTP 500 "Failed to
  parse tool call arguments as JSON ... missing closing quote" when generation was cut at max_tokens=8192 inside
  a ~29k-char edit_file/write_file argument. The error is deterministic (6 identical retries). vLLM would return
  the cut text with finish_reason=length and the scorer would send its "unclosed" nudge instead.
- Patch (run_local.py chat_retry): an HTTP 500 whose body contains "Failed to parse" is not retried; a synthetic
  finish_reason=length turn with content "<|tool_call>" is returned, so the loop sends the Kaggle "unclosed"
  nudge. Unit-tested (_t_unclosed.py: parse-failure 500 -> synthetic turn with no retries; other 500s still
  retried 5x). The three arms started before the patch run the OLD code; any task that ends chat_error:* is
  rerun under the patched code as a new tag (never by editing old result files).
- r_off_rr (rich_2943 only, patched code, thinking OFF, temp 0.2): submitted a 1101-char patch after 24 calls and
  76 turns, resolved=False. 51 of the 75 parsed turns were free get_status calls, longest consecutive streak 38.
  The real 31B has a maximum identical-call streak of 2, so this is a 12B symptom; the 80-turn cap is what bounds
  such runs. r_off therefore ends 4/8 (4077, 3518, 3454, 3718); 2943 is False both before and after the fix.

## FORENSIC VERDICT -- rich near-miss, two-pass gemma-audit (REVISE). 2026-10-14

First run of the new `gemma-audit` workflow (KB rebuild -> gemma-auditor audit -> independent refute pass on
a different model family -> mechanical stricter-of-two). Proposal:
`Gemma\kb\proposals\2026-10-11-rich-near-miss-forensic.md`. Reports (every claim cites a file path):
- audit:  `Gemma\kb\audits\2026-10-14-rich-near-miss-forensic.md`
- refute: `Gemma\kb\audits\2026-10-14-rich-near-miss-forensic-refute.md`
- final:  `Gemma\kb\audits\2026-10-14-rich-near-miss-forensic-final.md`

**FINAL VERDICT: REVISE.** Both passes said REVISE. The refute pass UPHELD the big diagnostic corrections and
OVERTURNED several of pass 1's exact numbers. What survives below is only what the refute pass upheld as
MEASURED, plus clearly-labelled INFERRED/UNVERIFIABLE items. This entry is append-only; earlier contradicted
entries are marked CORRECTED in the section after it (anchored by content, since the log is edited in place and
line numbers drift).

### What we were missing (MEASURED, external judge = raw traces + gold-first replay in the KB)
1. **The top-of-file read loop is a malformed-ARGUMENT-KEY bug, NOT broken `read_file` range semantics.** Across
   149 rich traces, 44 of 928 `read_file` calls are malformed (keys like `start_line"`, `end_line"`, `"end_line"`
   -- a quote folded into the key), affecting 19 of 149 rows. All 649 well-formed status-ok ranged reads returned
   the requested `start_line`; every one of the 44 malformed calls returned line 1 / no region. So ranged reads
   work; the model intermittently serializes the argument key wrong and silently gets the file top. (audit+refute
   Â§6; refute A2/A3 UPHELD.)
2. **WRONG-FIX dominates, not "can't land an edit".** Of 149 traced rich rows: WRONG-FIX 56, RESOLVED 45, LOCATE
   29, FOUND-NOT-LANDED 19; 24 rows made no edit attempt; 0 post-submit edits. The headline failure is submitting
   a *wrong* patch, not failing to submit. (refute A9 UPHELD.)
3. **rich_4079 is reachable and is EASY.** It resolves in 6/32 attempts (_v6out, v6c, v6t, v6z-armA, v10, v12_v2);
   gold is `rich/markdown.py::TableDataElement.on_text`. It is NOT structurally out of reach and NOT a
   "mislocalization" task. (refute Â§3, Â§4, A12.)
4. **v6b made real (refused) edit attempts at the call wall.** v6b rich_4079 step 31 and rich_4070 step 32 are
   edit-bearing structured calls the harness rejected with BudgetExceeded, each followed by an empty submit. "Made
   no edit" is false; "made no *successful* edit" is true. (refute A5 UPHELD; "would it have passed" is
   UNVERIFIABLE -- see caveats.)
5. **The 15-vs-28 call budget is not the lever.** rich_4079 resolves at the SAME 0.18 budget under the v6 prompt
   but fails under v19v3 after locating the gold line ~call 10 and searching to the wall. The difference is
   prompt-driven commit discipline, not budget or model. (prior log FINDING + refute prior-art RE-RUN tag.)

### Corrected counts (refute recount from runs.jsonl; these SUPERSEDE pass 1's numbers)
rich_3469 0/18 Â· rich_4070 0/13 Â· rich_4076 0/32 Â· rich_4077 26/32 Â· rich_4079 6/32 Â· rich_3471 3/11.
(Pass 1 had said 0/15, 0/26, 24/32, 6/31, 4/11 -- stale/wrong under the same KB fingerprint.)

### Caveats the audit forces us to carry (do NOT drop these)
- **3 of 4 targeted gold patches are LOCALLY INVALID** (rich_3469, rich_4070, rich_4079 fail gold-first; only
  rich_4076 gold passes = 24 tests). So "would the refused v6b edit have passed?" is **UNVERIFIABLE** by replay,
  not "would not have passed". Pass 1 overstated this as an inference; the honest answer is we cannot replay-decide
  it until the gold harness for those tasks is fixed.
- **"Coin flip" variance is descriptive, not measured** -- there are no same-config replicates (temp 0.2, n=1).
- **The 5,228-char unsubmitted v6 patch is DATA-ABSENT** (no on-disk trace). `_v6out` rich_4070 actually submitted
  a 2,223-char WRONG patch; it did not time out unsubmitted. (refute A6 UPHELD.)
- **Newer submission statuses (ref 57201051, branch 57146757) are UNVERIFIABLE/PENDING** against curated
  submissions; do not promote the log's receipt to an external fact. v6w @ 0.15 (57098497) IS externally confirmed.

### The next rich-only free-gate change -- REVISE (not PROCEED as proposed)
Hypothesis KEPT: a prompt block that makes the model emit a well-formed ranged `read_file` key (targets the
measured malformed-key mechanism; leakcheck CLEAN, no gold/fingerprint). What the audit REQUIRES changed before
it can be a recommendation:
- Use a **protocol 5-task** rich gate, not 6 (standing rule), and a **paired baseline/change** gate: run
  byte-identical v6w FIRST on the five tasks to establish ranged-read opportunities, malformed-key rate, and
  patch-banking baseline; THEN change only the prompt block. Floor-guaranteed (base arm must not regress).
- Condition the mechanism bar on **actual ranged-read opportunities** (a zero-malformed-key bar passes vacuously
  if no ranged read is attempted). Resolution is secondary until the mechanism clears its paired comparison.
- A valid 5-task set drawing from historically-affected rows: rich_4076 (EASY), rich_4079 (EASY), rich_3469
  (EASY), rich_3675 (HARD), rich_3676 (HARD). Baseline arm first (no matching v6w baseline exists across that set).
This change is NOT yet gated and NOT shipped. v6w @ 0.15 remains live-best. One scored slot/day; free gate first.

## LoRA DECISION + RICH SFT DATA BUILD (2026-10-14, user: "no 31B submission until the weekend")

### The 31B LoRA ledger is CLOSED as tried (do not retrain the same thing)
Eight levers measured, all negative: edit-anchor LoRA (q/v r32) made edit_fail WORSE; all-linear incl. MLP
(r32, 410 modules) went 0/5 "OVERBAKED" then 1/5 at alpha 0.5; q/v at serve-scale 0.25 went 0/3 with 2 of 3
banking NOTHING while no-adapter banked 3/3; the serve-time scale dial is exhausted and negative; MLP targets
refuted; quantization-matched training impossible on 31B (w4a16 is serving-only, no grad path); E2B/E4B
adapters produced FEWER patches than their own base; sub-agents refuted twice. Our one LoRA submission scored
0.05, the worst number ever recorded. Re-running any of these is a re-run of a refuted lever.

### But the failure CAUSES are diagnosed and are not "LoRA does not work"
- Capacity mismatch: the v2 adapter pushed 46 examples into 410 target modules at r=32 (934 MB). The 12B
  specialist died of over-strength (r=16/alpha=32 to loss 0.30 on ~32 examples -> greedy decode collapsed
  into a repetition sink, all args -> 1, triggered by per-turn token-cap overflow). Log's own words: an
  ALPHA/SCALE problem first, a DATA problem second.
- Wrong target twice: localization was prompt-solved at v17; edit-anchors are a non-problem (harness
  auto-unescapes \n and the 3-tier matcher forgave the one real anchor miss, 1 of 17 calls, self-corrected).
- Fake trajectories: the prior edit-discipline data was a 3-step cheat (read -> edit -> submit) with the
  target file handed to the model inside the assistant turn. No exploration, no explore->commit transition.
  The adapter trained on it produced search-death on 3 of 5 tasks.

### DATA BUILT THIS SESSION (train/build_rich_sft_data.py, new)
Two outputs, both grounded in real bytes; no tool observation is fabricated.

1. train/data/rich_gold_trajectories.jsonl -- 45 trajectories from 48 rich tasks (638 KB).
   Full 7-section harness user prompt (HARNESS_README 5.2 sections 1-5), then a REAL multi-step trajectory:
   locate (grep) -> read (ranged) -> edit (gold, per hunk) -> submit. Every observation is derived from the
   actual file at base_commit via `git show`. Trained under candidate D's prompt (sha256 de1dbc39103a0970,
   recorded per row so train/ship matching is verifiable). 9 trajectories are multi-file; median 1 edit,
   max 12. Drops: rich_4070 (33 hunks) and rich_3061 (13 hunks) as too_many_hunks; rich_3930 as
   post_image_mismatch (its gold deletes an entire 454-line file, an edge case the verifier refuses).
   INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: re-parsed all 257 tool calls and all 122 edit_file calls out of the emitted file
   with a separate parser, re-applied every old_string to the real repo bytes, and confirmed each result
   equals the gold post-image. 0 failures. Role alternation also checked. 0 failures.

2. train/data/wrongfix_contrastive_rich.jsonl -- 56 records, one per measured WRONG-FIX rich row
   (kb/runs.jsonl failure_class=WRONG-FIX), 11 distinct tasks (358 KB). Pairs the patch the model ACTUALLY
   submitted (reconstructed from its edit_file calls in the trace) with the verified gold edit, and
   classifies the defect, because the WRONG-FIX label alone conflates two different problems:
     wrong_content = 34   (well-formed edits on a file gold also edits; content differs) <- the real target
     serialization  = 10  (edit_file args malformed: old_string missing or collapsed into a JSON key)
     no_edit       = 6
     wrong_place   = 6    (edits only files gold never touches)
   Observed corruption shapes, verbatim from traces: old_string content becoming a JSON KEY
   (keys=['filepath','new_string','elif node_type == "softbreak"']); a key ending in `",old_string`;
   whole reasoning monologues bleeding into the args and ending in `<channel|><|tool_call>call`; and
   `start_line` appearing in edit_file args.

### BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN THE BUILDER (would have silently corrupted the dataset)
parse_hunks did not flush the pending hunk when a new `--- a/` file header started, so the LAST hunk of
file N was attributed to file N+1. Yield went 29 -> 45 trajectories after the fix, and the contrastive
defect classification shifted (wrong_content 29->34, wrong_place 11->6) because the gold file sets had been
wrong too. Any dataset built before this fix is untrustworthy.

### MEASURED: serialization is NOT a LoRA target under the shipped prompt
Malformed edit_file calls, cut by the prompt actually shipped (prompt_sha256 from kb/runs.jsonl):
- candidate D (today's L4x4 gate, 6 tasks): 0 of 8 edit calls malformed (0%).
- v6w (live-best): 2 of 15 (13%); 5 of 7 v6w rows had zero malformed calls.
- v19-family prompts: v19v3 8/14 (57%); the v2-adapter-gate prompt 31/39 (79%).
- Adapter runs specifically: v2_gate_s05c 13/16 (81%), v2_gate_out 10/12 (83%), lora025 6/6 (100%).
CONCLUSION: the serialization catastrophe belongs to the v19 prompt family and to the adapters themselves,
not to the shipped prompt lineage. A LoRA trained to fix serialization would train against a distribution we
do not ship. Drop serialization as a target; keep WRONG-FIX (wrong_content, 34/56) as the target.

### TRAINER CONSTRAINT DISCOVERED (would have silently reproduced a fixed bug)
train_lora.py defaults to --maxlen 768. All 45 new trajectories exceed it (median ~3600 tokens, max ~6300;
assistant-turn content median ~1527 chars, max ~10886). Training at the default truncates every trajectory
and cuts off the edit_file content, which is exactly the failure encode_example's docstring says was already
fixed once ("loss collapsed to ~0 and the model learned nothing"). Any run of this data MUST pass --maxlen
>= 8192.

### RECOMMENDED RECIPE IF WE TRAIN (pre-registered, not yet run)
- Target: WRONG-FIX / wrong_content on rich (34 verified contrastive pairs + 45 gold trajectories).
- Base: 31B. A 12B-trained adapter CANNOT serve on the scored 31B (dim mismatch, architecturally
  incompatible), and 12B serving measured 0/4 vs 31B 1/4 at 38% slower per task. 31B QLoRA trains free on
  Kaggle 4xL4 (96 GB, 30 GPU-hrs/week), so the rig is not the blocker.
- Shape: q/v only, r=8-16, alpha/r <= 1, 1 epoch, capacity matched to ~45-100 examples (NOT 410 modules),
  early-stop on a behavioral metric rather than loss.
- Gate: paired baseline/change on the 6 rich tasks we have ever resolved (rich_3278, 3471, 3676, 3882, 4077,
  4079 -- floor-guaranteed, base resolves them so any adapter that drops them is caught immediately) plus the
  3 hard ones (4076, 4079, 3469). Bar: resolve >= base on both sets with zero argument-collapse, and the
  malformed-key rate opportunity-conditioned per read_file call (not a vacuous absolute zero).
- Falsifier: if a correctly-shaped, correctly-targeted 31B adapter still degrades patch generation, the LoRA
  path is dead and we stop spending on it.
- Data ceiling, stated honestly: 45 gold trajectories + 34 contrastive pairs across 11 distinct tasks is a
  memorization risk, not a generalization guarantee. Only 6 distinct rich tasks have ever been resolved.

## ZERO-TOOL REVIEWER HYPOTHESIS -- TESTED OFFLINE AND KILLED (2026-10-15)

Question: of the 34 measured WRONG-FIX / wrong_content cases, how many carry a divergence signal that a
fresh-context, TOOL-LESS reviewer could use? Such a reviewer sees only the problem statement and the model's
submitted diff. It never sees gold, never runs tests, never opens the repo. Script:
train/test_reviewer_catchability.py. Output: train/data/reviewer_catchability.json. Cost: ~2 minutes, no GPU.

### RESULT: 1 of 34 (3%). 33 of 34 (97%) have NO usable signal.
The model's diffs name the symbols the issue names, in the files gold also edits, and are still wrong. That is
precisely the error class that requires EXECUTING THE TESTS to detect, which a tool-less reviewer cannot do.
Addressable share of the total measured failure mass: 1 of 149 traced rich rows (~0.7%). The hypothesis is dead;
do not spend GPU on it.

### METHODOLOGY WARNING -- this test gave three different answers, and two were wrong
Worth recording because a confident wrong number here would have burned a gate:
1. First version reported 34/34 = 100% "catchable". VACUOUS: two of the three signals ("covers <50% of gold's
   changed lines", "edited the same file as gold") are TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION for a WRONG-FIX label -- we selected
   for patches that differ from gold. They restate the label and measure nothing.
2. Second version reported 13/34 = 38% using "identifier the issue asks about, gold changes, model's diff omits".
   FALSE POSITIVES: it counted PROSE words. Spot-checking rich_3535 exposed it -- the issue says "Regex error ...
   single-width characters", and the model's diff edits the exact regex line gold changes (it wrote
   `\u0020-\u007e` where gold has `\u0020-\u006f`, a one-character error in a Unicode range). S1 fired only
   because a code diff naturally lacks the issue's prose vocabulary. Any code diff would "fail" that test.
3. Third version restricted S1 to CODE SYMBOLS (dotted / snake_case / CamelCase / ALL_CAPS): 1/34 = 3%.
   The single survivor is rich_4070 at size_ratio 0.18 (a tiny diff missing ConsoleOptions, JustifyMethod,
   RenderResult, RichHandler). S1 restricted to material-size diffs (size_ratio >= 0.5) is 0/34.
   The control (model also misses issue-named symbols gold did NOT change) is 1/1 = 100% but n=1, so it is
   UNINFORMATIVE and must not be read as evidence either way.

### CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SUB-AGENT QUESTION
The zero-tool reviewer was proposed as the one sub-agent shape that could not drain the shared tool-call budget
(tools: [] + include_contents: none + hard per-agent max_output_tokens). That design reasoning still holds and
is untested, but its target is now measured at ~3% of the class it was meant to serve. Combined with sub-agents
already refuted twice (dmitrii sweep; our v8 regression) on the shared-budget-pool and never-compact-overflow
failure modes, the sub-agent direction should be treated as closed for this competition unless a new measured
failure class appears that a second context could address.

### WHAT THE NEGATIVE ACTUALLY TEACHES (the durable finding)
WRONG-FIX is not "the model forgot to address something the issue asked for" -- it addresses the ask and gets
the CONTENT wrong (rich_3535: right line, wrong character in a regex range; rich_4079: diffs up to 5.5x gold's
size that still fail). This sharpens the LoRA target: the 45 gold trajectories we built teach the correct
content for the exact symbols involved, which is a better-aimed target than "fix wrong fixes" in general.

## LOCAL-SCORER FIX FOUND — hard-rich golds fail on pygments drift, not the tasks. 2026-10-15

Read-only investigation (bundled investigate recipe). Report: `Gemma\kb\audits\2026-10-15-hard-rich-gold-local-failure.md`.

**All three hard-rich gold-first FAILURES are OUR harness, cheaply fixable, scorer intact (MEASURED by
re-running the real kblib.replay engine):** the engine runs every task's tests in ONE shared `.venv`
(`sys.executable`) with NO per-task dependency install. rich's tests hard-code exact ANSI/pygments byte
output, so a pygments newer than the version each task's own `poetry.lock` pins fails unrelated tests (and
for rich_4079 the TARGET test) even though the gold code is correct. Each gold passes clean (exit 0, 0
fail/err, required_pass, harness_like) when pygments matches that task's lock pin: rich_3469 -> 2.17.2,
rich_4070/4079 -> 2.19.2. No single global pygments satisfies all three.

**FIX (does NOT weaken the scorer):** per-task dependency pinning — install the task's locked pygments +
markdown-it-py into the checkout env before running its tests (standard SWE-bench per-instance-env practice).
Same FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS required-node set, same JUnit validation, same zero-failure bar.

**IMPLICATION:** earlier offline reads of "the agent couldn't land rich_4079/4070" were partly measured
against a scorer that would have failed the GOLD patch too (the Biohub broken-gauge lesson). The trace-based
commitment finding stands (it did not use the local scorer), but a per-task-pinned local eval is a
PREREQUISITE for trusting the decode sweep / LoRA / router offline. This is the single highest-leverage fix
left. Recorded as curated claim J-local-gold-pygments-drift.

User ran a ~2-min offline test over the 34 measured wrong_content rich cases (a tool-less fresh-context
reviewer trying to flag a wrong patch WITHOUT executing tests).

**RESULT: 1/34 (3%) catchable; ~0.7% of the 149 traced rich rows. Reviewer/critic lever is DEAD — do not
spend GPU on it.** 33/34 edit the symbols the issue names, in the files gold edits, and are still wrong; only
test EXECUTION detects that, which a tool-less reviewer cannot do.

**Method caution (a confident wrong number would have burned a gate):** the naive version gave 100%/38%/3%.
- 100% was VACUOUS: "covers <50% of gold's lines" and "edited the same file as gold" are TRUE BY
  CONSTRUCTION of a WRONG-FIX label (we selected for diffs that differ from gold) -> they restate the label.
- 38% was FALSE POSITIVES from counting PROSE words a code diff naturally lacks. rich_3535 edits the EXACT

  fired on prose-vocab absence.

  concluding — the untuned number was 30x too high.)

**Durable finding (sharpens the LoRA target, NOT the reviewer):** WRONG-FIX is a FIX-CORRECTNESS failure, not
an ask-comprehension or localization failure. The model reaches gold's file+symbol and writes the wrong
CONTENT. rich_4079 produced diffs up to 5.5x gold's size and still failed, so size/effort is not the lack. The
offline/LoRA target is CORRECT EDIT CONTENT on this code; commitment gets you TO an edit, content-correctness
decides whether it passes. Both are only measurable with the per-task-pinned local scorer (the 2026-10-15
pygments-drift fix). Recorded as curated claims J-reviewer-critic-dead, J-wrongfix-is-content-not-ask.

## TASK-ROUTER LoRA SPEC (2026-10-15) -- user direction, captured

User: *"the leader is going to have trained a model that can evaluate each task, decide the best path for
each task, then uses the ML engine to guide every tool call."* Spec: kb/proposals/2026-10-15-task-router-lora-spec.md

### WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT TARGET (the connection earlier sessions missed)
The declarative submission surface CANNOT express per-task routing, so the weights are the only legal
channel for a per-task controller:
- HARNESS_README L154: ``tools`` and ``system_instruction`` inside ``generate_content_config`` are excluded
  by schema design and raise a validation error if set. An agent cannot rewrite its own tool surface.
- HARNESS_README L98: ``eval_config.yaml`` budgets are ONE global block for the whole submission -- not
  per-task, not per-agent, not runtime-editable.
- Sub-agents refuted twice (dmitrii sweep; our v8 regression) on shared-budget-pool + never-compact overflow.
=> YAML can express a STATIC branch (what the 0.12 branching submission did via {problem_description}
templating) but never a LEARNED one.

### MEASURED EVIDENCE POINTING HERE
- 12B oracle test: outcomes are TASK-determined, not sampling-determined (same five tasks resolved at temp
  0.2 and at temp 1.0/top_k 64; 5/12 vs 14/36). The task picks the outcome; the policy executes.
- rich_3944 edited the WRONG FILE because the issue contained the word "font" -- a routing failure.
- WRONG-FIX 34/56: well-formed edits on the right file with wrong content = what a badly-chosen path produces.
- Static branching prompt scored 0.12 (within noise of 0.15). Same hypothesis, crude execution.

### WHY THIS SURVIVES THE DATA CEILING THAT KILLED THE COMMITMENT LoRA
Routing is a far lower-entropy target than fix synthesis: ~5-10 distinct paths vs 129 distinct fixes. A
router trained on 129 examples can plausibly generalize; a fix-memorizer cannot (it learns 129 answers).

### THE MECHANISM FOR "GUIDE EVERY TOOL CALL" EXISTS
The v2 adapter (410 modules, all 60 layers) changed tool-call behavior catastrophically (81-100% malformed
edit_file calls on adapter runs). So a LoRA reaches into the tool-call policy. Open question: can it be
trained to GUIDE rather than CORRUPT -- a data-shape problem, already diagnosed.

### THE FOUR STEPS
1. Path labels + headroom (NO GPU). Derive ground-truth paths from gold for all 129 public tasks
   (target_files, target_symbol, n_edits, n_files, test_nodes via swegemma's own
   _extract_test_functions_from_patch rule, target_named_in_issue, symptom_class). THEN the free falsifier:
   classify each of the 149 traced rich failures as path_wrong / path_right_content_wrong /
   never_committed / unreachable. PRE-REGISTERED BAR: if path_right_content_wrong dominates, the router is
   aiming at the wrong class and we stop before spending GPU.
2. Router training set + train (GPU, small). (issue -> path) trajectories, chat-templated, loss masked to
   assistant turns, system = shipped D prompt (sha256 de1dbc39103a0970). r=8-16, alpha/r <= 1, 1 epoch,
   capacity matched to ~129 examples (NOT 410 modules), behavioral early-stop never loss, --maxlen >= 8192.
   By-task holdout.
3. Router validation (GPU, light). Path-match on holdout; must beat the trivial baselines (most-common-path,
   always-single-file-target-named); zero serialization regression.
4. Integration gate (GPU, full). Router + agent on the FAITHFUL scorer (swegemma 0.2.11 + SubprocessManager,
   semantics now known exactly), LARGE task set, paired baseline/change, floor-guaranteed on the 6 rich tasks
   we have ever resolved. Falsifier: if a correctly-shaped router still degrades patch generation, stop.

### NOT IN SCOPE
No autonomous self-tuning loop -- arms are run and scored, a human decides what changes. The
one-change-per-test discipline is what caught the inverted-alpha error, the circular catchability signals,
and the 3/4-vs-2/4 miscount this session; a loop that tunes itself would have shipped all three.
No scored submission until a gate beats baseline on the faithful scorer. v6w @ 0.15 live-best, never
overwritten without a verified beat.

## SCORER SEMANTICS -- NOW KNOWN EXACTLY (2026-10-15). swegemma-0.2.11 obtained and read.

Downloaded swegemma-0.2.11-py3-none-any.whl (117 KB, pure Python) from the wheelhouse dataset
metric/gemma-4-developer-agent-wheelhouse and extracted to harness_src/x/swegemma (40 files). We now hold
all three components: adk_eval_core, adk_submission, swegemma.

resolved = True requires ALL of:
1. test_patch non-empty (else "Missing test specification ... secret hydration failed or unavailable")
2. pytest exit_code == 0
3. JUnit XML present and parseable
4. total_tests > 0 and passed_tests > 0
5. total_failures == 0 AND total_errors == 0   <-- WHOLE-FILE ZERO-FAILURE BAR
6. every required node passed, where required = FAIL_TO_PASS + PASS_TO_PASS, or if those are empty, the
   ``def test_*`` functions ADDED by test_patch (_extract_test_functions_from_patch: added-defs first,
   then hunk-header and context fallbacks)
7. stdout free of "0 passed" / "no tests ran" / "collected 0 items"

### CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ENTRY OF MINE
I previously flagged our replay engine's whole-file zero-failure fallback as a "pre-existing scorer-parity
gap". THAT WAS WRONG. verification.py L297-301 applies exactly that bar, and applies it BEFORE the node
check. Our local scorer was faithful on the dominant criterion all along. The node-derivation rule also
matches ours. Both gaps I worried about are closed by reading the source.

### THIS EXPLAINS THE PYGMENTS FAILURES MECHANICALLY
An unrelated test failing in the same file -> total_failures > 0 -> resolved=False. That is exactly
rich_3469's test_inline_code failing on pygments color output. So per-task dependency pinning is not
cosmetic env-matching; it is REQUIRED by the harness's own whole-file bar. The audit's fix was correct and
necessary, and now we know why.

### IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR A LOCAL REPLICA
- Evaluator picks ContainerManager or SubprocessManager from config.sandbox -- the non-Docker path is
  first-class, not a fallback. That is the Colab/local route.
- SubprocessSandbox is explicitly recognized as a real sandbox (verification.py L655-660).
- JUnit XML is MANDATORY (L681: no XML on a real sandbox -> resolved=False). Our replay engine already
  passes --junitxml= and uses -q, which prints "N passed in Xs" -- satisfies both the XML and stdout checks.
- Evaluator._hydrate_task_from_secret loads test_patch_map/patch_map from a sibling secret/ bundle
  (solution.parquet/csv). That is where the real FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS come from -- hidden data we do
  not have. For the 129 PUBLIC tasks this does not bite (test_patch present -> nodes derived from patch),
  so public tasks are faithfully scorable offline. Hidden tasks are not.

## ROUTER SPEC STEP 1 RESULT (2026-10-15) -- labels built, headroom measured, NO GPU

Script: train/build_router_labels.py. Outputs: train/data/router_labels.json, train/data/router_headroom.json

### 1a. PATH LABELS: 114 of 129 tasks (48 rich + 66 fastapi)
Drops: 14 no_repo (requests 13 + httpx 1 -- repos not cloned locally), 1 no_source_hunks.
- n_edits: median 2, max 92.  multi-file: 34.  test_nodes derived: 113 tasks.
- target_named_in_issue: only 19 of 114 (17%).
- symptom_class: render 36, contract 27, io 25, other 18, parse 8.

### 1b. HEADROOM over 143 classified traced rich failures
  never_committed               37  (26%)
  path_wrong                    16  (11%)
  unreachable                    3  (2%)
  path_right_content_wrong      51  (36%)
  no_trace_or_label             36  (25%)
  ROUTER-ADDRESSABLE (sum of first three): 56/143 (39%)
  SYNTHESIS-ONLY (path_right_content_wrong): 51/143 (36%)

PRE-REGISTERED BAR was "if path_right_content_wrong dominates, stop". It is the largest SINGLE class
(36%) but does NOT dominate -- router-addressable is 39%. BAR NOT TRIPPED.

### BUT THE ROUTING-SPECIFIC TARGET IS NARROW AND NOT LEARNABLE FROM THE INPUT
Splitting the 39% addressable:
- path_wrong (genuine routing) = 16/143 = 11%
- never_committed = 26% -- this is the COMMITMENT problem in a different shirt (8 refuted LoRA levers)
- unreachable = 2% -- budget

And the 16 path_wrong cases are concentrated in THREE tasks, 12 of them rich_4076 alone. The model's
guesses across 12 different runs/prompts for rich_4076: markdown.py, text.py, pretty.py, containers.py,
_wrap.py, panel.py+rule.py -- gold is rich/ansi.py. It never once picked ansi.py.

DECISIVE CHECK -- is the correct route inferable from the issue text? NO:
  rich_4076  "preserve newlines" (71 chars)            -> gold rich/ansi.py :: decode      named=False
  rich_3469  "fix superfluous space" (75 chars)        -> gold rich/markdown.py            named=False
  rich_4079  "Inline table code" (71 chars)            -> gold rich/markdown.py            named=False
All three are PR-title-length statements with no target named. There is no lexical path from
"preserve newlines" to ansi.py -- that requires KNOWLEDGE, not routing. A router trained on these would
have to memorize, which is the forbidden bake.

### THIS CORROBORATES AN EXISTING HYPOTHESIS WE NEVER TESTED
Log ~L8864 already recorded, post-hoc on n=12: "statements under 100 chars (3944, 3470, 3480, 3472) went
0/4; statements of 450+ chars went 5/7. Possible reading: terse PR-title statements are under-determined.
NOT tested on the other 36 rich tasks." Step 1 now supplies the mechanism: the three routing failures all
have 71-75 char statements. Statement informativeness, not routing skill, is the binding constraint.

### VERDICT ON THE ROUTER SPEC
Not a hard stop (the bar was not tripped), but the routing-specific addressable share is 11%, concentrated
in 3 tasks whose correct route is not inferable from the input without memorizing. Training a router on
these would be the forbidden bake. The 26% never_committed chunk is the commitment problem, already
refuted across 8 levers.

RECOMMENDATION: do not proceed to Step 2 (train the router) on this evidence. The durable finding is that
STATEMENT INFORMATIVENESS predicts outcome -- which is a measurable, generalizable feature and a different
lever than routing. No GPU spent, no scored slot spent.

## FASTAPI vs RICH -- MEASURED (2026-10-15). Spec: kb/proposals/2026-10-15-fastapi-corpus-spec.md

User: *"we've been attacking Rich but are the fastapi issues easier to train off and have less randomness?"*
All numbers below are from files on disk (kb/runs.jsonl, train/data/router_labels.json). No GPU.

| | rich | fastapi |
|---|---|---|
| public tasks | 48 (37%) | 66 (52%) |
| traced runs | 201 | 29 |
| resolved | 58 (29%) | 0 (0%) |
| statement chars median / mean | 138 / 486 | 676 / 1112 |
| statements < 100 chars | 20/48 (42%) | 3/66 (5%) |
| target_named_in_issue | 7/48 (15%) | 12/66 (18%) |
| multi-file gold | 11/48 (23%) | 23/66 (35%) |
| per-task resolve rate mean | 0.24 | 0.00 |
| deterministic tasks (>=0.8 or <=0.2) | 15/17 (88%) | 5/5 (100%) |
| coin-flip tasks (0.3<r<0.7) | 0/17 | 0/5 |

### ANSWER
LESS RANDOM: yes, decisively -- but fastapi's determinism is deterministic FAILURE (0/29 resolved), not
stability. Zero coin-flip tasks in EITHER repo, so neither is genuinely noisy at the per-task level;
rich's spread comes from a mix of always-resolve and never-resolve tasks, not from coin flips.

EASIER TO TRAIN OFF: the INPUT signal is far better -- fastapi statements are ~5x longer (median 676 vs
138) and only 5% are terse vs 42% for rich. But there are NO positive agent runs to imitate (0/29).

### THE REFRAME THAT MATTERS
For a ROUTER we do not need successful agent runs -- we need (statement -> gold path) pairs, and the gold
path is derivable for all 66 fastapi tasks from gold patch + test_patch. So fastapi is the BETTER label
source even though it is the worse agent. This is exactly why fastapi was not viable for the commitment
LoRA (needs passing trajectories) but IS viable for a router.

### AND THE BOARD IS MAJORITY FASTAPI
66 of 129 public tasks (52%) vs rich 48 (37%). We have been optimising the smaller, terser, noisier slice.

### SPEC STEPS (all NO GPU until step 4)
1. FastAPI headroom classification -- re-run the four-way classifier over the 29 traced fastapi rows
   (build_router_labels.py currently filters rich only). Bar: if path_right_content_wrong dominates,
   fastapi is a synthesis problem and better statements do not help -- stop.
2. Statement informativeness -> path inferability across all 114 labelled tasks. This is the test the log
   flagged as never run (~L8864). Bar: must predict in BOTH repos or it is rich-specific.
3. Domain-shift check -- train-on-fastapi/validate-on-rich and vice versa. Bar: cross-repo path-match must
   beat the trivial baseline in BOTH directions, else it is a per-repo lookup.
4. Then decide the corpus, with numbers.

### RISKS RECORDED
fastapi 0% (no positive behaviour -- mitigated: router labels come from gold); domain shift (step 3);
better statements may mean easier TASKS not more signal (step 2 measures path inferability, not
difficulty); forbidden bake (route on shape, by-task holdout); fastapi tasks are bigger (35% multi-file,
statements to 10,095 chars -- cap length in training and measure whether truncation hurts).

Script: train/build_router_labels.py --repos fastapi (repo filter made configurable).
Outputs: train/data/router_labels_fastapi.json, train/data/router_headroom_fastapi.json

### THE FASTAPI QUESTION CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM EXISTING DATA
29 traced fastapi rows, but 23 of them (79%) are UNCLASSIFIABLE:

  fastapi_14246  _v10_kaggle_pull   never_committed          model=[] gold=fastapi/_compat/v2.py
  fastapi_14356  _v10_kaggle_pull   path_right_content_wrong model=gold file (dependencies/utils.py)

To answer the fastapi question we must GENERATE fastapi traces. Cheapest path: the v6w kernel already

## AUDIT VERDICT — content-correctness LoRA (NEEDS-DATA). Probe is REDUNDANT; data plan has no correctness signal. 2026-10-15

Via `gemma-audit` on `Gemma\kb\proposals\2026-10-15-content-correctness-lora-recipe.md`. Both passes NEEDS-DATA;
final = **NEEDS-DATA**. Reports: `Gemma\kb\audits\2026-10-15-content-correctness-lora.md` (+ `-refute.md`,
`-final.md`). The DIRECTION is upheld (WRONG-FIX = largest traced-rich class 57/155 = 37%, a genuine
fix-CONTENT failure; multi-layer adapters demonstrably take effect; prior adapter failures are execution
faults, not a refutation). It is NEEDS-DATA because both of the recipe's own gates are mis-specified and the
mechanisms it named don't work. Load-bearing corrections (all MEASURED):

1. **The Colab adapter-effect probe is REDUNDANT.** Our own runs are a natural A/B on the scored stack:
   `v2_gate_out` shipped the competition SAMPLE layer-0 stub (config byte-equal to `comp_files\adapter_config.json`,
   217,672 B) and behaved baseline-like (edits 5/5, rich_4077 resolved); `v2_gate_out2` shipped a 410-module
   multi-layer adapter (979 MB) on the same stack and produced tool_calls=0 on 5/5 (NUDGE_EXHAUSTED). Multi-layer
   adapters have a LARGE effect already. The open question is span/rank/STRENGTH (help vs OVERBAKE), not existence.
   => The probe does not need to be run; keep it only as a cheap wheelhouse smoke-test if convenient.
2. **CORRECTION to my own prior entry:** "v2 was near-inert partly due to layer-0" is FALSE. v2 was 410-module
   multi-layer and OVER-STRONG (not inert); the host's layer-0 renorm rule explains the SAMPLE stub (which
   v2_gate_out shipped), not the trained v2.
3. **No local 31B eval stack exists.** `eval_hf_adapter.py` is E2B 4-bit HF (no vLLM, not 31B); `run_local.py`
   drives a 12B GGUF stand-in (a 31B adapter can't serve on it); rp-4 scores PATCHES, not agent runs. So the
   recipe's "LOCAL no-adapter vs LOCAL adapter baseline" has NO stack. The first trustworthy judge is the FREE
   Kaggle rich gate — not a local run.
4. **The data plan has no correctness signal.** Self-distilling PASSING trajectories reinforces what the model
   already writes correctly; the failing class (one-char-wrong content on the right line, 5.5x-oversized-but-wrong
   diffs) is absent from successes BY CONSTRUCTION. The correctness signal lives in gold or in execution-feedback /
   preference pairs (pass-vs-fail on the same task, which rp-4 CAN now label offline). The recipe's "no gold" rule
   also bans the two already-built gold-DERIVED assets (`rich_gold_trajectories.jsonl` 45 rows,
   `wrongfix_contrastive_rich.jsonl` 56 rows) without resolving training-use vs inference-staging — a rules
   question to settle, not assume.
5. Methodology catches: "34 wrong_content cases" is 10 distinct tasks x repeated runs (overstates n ~3x);
   `same_file_as_gold=34/34` is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION (restates the label); `leakcheck --scope config` EXITS 1 on
   bare task ids rich_4079/rich_3535 in the proposal (no gold text, but ids must not travel into any config/prompt);
   `train_lora.py --maxlen` default is still 768 vs ~3600-token trajectories (must pass >=8192). Distinct rich
