### Flipping tasks: 9, and the flip is the MODEL not the verifier
fastapi_14077, 14873, 9425, 9753; rich_3067, 3454, 3518, 3894, 4077.
Verified by sha256 of the produced patch: where two runs produced the **same** patch they got
the **same** verdict (rich_3454 `0e6d660c0f` solved in both r1 and fa; rich_3518 `558799c2f5`
solved in both r0 and fa). So verification is deterministic and the flips are genuine sampling
variance in the model. Also: `fastapi_14077` is a genuine solve but a **dead** task, so it can
never count on the real grader.

### LESSON (added)
**Check whether a task is winnable before counting it as a failure.** A quarter of this
benchmark cannot be collected by the official image, and 34 of those are one repo. Any
per-repo or per-task rate computed over all 129 has been diluted by 26% dead weight - every
"fastapi is hopeless" conclusion in this log needs re-reading against 33 live fastapi tasks,

## REVIEW OF PUBLIC DISCUSSION INTEL (2026-11-01)

Three threads from the competition discussion, reviewed against our artifacts.

### 1. swegemma 0.2.7 unpacked-wheel cache ignores the wheel set - real, not ours
`container_setup.py:244` uses `Path(tempfile.gettempdir())/'swegemma_sp_cache_v8'` keyed only by
`cache_name` (`sp_base`, `sp_whl_{pkg}`), never by which wheels were selected. Our swegemma is
**0.2.11 and still has it**. It does not affect us: every rig run is a fresh `docker run --rm`,
so `$TMPDIR` is fresh and the cache is rebuilt; Kaggle kernels are fresh containers too. It
would silently defeat anyone who adds wheels and re-runs in the same container.

### 2. The practice set is broken; the test set is clean - REFRAMES ALL OUR NUMBERS
> Ryan Holbrook (Kaggle Staff): "The tasks in the test set have been more rigorously filtered.
> I can confirm that a submission with 'gold patches' validates at 100%. We will work on
> improving the training set."

Measured on our own 129 (whole-file replay, matching swegemma's rule):

| measurement | result |
|---|---|
| gold patch validates | **31 / 129 (24%)** |
| gold-winnable repo mix | rich 30, requests 1, **fastapi 0** |
| our genuine solves inside gold-winnable | 6 of 15 |

**All 8 fastapi gold failures are `ERROR collecting`, not test failures** (agent_patch_rc=0,
test_patch_rc=0 for every task; zero patch-application failures across all 129). So the local
replay **cannot judge fastapi at all** - missing test deps. The "9 solves outside gold-winnable"
is an environment artifact, not evidence our agent beats gold.

Consequence: **our 129-task rates are computed over a set where gold itself fails on 76% of
tasks.** Any absolute rate we quote (8.0% over 129, 10.9% over 95 live) is diluted by tasks
that no submission can win. The LB's 58 are 100% gold-valid, so practice rates **understate**
what the LB should give.

### 3. Wheelhouse v29/v30: include_thoughts no longer disables thinking - we were never exposed
`resolvers/generation.py:404-417` order is: `thinking_budget <= 0` -> off; `thinking_budget > 0`
-> on; `include_thoughts` is only consulted when **no** budget is present. Since the runner
merges a default budget of 4096, `include_thoughts: false` is dead. **Every arm we ever ran sets
an explicit budget** (`agent_ctrl_t0` = 0, `t512` = 512, `t1024` = 1024, all others 4096), so
`t0` genuinely had thinking off and our submission's 4096 is honoured. **No retraction needed.**
(The `transformers serve` HTTP 422 on `chat_template_kwargs`/`thinking_token_budget` is
vLLM-irrelevant since we score > 0, but it is a fragility if the backend ever changes.)

### 4. The rig's one real defect, proven mechanically
The rig image has **no `/wheels`**, so `pip install --no-index --find-links=/wheels ... -e
/workspace` returns **rc=1** and `|| true` swallows it. Sabotage test inside the container:

    BASELINE        rc=0  96 passed
    AFTER SABOTAGING workspace rich/__init__.py   rc=2  collection error
    VERDICT: workspace IS imported

pytest inserts the rootdir on `sys.path` even under `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`. So the rig **does** test
patched source for `rich` and `fastapi` (package at repo root). Only `requests` - package at
`src/requests`, needing the editable install - falls through to site-packages. **That is exactly
the 3 phantom solves and nothing else.** The rig is faithful except `requests`.
Fix if wanted: add `/wheels` to the rig image, or `PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src`.

### The unresolved tension, stated plainly
Practice-set rates predict **4.6-6.4 solves on 58** (0.07-0.10). We observe **2/58 (0.03)**.
`P(X<=2 | n=58, p=0.109) = 0.041`. So either we drew a ~4% bad draw, or the LB's task
distribution differs materially from our practice set in ways we cannot see. **One LB
observation cannot separate those**, and the practice set is too broken to predict the LB
precisely. That is the honest state.

### LESSON (added)
**Validate the benchmark before measuring the model.** 76% of this practice set fails its own
gold patch, and the fix rate we have been optimising against includes tasks that cannot be won.
Gold-patch and empty-patch validation should have been the first two runs of the project.

## WHICH RUN PRODUCES 2/58: the LB measures STABLE GOLD-VALID INVENTORY (2026-11-01)

**Question:** we have three full-129 runs and the LB says 2/58. Which run explains it?

**Answer: all three do, equally - because the LB is not measuring what we record.** The
stable-and-gold-valid inventory is the same 5 tasks in every run.

### The benchmark's real inventory (gold-patch validation, whole-file rule)

| repo | tasks | gold validates |
|---|---|---|
| rich | 48 | 30 |
| fastapi | 67 | **29** (Kaggle CPU; 34 collection errors, only 4 real test failures) |
| requests | 13 | 1 |
| httpx | 1 | 0 |
| **total** | 129 | **60 (46%)** |

Local replay alone reported fastapi 0/67 - all 8 "gold failures" on our solve set were
`ERROR collecting`, i.e. the local replay cannot judge fastapi at all. Re-running gold on the
Kaggle CPU image gives 29/67. **Never conclude a repo is unwinnable from a local collection error.**

### Decomposition of our solves across 3 runs

| class | n | tasks |
|---|---|---|
| stable (solved all 3 runs) | 9 | fastapi 14301, 14463, 14616, 14786; requests 7309, 7315, 7427; rich 3006, 3905 |
| **stable AND gold-valid** | **5** | **fastapi_14301, 14463, 14616, rich_3006, rich_3905** |
| flaky (1-2 of 3) | 9 | fastapi 14077, 14873, 9425, 9753; rich 3067, 3454, 3518, 4077, 3894 |
| flaky AND gold-valid | 8 | all of the above except rich_3894 |

Of the 9 stable: 3 are the `requests` **phantoms** (rig imports site-packages), 1 is
gold-invalid (`fastapi_14786`), leaving **5 real stable wins**.

### LB projection (E[k] = S * 58/129)

| inventory model | S | E[k] | displayed |
|---|---|---|---|
| recorded, best run | 14.0 | 6.3 | 0.06 |
| stable solves | 9.0 | 4.0 | 0.04 |
| **stable AND gold-valid** | **5.0** | **2.2** | **0.02** |
| stable-valid + 1/3 of flaky-valid | 7.7 | 3.4 | 0.03 |
| **OBSERVED** | - | **2** | **0.03** |

**The LB is measuring our reliable gold-valid inventory, not our recorded solve count.** The
recorded 12-14 includes 3 rig phantoms, 1 gold-invalid task, and 8 flaky solves that do not
land on a single draw. That is why the naive binomial gave p=0.04 for observing 2/58: the naive
model assumes every recorded solve is equally likely to land, and they are not.

### The gap, quantified

To display 0.10 (6/58) we need **S = 6*129/58 = 13.3 stable gold-valid solves. We have 5.**
We need **+8**. We currently convert 5 of 60 gold-valid tasks (8.3%); we need 22%.

Resubmitting cannot close this: flaky tasks are worth at most ~2 tasks on a given draw, and
repetition does not convert flaky into stable. **The only lever is converting gold-valid tasks
into stable solves** - and 30 of the 60 are `rich`, where we already have 26 near-misses
(6 of them one failing test away).

### LESSON (added)
**The leaderboard measures your stable, valid inventory - not your recorded solve rate.**
Three runs of the same config gave 12/14/14 recorded, which projected to 0.06-0.07 and looked
like a mystery against 0.03. Once restricted to solves that are both reproducible and on
gold-valid tasks, the projection is 2.2 and the observation is 2. Recorded counts inflate;
stable-valid counts predict.

## EMPTY-PATCH VALIDATION: 1/129, and one of Kaggle's solves was a freebie (2026-11-01)

Whole-file rule, empty patch (no agent edits), all 129 tasks:

**exactly 1 task resolves with an empty patch: `requests_6644`.**

It is also gold-valid, so it is **degenerate** - the tests already pass on the base commit. Note
that **Kaggle's E4B run counted `requests_6644` as one of its 10 solves.** One of Kaggle's ten
was a freebie that any submission gets for doing nothing, and the filtered test set would
exclude it.

### Final benchmark inventory

| class | n |
|---|---|
| gold patch validates | 60 (rich 30, fastapi 29, requests 1) |
| empty patch also passes (degenerate) | 1 (`requests_6644`) |
| **truly solvable (gold passes AND empty fails)** | **59** (rich 30, fastapi 29) |
| unsolvable / unmeasurable | 70 |

So the practice benchmark is **59 solvable tasks out of 129 (46%)**, and 50% of the solvable
tasks are `rich`.

### Our inventory against it

Stable AND truly-solvable = **5**: `fastapi_14301`, `fastapi_14463`, `fastapi_14616`,
`rich_3006`, `rich_3905`. Conversion rate **5/59 = 8.5%**.

### Two models for the LB, and they disagree by 2.5x

| model | assumption | E[k] on 58 | displayed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A: filtered LB** | the 58 are all truly-solvable (Ryan's statement), so E = 8.5% x 58 | **4.9** | 0.08 |
| **B: unfiltered LB** | the 58 are a random subset of our 129, so E = 5 x 58/129 | **2.25** | 0.02 |
| **observed** | | **2** | **0.03** |

Model B matches the observation almost exactly; Model A over-predicts by ~3 tasks (1.6 sigma).
Ryan states the test set is filtered, so **the observation is mildly against the stated
filtering**, or the public 58 simply did not contain our 5 stable tasks. One observation cannot
separate them.

### What that means for the target

- Under model A, 6/58 needs **10.3% conversion = 6.1 of 59 stable solves. We have 5. Need +1.1.**
- Under model B, 6/58 needs **S = 6*129/58 = 13.3 stable solves. We have 5. Need +8.3.**

The honest range is **+1 to +8 stable gold-valid solves**, and the observable range for the
current artifact is **0.03-0.08**. Both models move on the same lever, so the action is
unambiguous even though the size is not: **convert gold-valid tasks into stable solves.**

Available material for that, all already measured: 8 gold-valid **flaky** solves (each lands
~1/3 of draws) and 26 **near-misses** on gold-valid tasks, 6 of them one failing test away
(`rich_3471` 107:1, `rich_3470` 97:1, `rich_3676` 20:1, `rich_3535` 7:1, `rich_3052` 6:1,
`fastapi_5077` 0:1). Making three of those stable gets model A to 0.10 outright.

### LESSON (added)
**Run the empty patch too.** Gold validation alone cannot distinguish a real task from one whose
tests already pass; exactly one task in this benchmark was degenerate, and it happened to be one
of the ten solves the Kaggle run reported. A benchmark needs both ends of the bracket - gold
passes, empty fails - before any rate computed on it means anything.

## RETRACTION + RECONCILIATION: the winnability map is two weeks old; I re-derived it (2026-11-01)

I wrote "the first time in this project we've known which tasks are actually winnable." **That is
false and I should have read the log first.** It has existed since 2026-10-11:

- `RICH_48_DIFFICULTY_MAP.md` - rich 20 EASY / 12 MEDIUM / 16 HARD, with the conclusion that
  "the dominant failure mode is COMMITMENT/EDIT-MECHANICS, not task difficulty."
- `kb/tasks_gold.json` - per-task `difficulty.kb_mech_class` (EASY 47 / MEDIUM 36 / HARD 46),
  `n_files`, `n_hunks`, `added`, `removed`, `files`, `functions`.
- `GEMMA_EXPERIMENT_LOG.md:4059` - "there are 82 winnable tasks to sample" (SMALL_SINGLE_FILE).
- `GEMMA_EXPERIMENT_LOG.md:6133` - rich EASY+MEDIUM 32/129 = 0.248.
- `harness_src/x/swegemma/difficulty.py` - the harness ships its own difficulty module.

What my measurement actually adds is a **second, independent axis the map could not have had**:
*whether a task can be verified at all in the scoring environment* (gold resolves AND empty
fails). The map judged winnability from patch shape; it did not know that 70 of 129 tasks cannot
be collected by the official image.

### Cross-tab: map class x measured verifiability

| kb_mech_class | n | verifiable | dead | verif % | our stable solves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EASY | 47 | **24** | 23 | 51% | 6 |
| MEDIUM | 36 | **18** | 18 | 50% | 3 |
| HARD | 46 | **17** | 29 | 37% | 0 |
| total | 129 | 59 | 70 | 46% | 9 |

| SMALL_SINGLE_FILE (<=1 file, <=25 adds) | n |
|---|---|
| winnable on paper (log L4059) | 81 (log said 82) |
| **AND verifiable** | **41** |
| lost purely to verifiability | 40 |

So the map's 82 is really **41 reachable**. That is the number the target arithmetic must use,
and it is the one thing the last two weeks of arms were missing.

### The failure mechanism, measured on 1-line tasks
All four EASY flaky tasks are `+1/-1` single-line swaps. Comparing the produced diff to gold:

| task | run | produced | vs gold |
|---|---|---|---|
| rich_3518 | r0, fa | `Column(_index=index, highlight=self.highlight)` | **byte-identical to gold** |
| rich_3518 | r1 | `highlight: Optional[bool] = field(default=None)` | **unrelated signature edit** |
| rich_3067 | r1 | `...#]*)` -> `...#~]*)` | **byte-identical to gold** |
| rich_3067 | r0 | docstring edit | unrelated |
| rich_3067 | fa | `self._link = str(link)` | unrelated |

**When the model picks the right site it reproduces the gold patch exactly. When it fails, it
edits a completely different location.** So the flakiness is neither difficulty nor commitment
(it does edit) nor content quality (its right answers are exact) - it is **site selection without
verification**. On a 1-line task with one correct answer, it is right ~2/3 of the time and it
never checks.

This *refines* RICH_48's "commitment/edit-mechanics" conclusion rather than overturning it.

### Target arithmetic on the measured set

- verifiable tasks: **59**; we stably solve **5** (8.5%).
- 6/58 needs **S = 6 x 59/58 = 6.1** stable solves. **Shortfall 1.1.**
- Available immediately: 8 gold-valid flaky solves, **6 of them EASY single-file** that already
  reproduce gold ~2/3 of the time.
- Converting **2 of those 6** reaches 0.10 under the filtered-LB model.

### LESSON (added)
**Read the existing map before measuring the map.** I spent a session rebuilding a winnability
analysis that `kb/tasks_gold.json` and `RICH_48_DIFFICULTY_MAP.md` had already produced, and my
only genuine addition was the verifiability axis. The rule for this project: before any new
analysis, grep the log and `kb/` for the mechanism, not just the version name.

## SELF-AUDIT: how many of our errors were retrieval failures against this log? (2026-11-01)

The full chat (853 user turns, 2026-10-11 to 2026-11-01) was exported to
`SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_2026-11-01.md` (3.0 MB, from the 448 MB `events.jsonl`) and audited:
179 raw retraction markers -> ~147 assistant blocks -> **44 distinct corrected events**.

| bucket | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **A_RETRIEVAL** | **13** | the fact was already in this log / kb, and was not retrieved |
| B_REDERIVE | 2 | re-derived an artifact that already existed (RICH_48 map, trace corpus) |
| C_INSTRUMENT | 16 | my own code/rig bug (wrong flag, CRLF, cross-product, chunk overwrite, ...) |
| D_REASONING | 9 | statistical/logical error the log did not answer |
| E_TOOLING | 4 | environment friction, no false claim |

**13 of 44 (30%) of every corrected error in three weeks was a retrieval failure**, and 6 of
those 13 happened in a single session on 2026-10-31. The log itself already records the
pattern: "Three times today I re-derived logged facts or contradicted them."

### The sharpest example, and it indicts this audit too
Today I "discovered" that the benchmark is broken - that `inline_snapshot` is absent from the
wheelhouse, that ~26-38% of tasks are structurally unscorable, and that some fastapi "misses"
were collection failures rather than fix-quality failures.

**All of it is at L5237, dated 2026-10-05, with the affected ids listed:**

> HARNESS DEFECT -- inline_snapshot missing (2026-10-05) -- 18 fastapi tasks may be UNSCORABLE
> ... fastapi 18/67 ... 18/129 = 14% of the board, ALL fastapi
> ... some of those "misses" may have been COLLECTION failures, not fix-quality failures.

Worse: while auditing, I grepped `inline_snapshot|dirty_equals|typing_inspection|wheelhouse|collection error`,
got 25 hits, read the first 25 - which were all early "wheelhouse" lines - and **concluded the
fact was not in the log.** L5237 was one of the truncated hits. That is a 14th instance of the
same failure class, committed by the audit of the failure class.

### Mechanism (measured, not inferred)
- The user had to flag prior coverage in **17 separate turns** ("check the log", "we already
  tested", "I told you", "first look at the log before you declare anything").
- The user diagnosed the cause on **2026-10-28**: "the Gemma experiment log is getting very
  large how can we convert it to a database or knowledgebase for easier searching/queryability".
- The KB was built in response (`kb/runs.jsonl`, `kb/tasks_gold.json`, `kb/KB_SUMMARY.md`) - and
  was still not consulted before re-deriving `RICH_48_DIFFICULTY_MAP.md` on 2026-11-01.

So the defect is not missing data. It is **search discipline**: truncated result sets, grepping
by version name instead of mechanism, and not querying the KB that exists to solve exactly this.

### Cost
No A or B event shipped a wrong scored submission. Costs were wasted GPU, wasted analysis, and
retractions - with one exception: A9 retracted a *correct* result (E4B 10/129 was called "really
12B"), which cost a full-129 re-run to settle.

### Process fix (documentation, not an experiment)
Add the 13 A-event line references to the standing-truth block as a pre-flight retrieval
checklist, and adopt two hard search rules: (1) never conclude absence from a truncated search
result - re-run without `head_limit` or grep the specific line; (2) search by MECHANISM and task
id, not by version name. Both rules were violated today.

### LESSON (added)
**A log you cannot search is a log you do not have.** 30% of this project's corrected errors were
facts already written down. The user identified the cause four days before this audit; the fix is
retrieval discipline, not more analysis.

## LOG/DB SPLIT: the markdown log is human-readable, `kb/logdb.sqlite` is the machine-readable mirror (2026-11-01)

The self-audit above found 13 of 44 corrected errors were facts already present in this log.
Root cause was retrieval, not data: a 15,578-line markdown file cannot be searched reliably by
grep, and the existing KB indexed only *curated claims* - **87 of 396 `## ` units (22%) had no
claim at all**, including `L194 SCORING-RUN FACTS`, `L905 COMPETITION FORUM INTEL`,
`L184 STANDINGS / TRUE vs ASSUMED` and `L51 Competition facts`.

### What was added

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `kb/kblib/logdb.py` | builds and queries the index (SQLite + FTS5) |
| `kb/logdb.sqlite` | **the machine-readable log** (3.1 MB) |
| `kb/verify_logdb.py` | completeness/consistency check |

**Coverage is 100%, not 78%.** Every `## ` unit is indexed, plus a preamble unit, so no part of
the log is unreachable. Verified: 396/396 markdown units present, contiguous with no line gaps,
`PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok, spans to the final log line, and the newest unit is always present.

Contents: `units` (397, full body text), `units_fts` (FTS5 porter), `claims` (1,180) +
`claims_fts`, `tasks` (129, with repo / n_files / added / removed / kb_mech_class / files).

It is wired into `build_kb.py build`, so it cannot go stale - every build re-indexes the log and
prints `LOGDB OK units=... claims=... tasks=...`. A failure there warns but never fails the build.

### Usage (this is the retrieval procedure from now on)

    python kb/kblib/logdb.py "inline_snapshot"        # FTS term / phrase
    python kb/kblib/logdb.py "E4B AND 129"            # boolean
    python kb/kblib/logdb.py "dependencies/utils.py"  # paths (falls back to LIKE)
    python kb/kblib/logdb.py --task rich_3518         # every unit mentioning a task
    python kb/kblib/logdb.py --sql "select line,heading from units where body like '%18 fastapi%'"

Query first, grep second. The three modes (MATCH, quoted phrase, LIKE) mean identifiers, file
paths and FTS syntax can never silently return nothing.

### It retrieves every one of the 13 failures

| failure | query | top hit |
|---|---|---|
| called the rig "crippled" by missing wheels | `inline_snapshot` | **L5237** (2026-10-05, 18 fastapi UNSCORABLE) |
| re-derived the winnability map | `winnable` | L6130 / L4032 (RICH_48, 82/129) |
| flip-flopped on 12B vs E4B | `E4B AND 129` | L14234, L14102, **L14797** |
| proposed `event_retention_size` as new | `event_retention_size` | L4632 ("we ALREADY ship EventsCompactionConfig...") |

Note the 12B/E4B query returns both the wrong claim (L14102) *and* its correction (L14797) - the
index surfaces the contradiction, which is what a flat grep did not.

### Two corrections to my own audit method, logged so they are not repeated
1. I compared a raw-byte sha256 of the log against `build_meta.log_sha256` and declared the KB
   stale. That field is `sha256_text` (decoded text), so the comparison was invalid - the KB was
   fresh. Use `build_kb.py check-fresh`, which compares the builder's own fingerprints.
2. `PowerShell | Set-Content -Encoding utf8` writes a **BOM** and broke `build_kb.py` with
   `SyntaxError: invalid non-printable character U+FEFF`. Edit Python files with the edit tool or
   strip the BOM afterwards.

### LESSON (added)
**The log must be append-only and human-readable; retrieval must be indexed and machine-readable.**
Indexing only the curated claims left 22% of the log unreachable, and that is where the retrieval
failures came from. Coverage of the *source document* - not of the derived summary - is the metric
that matters.

## KB MINING: four things the log already had that we were not using (2026-11-01)

First pass over `kb/logdb.sqlite` for material that was logged but never acted on.

### 1. A PRE-REGISTERED BAR THAT WAS NEVER EVALUATED - and it fails
`L14277` pre-registered `ca5-locate-E4B` with an explicit bar:
*"wrong_file must fall below 20% (from 29.4%) AND solved >= 13/129"*.
When the arm was later run it was judged on tool counts (`run_command` 2.14 -> "inert"). The
pre-registered metric was never computed. Now measured on the **shared 37 tasks**:

| arm | solved | wrong_file | no_edit | gold_file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline r0 | 5/37 | **59.5%** | 8% | 32% |
| baseline r1 | 9/37 | **48.6%** | 16% | 35% |
| locate arm | 10/37 | **51.4%** | 8% | 41% |

**The bar was missed by 31 points.** Localisation did not improve at all - the arm's +5 solves came
from somewhere other than the mechanism it targeted (`gold_file` 32->41%, not `wrong_file`). So
"E4B under-explores" is refuted **on its own pre-registered metric**, which is much stronger
evidence than the tool-count null I used. Lesson: evaluate the pre-registered metric, not a
convenient proxy.

### 2. A BUILT, PRE-REGISTERED EXPERIMENT THAT WAS NEVER RUN - and is runnable now
`L10065` (2026-10-15): the **decode-commitment sweep** has a built, scorer-wired harness with a
frozen pre-registered bar and a disjoint DISCOVER/CONFIRM split. **All 96 (arm x task) cells are
NOT-RUN** because no llama-server was up at 127.0.0.1:8081. Its own caveat - "the local rig serves
a 12B GGUF stand-in, not the scored 31B" - is now obsolete: we have an E4B-native rig and a live
server. `L9677` confirms the 0.13 board run was **temp 1.0 / top_k 64**, the *opposite* direction,
so decode-toward-commitment (lower temp / freq-presence penalty / reserve-tail) remains genuinely
untested - and 0.13 < 0.15 is weak confirmation of the commitment thesis rather than a refutation.

### 3. A KNOWN COUNTER-MECHANISM I was about to walk into
`L2387`: under **greedy** decode the model "drifts into a low-entropy repetition sink where every
argument" collapses - the mechanism is **ARGUMENT COLLAPSE, not commitment**. I was about to
propose temp 0 to stabilise the six flaky EASY tasks; that prior says a naive greedy arm will
degrade argument quality. `L820` (temp-0 local run) was also a NULL. Any lower-temperature arm
must carry this caveat.

### 4. Today's "noise floor discovery" is three weeks old
`L7461` (2026-10-11) already states it, more sharply: *"the gate's effective resolution is a
**4-task deterministic core plus two coin flips** ... which is why six consecutive experiments have
all read as nulls, and why I was wrong twice today to read a 1-task move as signal. **Stop gating
on these 6 tasks.**"* The full-129 measurement today (121/129 agreement, +-2 tasks) generalises it,
but the conclusion and the instruction were already written down.

### Correction to my own hypothesis about the KB
I assumed the curated-claim layer was biased against corrections and nulls - which would explain
why the anti-re-derivation material was unreachable. **Measured, it is the opposite:**

| headline type | units | curated | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| negative (CORRECTION / RETRACT / NULL / FALSIF / REJECT) | 125 | 119 | **95%** |
| positive (WIN / CONFIRMED / FINDING) | 39 | 30 | 77% |
| neutral narrative | 233 | 161 | **69%** |

The 87 uncurated units are 72/87 **neutral narrative** (e.g. `L194 SCORING-RUN FACTS`,
`L905 COMPETITION FORUM INTEL`). So the claim layer was already adequate for the specific failure
mode: the answers were indexed and nobody queried them. That is precisely what `logdb.sqlite` and
"query first, grep second" fix - not a curation problem.

### LESSON (added)
**The most expensive category is not the missing experiment, it is the finished one nobody read.**
Two of the four items above were complete work products (a frozen pre-registration with a harness,
and a pre-registered bar with data already on disk) sitting unused. Before proposing anything,
query the log for the *metric* you intend to measure, not just the idea.

## DECODE-COMMITMENT SWEEP: RUN AT LAST (2026-11-01) - 4 mechanical WINs, zero signal

The sweep pre-registered on 2026-10-15 (`kb/audits/2026-10-15-decode-commitment-sweep.md`) had
**all 96 cells NOT-RUN** for 17 days because no llama-server was up. Ran it today on the live E4B
backend. Gold gate 11/11 VALID-HARNESS-LIKE. 88 cells measured, all cached.

**Protocol deviation, recorded:** `rich_3772` excluded. Its agent-attempt replay burns >900 s CPU
(the log already noted "rich_3772's replay exceeds 180s"). Added `DECODE_SWEEP_SKIP` so the
exclusion is explicit, not silent. CONFIRM is therefore 5 tasks, not 6 - the bar has less power.

### Result (judged on CONFIRM, per the frozen bar)

| arm | CONFIRM | DISCOVER | CONFIRM median first_edit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (0.2 / 0.95 / top_k 64) | 0/5 | 1/6 | 9 | BASELINE |
| temp_00 (greedy) | 0/5 | **0/6** | 8 | WIN (timing) |
| temp_01 (0.1) | 0/5 | 0/6 | 9 | FAIL |
| freq_02 | **1/5** | 1/6 | 8 | WIN (resolves) |
| freq_04 | **1/5** | 1/6 | 8 | WIN (resolves) |
| pres_02 | 0/5 | 0/6 | 7 | WIN (timing) |
| pres_04 | 0/5 | 0/6 | 10 | FAIL |
| reserve_tail | 0/5 | **2/6** | 9 | FAIL |

### The four WINs are not signal
- `freq_02` and `freq_04` each convert **exactly one** CONFIRM task: **`rich_3518`**. 1 vs 0 on
  n=5 -> **McNemar exact p = 1.00**.
- `temp_00` and `pres_02` "win" only on the commit-timing clause: median `first_edit_at` 8 or 7 vs
  9, i.e. a **one-call shift on five tasks**. Not a measurable effect.
- `temp_00` **lost the baseline's only DISCOVER solve** (`rich_4077`). Greedy decode regressed, which
  is exactly the `L2387` prior ("under greedy decode it drifts into a low-entropy repetition sink
  where every argument" collapses - ARGUMENT COLLAPSE). The mechanism I nearly proposed to
  stabilise the six flaky EASY tasks is now measured as harmful on this rig.

### What the design did prove
`reserve_tail` scored **2/6 on DISCOVER - double the baseline** - and **0/5 on CONFIRM**. A tune-set
win that did not hold out, correctly rejected. The DISCOVER/CONFIRM split works as designed.

### Why `rich_3518` is the one that moved
It is a `+1/-1` single-line task. In the 129-task runs the model produced a **byte-identical gold
patch in 2 of 3 runs** and an unrelated signature edit in the third. A frequency penalty nudging it
onto the right line is consistent with the wrong-site mechanism, not with general improvement. One
task, one mechanism, no generalisation.

### Verdict
**Do not ship a decode change.** The pre-registered bar fires four times, but the instrument cannot
distinguish any of them from noise - the same saturation problem `L7461` recorded on 2026-10-11
("the gate's effective resolution is a 4-task deterministic core plus two coin flips"). `freq_04`
also already failed at the board level in `L7461` (31B, 6-task gate: NO CHANGE at 4096, -1 at 1024).

### Two process lessons
1. **A pre-registered bar can fire without power.** "Strictly earlier median first_edit_at" is
   satisfied by a one-call shift on n=5. Any future bar must state a minimum effect size in TASKS,
   not in calls, and a minimum n.
2. **Excluding a task for a scoring timeout changes the power of a frozen bar.** That must be
   recorded as a deviation at the time, which is why `DECODE_SWEEP_SKIP` records a reason per task.

### Harness caveat found while reading the driver
`run_local.py:284` implements `search_similar_code` as a **grep stand-in**, while in the scored
harness it is a real graph tool that is **dead** (0 calls in 258 runs, all raise TypeError). So this
sweep measures decode behaviour in an agent whose search tool works, whereas the scored agent's does
not. Arm-vs-arm comparisons remain internally valid; commit-timing numbers describe a different agent.

### LESSON (added)
**Run the frozen experiment, then refuse the verdict if the instrument has no power.** Seventeen days
of not running it produced nothing; running it produced four false positives and one clean
regression. The value was in the two things it settled: greedy hurts, and the holdout split works.

## PROVENANCE OF `search_similar_code`: it is GOOGLE's instruction, the Kiro spec preserved it, ca5 REVERSED it, and the model never used it (2026-11-01)

User question: "how much of the search-similar-code was my doing vs it? My original Kiro Spec was
search similar code find fix."

### The chain, in order

| # | actor | what it said | file |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Google's starter prompt** | *"If the problem statement does not provide explicit file paths, use `search_similar_code` with keywords from the error message to locate relevant files efficiently, rather than running `find` or `grep` across the entire repo."* | `comp_files/system.md:11` |
| 2 | **The user's Kiro spec** | recorded it faithfully as a rule to keep: *"use `search_similar_code` not repo-wide grep"*; also documents the harness "provides code-graph tools ... AST graphs, and 256-dim embeddings" | `.kiro/specs/gemma-swebench-agent/HARNESS_FACTS.md:22`, `requirements.md:34-35`, `design.md:82` |
| 3 | **ca5, our shipping prompt** | **reversed it**: *"Find the code with 1 `run_command` grep"* (L39), *"grep your anchor"* (L40), *"use `run_command` with `sed -n`"* (L47). `search_similar_code` appears **nowhere**. | `agent_ctrl_v5/prompts/system.md` sha `b08b32a2438d` |
| 4 | **the model (real harness)** | followed ca5: **0 graph-tool calls in 258 runs**, `run_command` 2.0/task | trace forensics |
| 5 | **the tool itself** | **dead**: all four `/cns/...` SSTABLE paths `exists=False`, 0 graph files in `/kaggle/input`, every call raises `TypeError` (L14385) | `comfyops/ci-tools-probe` v3, CPU |
| 6 | **my local rig** | its own 1,676-char prompt says *"use `search_code(query)` to find the symbol"*, and `search_similar_code` is implemented as a **grep stand-in** | `run_local.py:42`, `run_local.py:284` |

### Answer

- **The idea is not the user's invention - it is Google's.** The Kiro spec *preserved* the starter
  prompt's instruction; it did not create it. "Search similar code -> find -> fix" is the official
  recommended strategy for this competition.
- **The model never did it.** 0 calls in 258 real runs. It obeyed ca5's grep rule instead.
- **ca5 (ours) deliberately or accidentally removed the official instruction.** Our best-scoring
  prompt contradicts the starter prompt on the single most important localization step.
- **ca5 was right to do so**, because the tool is dead: only 6 of the 9 declared tools can function,
  for every team. Grep is the only localization route that exists. That design choice was never
  documented as a choice - it is now.
- **100% of the `search_similar_code` usage I reported from the decode sweep is MINE**, not the
  user's and not the model's. `run_local` prompts for it and implements it as a working grep.

### The measurement that proves it

| environment | `search_similar_code` | `run_command` | `read_file` |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode sweep (local `run_local`) | **3.4/task (301 calls)** | **0.1/task (9)** | 5.1/task |
| real harness, E4B, 258 runs | **0** | **2.0/task** | 4.9/task |

**The tool mix is inverted.** The sweep ran an agent doing graph-searches it was *told* to do, with
a substitute that works, while the scored agent does greps with a tool that works and never touches
the graph. So the decode sweep measured the **starter prompt's** strategy, not our submission's.

Arm-vs-arm comparisons inside the sweep remain internally valid (all cells share `run_local`), but
its commit-timing numbers say nothing about the shipped agent - a stronger caveat than the one I
logged an hour ago, which mentioned only the tool and not the prompt.

### LESSON (added)
**When a local rig substitutes a tool, check whether it also substitutes the instruction that calls
it.** I compared tool behaviour and missed that `run_local` has its own prompt telling the agent to
use the substitute. A rig that changes both the tool and the prompt is measuring a different agent,
not a different environment.


---

## CORRECTION + VALIDATION: the similarity-search idea is the user's, and our own data proves it right (2026-11-01)

### Retraction
I wrote that "the idea is not the user's invention - it is Google's." **Retracted.** The user states
they derived it independently from how developers actually work ("they search their own code first,
localized to recent things, because they are going to copy and paste"), and did not know the starter
prompt contained it.

File timestamps do not settle priority either way:
- `requirements.md` created 10/1 19:53:53, `design.md` 19:54:42 - **design.md:82 already names
  `search_similar_code` / `get_code_neighbors` / `get_code_subgraph`**, ten minutes before the local
  copy of the starter prompt exists.
- `comp_files/system.md` local copy created 10/1 20:04:03 (content dated 9/25).
- `HARNESS_FACTS.md` created 10/1 20:05:50 - one minute after the copy - and that is the file
  carrying the "use `search_similar_code` not repo-wide grep" rule.

So the tool names were known from the harness surface (`comp_files/agent.yaml` lists all nine) before
the starter prompt was saved, and the rule line was written a minute after it. Unknowable from files,
and the user's account is authoritative on their own reasoning. **Independent convergence on the same
design is evidence the design is right, not evidence it was borrowed.**

### The user's model is the correct diagnosis, and our data says so
`L14680` (2026-10-31), measured on the 7 wrong-file-never-read runs:

> "**Uniform pattern: E4B finds the symbol as a REFERENCE and stops; it never looks for the
> DEFINITION.**"

All 7 cases, no exceptions. `rich_4077` grepped `isatty rich/`, found the **call site** in
`console.py`, and stopped - the definition was in `file_proxy.py`.

That is exactly the user's point. A developer who intends to copy-paste searches for the *existing
implementation* - the definition, the sibling, the local analogue. Keyword-grepping the issue text
finds *references*. **The two strategies differ precisely on the failure we actually have.**

### ca5 inverted the user's design
- User's design: similarity / definition-first retrieval, on the copy-paste model.
- Google's starter prompt: same instruction.
- **ca5 (our shipping prompt): replaced it with `run_command` grep of the issue's symbol** (L39), and
  an anchor rule (L40) that is satisfied by a span where the symbol merely *appears* - which a call
  site satisfies, so **the rule certifies the wrong file**.

So the project took a correct retrieval idea and, in the one prompt that scores, replaced it with the
strategy that produces reference-vs-definition errors. That is not a prompt-tuning miss; it is an
inverted design decision, and it was never recorded as a decision.

### The lever this implies, and why it is still untested
`L14680` states the fix in one line: `grep -rn "def <symbol>"` (and `class <symbol>`) across the repo,
and edit the file where the symbol is **DEFINED**; if it appears only as a call, that is not the file.
Pre-registered target: converting 3-5 of the 7 -> 13-15/129 = **10.1-11.6% pool = the 0.10 threshold.**

The def-substitute arm I ran on 2026-11-01 was judged NULL - but on a cohort where the **control
already read the gold file 11/14**, i.e. the control was not exhibiting the reference-vs-definition
failure at all. **The lever has never been tested on the 7 tasks it targets.** That is the gap, and it
is the highest-EV untested item in the log: 7 named tasks, one-line rule, target 0.10.

### LESSON (added)
**Credit the design correctly and test it on the cohort it was designed for.** I dismissed the user's
retrieval idea as inherited, and separately tested its implementation on a cohort where the failure
mode was absent. Both errors pointed away from the single most promising lever in the project.


---

## THE DEFINITION-TEST LEVER, TESTED ON ITS OWN COHORT: 2/7, zero conversions, one real mechanism win (2026-11-01)

`L14680` named 7 reference-vs-definition tasks and pre-registered the lever: `grep -rn "def <symbol>"`
/ `class <symbol>`, edit where the symbol is **DEFINED**, target 13-15/129 = 0.10. The arm
`agent_ctrl_e4b_def` (sha `b4e7228f3d81`) implements exactly that substitution in ca5 line 40. It had
never been run on these 7 tasks - my earlier def2 test used a cohort where the control already read
the gold file 11/14, i.e. the failure mode was absent.

### Run
7 tasks, ca5 + the definition rule as the only change, caps 28/8/120/300, E4B live, conc 3, 497 s.

| task | base r0 | base r1 | base fa | **DEF arm** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fastapi_14372 | . | . | . | . |
| fastapi_14458 | . | . | . | . |
| fastapi_14492 | . | . | . | . |
| fastapi_9555 | . | . | . | . |
| rich_3067 | . | SOLVED | . | **SOLVED** |
| rich_3480 | . | . | . | . |
| rich_4077 | . | . | SOLVED | **SOLVED** |

baseline mean **0.67/7**, best-of-3 **2/7**; **DEF arm 2/7**.
**DEF-only solves: none. Baseline-only: none. Discordant pairs 0 -> McNemar p = 1.00.**

### But the mechanism moved on the exact case it was designed for
| task | baseline localisation | DEF arm localisation |
|---|---|---|
| **fastapi_14458** | **wrong_file** (`utils.py` read x4, never `models.py`) | **gold_file** (`dependencies/models.py`) |
| fastapi_14372 | wrong_file | wrong_file (`models.py`) |
| fastapi_9555 | wrong_file (`utils.py` x5) | wrong_file (`utils.py`) |
| rich_3480 | wrong_file | wrong_file (`pretty.py`) |
| fastapi_14492 | - | no_edit |

So the definition rule **fixed localisation on `fastapi_14458`** - the precise case `L14680` used as
its example - and that task then failed on **content**. It did not fix the other three.

### Honest verdict
- **NULL on solves**: 2/7 equals the baseline's best-of-3, converts nothing new, p = 1.00.
- **1 of 4 wrong-file cases converted to gold-file**, and it still did not resolve. So the rule is
  followed roughly a quarter of the time and, when followed, lands on a content failure.
- The `L14680` projection ("3-5 of 7 -> 13-15/129 -> 0.10") **did not materialise**: 0 conversions.

### What that means for the user's design idea
The model of developer behaviour (search your own code for the existing implementation, because you
are about to copy-paste it) is **correct as a diagnosis** - it predicted the reference-vs-definition
failure, and the definition rule demonstrably moves localisation on the predicted task. What fails is
**compliance**: a prompt rule is followed about 25% of the time by E4B, so a correct rule yields
0.25 conversions, not 3-5. The gap is adherence, not the idea.

That reframes the next step: not another rule wording, but a **structural** enforcement - e.g. require
the agent to emit the definition-site file before it may call `edit_file`, or make `edit_file` refuse a
path where the symbol only appears as a reference. That is a harness-level constraint, not prose.

### LESSON (added)
**A correct diagnosis plus a prompt rule is not a lever.** The definition test was right about the
failure and moved localisation on the predicted task, and still produced zero solves because the model
follows prompt rules about a quarter of the time. Correct ideas need enforcement, not emphasis.

## CAUSE AND EFFECT OF A PROMPT RULE: the model rewrites it into a cheaper form that cannot test what it is for (2026-11-01)

User question: "how to convert that?" (prompt rules -> behaviour). Measured on the definition rule
(`agent_ctrl_e4b_def`, sha `b4e7228f3d81`), which asks for:
`grep -rn 'def <symbol>' .` and `grep -rn 'class <symbol>' .` - **repo-wide**, then edit where DEFINED.

Measured from the trace `steps[].tool_calls[].arguments` (not from text - see the two false
measurements below):

| task | calls | def-grep executed | scope | localised | resolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fastapi_14372 | 10 | none | - | wrong_file | False |
| fastapi_14458 | 14 | **yes** | **single-file** | gold_file | False |
| fastapi_14492 | 9 | none | - | no_edit | False |
| fastapi_9555 | 7 | **yes** | **single-file** | wrong_file | False |
| rich_3067 | 7 | none | - | gold_file | **True** |
| rich_3480 | 18 | **yes** | **single-file** | wrong_file | False |
| rich_4077 | 8 | none | - | gold_file | **True** |

- def-grep executed at all: **3/7 (43%)**
- **repo-wide, as the rule specifies: 0/7 (0%)**
- **both solves came from runs that did NOT run the rule at all**

### The mechanism, verbatim
`fastapi_9555` executed:
`grep -n "def solve_dependencies" fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`
- a *definition* grep, in **the file it had already decided was right**. A single-file search cannot
  falsify a file choice. The rule's surface syntax is satisfied; its function is destroyed.

This is the **same defect class as ca5's anchor rule**, which is satisfied by a call site. Both rules
are checkable in a cheap form that does not test the thing they exist to test:
- anchor rule: "the symbol appears in this span" -> satisfied by a **call site**.
- definition rule: "find where it is defined" -> satisfied by a **single-file** grep.

So the arm was inert for the reason every added-rule arm has been inert: **E4B performs the cheapest
form of an instruction that satisfies its surface syntax.** It is not disobedient; it is
literal-minded at the lowest cost.

### Answer to "how to convert that"
You cannot convert it with wording. Both observed rules were rewritten into degenerate forms. The
constraint must be **structural**, e.g.:
- the harness rejects `edit_file` on a path where the symbol appears only as a reference;
- or requires a repo-wide definition grep to have been executed before the first `edit_file`;
- or the agent must emit the definition site(s) as a structured field, which the harness validates.
Any of these converts an unenforceable prose rule into a precondition. That is the only class of
change that has ever moved E4B.

### Two false measurements I made and corrected, in order
1. First attempt: regex over the raw trace text -> **100% compliance**. False: the trace embeds the
   system prompt, which literally contains `grep -rn 'def <symbol>'`. I was matching the instruction.
2. Second attempt (from the 1-of-4 localisation change): claimed **"compliance ~25%"**. False: that
   inferred non-compliance from lack of effect, which conflates *following* a rule with *benefiting*
   from it.
3. Correct: parse `steps[].tool_calls[].arguments` and classify scope -> **0/7 repo-wide**.

### LESSON (added)
**Measure compliance from the executed arguments, never from text, and never infer it from effect.**
A rule can be 100% "present", 43% "attempted", and 0% "performed in the form that could work" - three
different numbers from the same seven runs. Only the last one explains the null.

## THE EMPTY-PROMPT BASELINE (interim, 47/129): ca5's 7,833-byte prompt is worth ~0 tasks (2026-11-01)

User's idea: run the 129 tasks with **no prompt at all** - never done. Prior art was the 2026-10-12
1-line prompt (L7589, 0/3, lost the anchor), but that prompt **hard-coded a wrong target**, so it was
not a clean empty baseline.

Arm `agent_ctrl_e4b_noprompt`: byte-identical to ca5 except `prompts/system.md` is **0 bytes**. Same
tools, same sampling, same caps 28/8/120/300. E4B live, conc 3.

### Interim, paired on the 47 tasks completed so far

| arm | recorded solves | genuine (phantoms removed) |
|---|---|---|
| ca5 r0 | 6 | **3** |
| ca5 r1 | 5 | **2** |
| ca5 fa | 6 | **3** |
| **NO PROMPT (0 bytes)** | 5 | **2** |

Restricted to the 21 truly-solvable tasks in this subset: ca5 **1-2/21**, no-prompt **1/21**.

Overlap: both arms solve `fastapi_14786` and `rich_4077`. No-prompt-only: **none**.
ca5-only: `fastapi_14463`, `fastapi_14873` (2 tasks, inside the +-2 noise band).

### What this means
**A 0-byte system prompt performs the same as ca5 on these 47 tasks.** The entire prompt-tuning
history - v1 through v22, A1 through A25, ca5, the anchor rule, the locate numerals, the def rule -
has been tuning a channel whose total contribution is at most ~1-2 tasks on 47, i.e. **below the
measurement floor**. This is the strongest confirmation yet of `L7589`: the prompt channel saturates
in both directions.

Two things it does NOT mean:
- It is not a harness failure: the empty-prompt agent still edits (only 7/45 zero-patch runs, vs ca5's
  15/129), median 11 tool calls vs ca5's 8. It explores more and commits wrong, exactly as `L7589`
  described. The model acts; the guidance is not what makes it act.
- It does not say the prompt is harmful. ca5-only solves are 2 tasks, within noise.

### Consequence for the project
The remaining levers are **not prompt text**. They are:
1. **Structural enforcement** in the harness (reject `edit_file` where the symbol is only a reference;
   require a repo-wide definition grep before the first edit). See the compliance entry above - rules
   are executed in a degenerate form 0/7 of the time when only prose asks for them.
2. **Model / backend** (quantisation, context, the 59-task solvable ceiling).
3. **Submission variance** (the reachable-set arithmetic already logged).

Every further prompt arm should be considered unmeasurable at 129 tasks and abandoned.

### Caveat
47/129 cells, so the subset is fastapi-heavy and mostly dead-task loaded; the truly-solvable slice is
21 tasks. Direction is decisive (no-prompt is not worse), magnitude is not. Full run pending.

## EMPTY-PROMPT BASELINE, FULL 129: the prompt is worth +2 to +4 solves and 3 reproducible tasks - I over-called the interim (2026-11-01)

Full run completed: 129/129, rc=0, 4834 s, `agent_ctrl_e4b_noprompt` (system.md = 0 bytes).

### Final numbers (phantoms removed; "gold-valid" = restricted to the 59 truly-solvable)

| arm | recorded | genuine | **gold-valid /59** |
|---|---|---|---|
| ca5 r0 | 12 | 9 | **8 (13.6%)** |
| ca5 r1 | 14 | 11 | **9 (15.3%)** |
| ca5 fa | 14 | 11 | **10 (16.9%)** |
| **NO PROMPT (0 bytes)** | 10 | 7 | **6 (10.2%)** |

Fair pairwise McNemar vs no-prompt: ca5-only 6 / noprompt-only 4 (p=0.754), 6/2 (p=0.289),
6/2 (p=0.289). **No pair reaches significance**, but the direction is consistent in all three.

### RETRACTION of the interim claim
On 47 tasks I wrote "a 0-byte system prompt performs the same as ca5" and "the entire prompt-tuning
history has been tuning a channel whose total contribution is at most ~1-2 tasks ... below the
measurement floor." **That was an over-call on a fastapi-heavy, dead-task-loaded subset.** At 129 the
prompt is worth **+2 to +4 gold-valid solves**, and - more importantly - it is responsible for the
tasks that are solved *reproducibly*:

- **ca5 stable gold-valid core (solved in all 3 runs): 5 tasks** - `fastapi_14301`, `14463`, `14616`,
  `rich_3006`, `rich_3905`.
- **Solved by ca5 in all 3 runs and NEVER by no-prompt: `fastapi_14463`, `fastapi_14616`,
  `rich_3905`** (3 tasks).
- no-prompt (1 run) solves 6 gold-valid, including 3 that ca5 only gets flakily (`fastapi_9753`,
  `rich_2725`, `rich_3454`/`rich_4077`).

So the prompt's contribution is not "more solves"; it is **stabilising a specific 3-task core**.
Remove it and the stable-valid inventory drops from 5 to ~2.

### What this does to the strategy
- The prompt is **not worthless**, but its entire measured value is ~3 tasks out of 129 (2.3%), i.e.
  ~1.3 tasks on the 58-task board - at the edge of the +-2 measurement floor.
- It is therefore **not the lever to 0.10**. Getting to 6/58 needs +1 to +8 *stable* solves depending
  on the LB model; the prompt already gives all it has.
- It **is** worth keeping exactly as-is: it is what makes `14463`, `14616`, `3905` reproducible, and
  reproducible solves are the only ones that count on the board.
- No further prompt arm should be attempted. Structural enforcement (harness preconditions) and the
  backend remain the only untested levers.

### LESSON (added)
**Do not call a null on a subset that is mostly unscorable.** At 47 cells the subset was 60% dead
fastapi tasks and the arms looked identical; at 129 the prompt's contribution is real, consistent, and
concentrated in 3 named tasks. Interims on partial cohorts should be labelled "direction only" and
never stated as findings.

## CORRECTION: fastapi is our STRONGEST repo, not the dead weight - my "34 dead" framing misled (2026-11-01)

User challenge: "what do you mean fastapi aren't solvable? I know for a fact e4b has solved FastAPI
before - at least half in previous runs were split between rich and fastapi." **The user is right and
my framing was wrong.**

### Per-repo truth table (129 tasks, 4 E4B runs)

| repo | total | gold-valid | dead | genuine union | **stable (all 3 ca5 runs)** | no-prompt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **fastapi** | 67 | **29 (43%)** | 34 | **8** | **4** | 3 |
| rich | 48 | 30 (63%) | **0** | 7 | 2 | 4 |
| requests | 13 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| httpx | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | 129 | 59 | 34 | 15 | 6 | 7 |

- **fastapi genuine solves (union): 8 of 15 = 53%** - the user's "at least half" is exactly right.
- **fastapi stable solves: 4 vs rich's 2.** fastapi is our *stronger* repo on the metric that predicts
  the board.
- The 34 dead tasks are all fastapi, but that is **51% of that repo, not all of it** - 29 fastapi tasks
  are gold-valid and therefore fully winnable. I let a true count imply a false conclusion.
- 49% of the 59 solvable tasks are fastapi (29/59); 51% are rich (30/59). Roughly even, not
  "fastapi is the dead repo, rich is the winnable slice".

### What IS true about rich
Near-miss volume (a run that passes some tests and fails others):

| definition | rich | fastapi | requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| near-miss, any file | **37** | 11 | 1 |
| near-miss, gold file only | 26 (earlier measurement) | - | - |
| **one failing test away** | **14** | 1 | 0 |

So rich holds the *unconverted volume* (14 tasks one test from passing) while fastapi holds our
*conversion*. Both are real; they are different problems:
- **fastapi**: we convert well (4 stable of 29 valid = 14%) but there is little near-miss material.
- **rich**: we convert badly (2 stable of 30 valid = 7%) with 14 tasks one test away.

### Consequence
Do not de-prioritise fastapi. The correct statement is:
- 34 fastapi tasks are unwinnable **for everyone** (wheelhouse defect), leaving 33 live fastapi tasks,
  29 of them gold-valid - and we already solve 4 stably there.
- rich is where the marginal conversions are, because 14 tasks are one assertion from passing.

### LESSON (added)
**A true count can carry a false implication.** "34 dead, all fastapi" is arithmetically correct and
led me - and would lead a reader - to treat fastapi as dead weight, when fastapi supplies 53% of our
genuine solves and 67% of our stable ones. Always report the per-repo *live* denominator beside the
dead count.

## SUBMISSION HISTORY DECODED: the LB is a 1-task ladder, grader sigma = 1, and RESUBMISSION CANNOT REACH 0.10 (2026-11-01)

The user supplied the full submissions page. Decoding every displayed score through
`floor(k/58*100)/100`:

| displayed | k/58 | submission |
|---|---|---|
| **0.20** | **12** | ca5: pre-edit anchor-grep, no sub-agents, v10 config (4d ago) |
| **0.18** | **11** | **same pack, resubmitted, IDENTICAL BYTES** (1d ago) |
| 0.17 | 10 | Gemma Sibling-Conform 31b A3 hard v11 (7d) |
| 0.15 | 9 | A23 arm v3 (6d) |
| 0.13 | 8 | A25 router blind: classify-dispatch, 2 sub-agents (5d) |
| **0.03** | **2** | E4B ca5 anchor-grep (small-model candidate, 3d) |

The ladder is **exact and gap-free**: every one of these scores maps to a single integer k out of
58, and each adjacent step is one task. This is independent confirmation of the N=58 truncation.

### MEASURED grader variance: 1 task, on a fixed artifact
`0.20` -> `0.18` on **byte-identical** bytes is **12/58 -> 11/58**. That is the direct measurement
of grader stochasticity on one fixed artifact that this project has been trying to obtain:
**sigma_eff = 1 task = 0.017 displayed.**

### RETRACTION: resubmission cannot get E4B to 0.10
I recommended twice ("3-5 identical resubmits -> 0.10-0.12", and "the highest-EV action") using a
**binomial sigma of 2.07**. The measured sigma is **1**. Recomputing E[max of n] with mean 2/58,
sigma 1:

| n draws | E[max] | displayed |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.56/58 | 0.04 |
| 3 | 2.85/58 | 0.04 |
| 5 | 3.16/58 | 0.05 |
| 10 | 3.54/58 | **0.06** |

**Resubmission caps E4B at ~0.05-0.06.** Reaching 0.10 needs **6/58, which is 4 sigma above the
mean of 2** - not a variance play. The plan was wrong and the variance route is closed.

### The board also ranks the arms, and it is monotone in complexity
A3 hard **10** -> A23 **9** -> A25 router with 2 sub-agents **8**, against ca5 **12**.
**Every mechanism added on top of the simple bundle cost tasks, and the multi-agent router cost 4**
- a regression far larger than the +-2 local noise floor. This is the board agreeing with two local
findings from today: the prompt adds only ~3 tasks, and added rules are executed in degenerate form
or not at all.

### What is now established
1. To move E4B from 0.03 to 0.10 requires **+4 real, stable solves** on the 58 (2 -> 6). No amount
   of resubmission, and no prompt variant we can measure, delivers that.
2. The main track's 0.20 was a favourable draw: two draws average **11.5/58 = 0.198**. Resubmitting
   is worth E[max of 3] = **0.21**, i.e. +1 task - marginal but positive, and auto-selection already
   takes best-of-2.
3. The only remaining route to +4 stable E4B solves is a mechanism that makes a *specific named
   task* resolve reproducibly. The 14 rich tasks one assertion from passing and the 4 stable-valid
   fastapi solves are the entire inventory of candidates.

### LESSON (added)
**Do not recommend a variance strategy without a measured variance.** I used a binomial sigma
(2.07) when the project already suspected sigma_eff ~1, and the recommendation inverted: resubmission
goes from "the highest-EV action" to "capped at 0.06". A single byte-identical resubmission would
have measured this weeks ago.

## OUTSIDE REVIEW LANDED: three blocking errors in my own headline numbers (2026-11-01)

Two external models (claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6-sol) ran `AUDIT_PROMPT_OUTSIDE_REVIEW.md`; a merger
reconciled them against raw artifacts. Report: `kb/audits/outside-review/outside-review-final.md`.
**I re-verified the blocking items myself. All confirmed. They invalidate numbers I have been
quoting all day.**

### M6 (BLOCKING, worst): the decode sweep scored baseline and arms with DIFFERENT engines
Verified directly from `kb/audits/2026-10-15-decode-commitment-sweep.jsonl`, field `scorer_engine`:

| arm | engine | rows |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | **rp-4** | 11 |
| temp_00, temp_01, freq_02, freq_04, pres_02, pres_04, reserve_tail | **rp-5** | 11 each |

**The baseline was scored by a different engine than every arm.** The arm-vs-baseline comparison is
therefore invalid, and so is my "4 WINs are noise" verdict - it compared across scorers. The report
header even says rp-5 while its title says rp-4. My conclusion ("greedy hurts", "the holdout split
works") rested on this table and must be treated as unestablished.

### M2 (BLOCKING): "34 dead because the OFFICIAL image cannot collect" is wrong
Verified: official image **28**, local rig **32**, both 26, **union 34**. I reported the union while
the heading claimed the official image. The log's own table showed 28 and 32 directly beneath that
heading. Local-only six: `fastapi_11355, 14099, 14356, 14455, 14962, 15745` - of which `14356` and
`15745` never produced an official log at all (they died on context overflow / 8-min timeout, tests
never ran). **Defensible grader-dead count = 28, not 34.**

### M1 / M11 / M12 (BLOCKING): the gold inventory undercounts, and three tasks are misclassified
Verified against the official grader's own records:

| task | my classification | official grader |
|---|---|---|
| `fastapi_14786` | "gold-invalid", excluded from stable set | **resolved=True, 9 passed in 0.45s** |
| `rich_3894` | gold-invalid | **resolved=True, 42 passed 4 skipped** |
| `fastapi_14077` | "a genuine solve but a DEAD task" | **resolved=True, 3 passed in 0.37s** |

Two mechanisms the review identified for the undercount, both mine:
1. **Node-mode cross-product.** `replay_verify2.py` built `file::fn` nodes as a cross product across
   test files, so **0 of the 24 multi-file fastapi tasks** were ever recorded gold-valid; all 29 came
   from the 43 single-file tasks.
2. **Skips counted as failure.** My files-mode replay added `skipped` to the failure count, while the
   harness runs whole files and only rejects failures/errors (or a *required* node that is skipped).
   **13 rich tasks fail on skips alone**, and in node mode 8 of them pass their required nodes.

So **"59 truly solvable" is a LOWER BOUND produced by an over-strict replay, not a ceiling.** The
benchmark is larger than I said, and `stable-and-gold-valid` is **>= 6, not 5**.

### M3 (BLOCKING): my "noise = +-2 tasks" is contradicted by my own data
The review points at `m1_full129/ca5` vs `ca5_v2`: identical config, differing only in output path,
recording **15 vs 10** - discordant **5/0**, agreement 124/129, McNemar **p = 0.0625**. **I measured
this exact comparison earlier today and logged "ca5 vs ca5_v2: 124/129 (0.96)"** - then went on to
state +-2 noise from the capped pair. Two identical pairs gave spreads of 5 and 2; +-2 was one
observed difference, not a variance estimate.

### M5 (material): the prompt claim is smaller than stated
With `ca5_v2` added to the prompt-arm set, always-solved across all **5** prompt runs = **2**
(`fastapi_14463`, `rich_3905`) - `fastapi_14616` is missed by `ca5_v2`. And `rich_2725` is solved by
**no** prompt run (0/5); it is the only no-prompt-unique solve, not "a task ca5 gets flakily" as I
wrote. No-prompt arm is still n=1, so "never" means "not in one draw".

### M9 (material, merger-only finding - neither reviewer raised it)
My binomial best-of-N model assumed **drawing a new 58-task set**. The hidden 58 are **fixed**.
Resubmission redraws only the agent's sampling on the same 58. So the p=0.163 "ordinary noise"
statement about task-set sampling is correct, but the corollary I drew from it (resubmit -> 0.10) was
already retracted on 2026-11-01 for a different reason (measured sigma=1). Two independent reasons the

The reviewers claimed the `rich_3772` exclusion and the sweep's bar-design flaw were "not recorded
anywhere a reader would find it". **Both are recorded** - L15723-15726 for the deviation, L15768-15771
for "a pre-registered bar can fire without power". The genuine defect is narrower: the generated

On the grader, `fastapi_14978` and `fastapi_15745` died at "Agent exceeded session timeout (8.0 min)",

### M21 (material): `out_e4b_v3` is a COPY, not a replicate
`task_results.all.jsonl` matches `out_e4b` on all 129 rows; per-task durations identical (median
188.84 s both); eval logs carry identical stream timestamps; both `agent_ca5` bundles byte-identical.
**So Kaggle-side run-to-run variance on the full 129 with this bundle is n = 1.** I had been treating

**Not established** (must not be quoted): the 59/129 ceiling; the 34-dead figure; +-2 noise; the
decode sweep's 4-null verdict and its "greedy hurts / holdout works" conclusions; 5 stable gold-valid;

### LESSON (added)

## CORRECTION: skills CAN ship executable scripts. L3723 ("skills can't ship runtime .py") is WRONG (2026-11-01)

**Official competition page (Evaluation section, pasted by user 2026-11-01):** the `submission.zip` layout lists
`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `scripts/` ("Python or bash scripts executed in a sandbox") and `resources/`. The
"Tool, Prompt, and Skill Rules" say that scripts executed via `run_skill_script` "run securely inside the
competition's persistent Docker container, sharing filesystem access with run_command and debiting execution time
against your central budget". `HARNESS_README.md:92-94,114,144` agrees: `.py` is allowed as "ADK skill scripts".

**Harness source agrees:**
- `agent_runner.py:609-627` passes an `AdkSandboxCodeExecutor` to `compile_submission`.
- That executor writes the script into `/workspace` and runs it with `python3` (`adk_eval_core/sandbox/base.py:164-220`).
- ADK 1.36.1's `RunSkillScriptTool` executes files from the skill's `scripts/` directory.

**Local compile probe (rig image `gemma-parity-rig`, real `adk_submission` 0.2.13):** an `agent.yaml` with
`skills: [skills/check-patch]` compiles to an LlmAgent with a SkillToolset. The model sees `list_skills`,
`load_skill`, `load_skill_resource` and `run_skill_script`. Gotcha: SKILL.md must start with `---` with no UTF-8
BOM. PowerShell's `-Encoding utf8` writes a BOM and fails compile with "SKILL.md must start with YAML frontmatter".

**What L3723 got right:** the harness never `import`s competitor Python. **What it got wrong:** concluding that
nothing we ship can execute. Skill scripts execute in the task sandbox through `run_skill_script`.
**Consequence:** an in-sandbox verification script (compile the changed files, run the existing tests for the
edited module, report pass/fail in one call) is a legal, shippable artifact. That reopens the structural fix for
the "submits without testing" failure: 46 of 52 E4B misses on its 17 reachable tasks were wrong patches submitted
untested (outside-review §6 follow-up). Not yet tested end-to-end in a scored-like run.

## SUBMIT-GATE SKILL: gate detects wrong patches; first live arm is NULL (2026-11-01, local E4B, n small)

**Arm A: `submit_patch` removed (`agent_ctrl_e4b_nosub`), rich_3894 + fastapi_14616.** This reproduces the user's
earlier "it still kept submitting". Mechanism, read from tool_calls:
- `get_status` reports `patch_size: 0` until `submit_patch` is called. ca5 step 3 says "if patch_size is still 0
  you have not edited anything", so after a correct edit the model believes it has not submitted.
- With no submit tool, rich_3894 called `get_status` 115x. It is free and resets the nudge counter, so it ran until
  context overflow at 432 s. fastapi_14616 tried `run_command("submit_patch()")` 9x.
- The harness also injects "call submit_patch" in its task prompt (`agent_runner.py:411`), in nudges (`:998`) and in
  every budget-counted tool result once <=10 calls remain (`tools/base.py:47-66`).
- Verdict: removing the tool alone cannot work.

**Arm B: `agent_ctrl_e4b_gated` (built by `local_eval/parity_rig/_build_gated.py`).**
- Structure: SequentialAgent [fixer = ca5 with the 5 submit-role lines changed, no submit_patch, then verifier =
  short prompt + skill `submit-gate` + submit_patch].
- Compiles with the real adk_submission 0.2.13. The verifier gets a SkillToolset; the skill path resolves from the
  submission root.
- Two gate bugs found and fixed:
  - ADK runs skill scripts from a temp copy of the skill (`<sandbox>/tmp/tmpXXXX/scripts/`), not from the repo. The
    workspace has to be located via PYTHONPATH / HOME / `/workspace`.
  - The revert step touched the harness's conftest.py/pytest.ini and used a shared /tmp file.

**Offline gate test** (`_gate_offline.py`: every recorded E4B patch from the 7 129-task runs, plus gold, applied to
the snapshot, then check.py):
- Correct patches: gold 18/18 and every resolved E4B patch -> ACCEPTED. Zero false rejections.
- Wrong patches: 20/45 REJECTED (44%).
  - rich: 16/25 (64%). Existing tests break: test_inspect x7, test_table, test_prompt x6, test_ansi.
  - fastapi: 4/20, syntax errors only. Many fastapi tests cannot collect locally (inline_snapshot/dirty_equals), and
    the test picker selects irrelevant files (`test_multipart_installation.py`).

**Live replicate batch:** 6 flaky rich tasks + 2 stable, 2 reps (`_skilltest.py`, caps 28/8/120, conc 2).
- Result: gated **8/16 = 0.50** vs ungated **29/56 = 0.52** over the 7 existing runs on the same 8 tasks. **NULL.**
- Gate verdicts were correct where the tests have signal (R on every wrong 3894/3518/3882 first attempt).
- **Retry conversion: 0/5.** After a REJECTED, the verifier's re-edits never produced the right fix. In rich_3067 r0
  the verifier reverted the fix to the original text and submitted without re-running the gate (rule violation).
- One stable miss: rich_3905 r1. The fixer added new start/stop methods, the existing tests pass, so the gate accepted.
  This is a semantic miss the gate cannot see. n=1, not attributable.
- rich_3454 r0: the fixer stopped after reading tests and the verifier never ran. Scored via the fallback working-tree
  diff (WIN).

**Read:** detection works; repair-by-feedback does not at E4B. Next arm to test is **rejection sampling**: on
REJECTED, reset to baseline and let the FIXER make a fresh attempt (LoopAgent [fixer, verifier], max 3). Flaky tasks
are 29-43% per attempt, so best-of-3 with a filter that catches 75-100% of the wrong ones should convert. Each
attempt on these tasks costs ~3-10 calls / 40-120 s.

## THE USER WAS RIGHT: sigma is ~2, not 1, and the step size is symmetric — harvesting reaches 0.24 (2026-11-02)

User: *"if it can drop by .02 it could rise by .02."* Correct, and it exposes two errors of mine.

### Error 1: I quoted an unachievable score
I wrote "E[max of 3] = 12.3/58 -> **0.21**". **0.21 does not exist.** `floor(k/58*100)/100` jumps
**0.20 (k=12) -> 0.22 (k=13)**. I was treating an expected value as if it were a displayable score.

### Error 2: sigma = 1 was inferred from ONE pair
`0.20 -> 0.18` on identical bytes is **one** observation of one task of churn. I then used sigma=1 to
conclude resubmission was near-worthless. The leaderboard says otherwise.

### Observed leaderboard (pulled via CLI, 2026-11-02)
| rank | team | score | k/58 | entries |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Yurnero | 0.29 | **17** | **18** |
| 2-5 | Yike Xu, MUHAMMED IDRIS, SAVE, chizhu | 0.24 | **14** | - |
| us | - | 0.20 | 12 | ~10 |

A **cluster of four teams at 14/58** suggests 14 is the "good artifact" centre, and #1's 17 is a draw
above it. What sigma makes 17 reachable in 18 draws from a centre of 14?

| sigma | P(>=17) per draw | P(>=17) over 18 draws |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 0.006 | 0.106 |
| 1.5 | 0.048 | 0.586 |
| **2.0** | **0.106** | **0.866** |
| 2.5 | 0.159 | 0.955 |

**sigma = 1 makes the leaderboard a 10% event; sigma ~ 2 makes it an 87% event.** The board therefore
favours **sigma ~ 2**, which is exactly what the outside review's M3 said independently
("5-8 discordant tasks of 129 -> 2-4 of 58"). My sigma=1 from a single pair was an underestimate, and
the conclusion I built on it - "resubmission is worth at most +1 task" - is retracted.

### What an extra draw is actually worth (centre 11.5, sigma 2)
| outcome | per draw | over 7 draws (a week of travel) |
|---|---|---|
| >= 0.22 (k=13) | 0.309 | **0.92** |
| >= 0.24 (k=14) | 0.159 | **0.70** |
| >= 0.25 (k=15) | 0.067 | - |

**Harvesting daily during travel is expected to reach 0.22 and has a 70% chance of reaching 0.24** -
which is the #2-#5 cluster. That is a materially better outcome than I told the user, and it makes the
mobile-submit notebook (`MOBILE_SUBMIT.md`) the highest-value artifact built today rather than a
convenience.

### Also corrects a stale number
The log's "gap to #1 = 3 tasks" is out of date. #1 is 17/58; we are 12/58. **Gap = 5 tasks**, and the
gap to the #2 cluster is 2.

### Caveats
- sigma ~ 2 is INFERRED from leaderboard structure, not measured. The centre 11.5 rests on 2 draws.
- Both estimates are soft; the direction is not.
- The E4B conclusion is unaffected: there the centre is 2/58, so even sigma=2 gives
  P(>=6/58) = P(Z >= (5.5-2)/2 = 1.75) = 4% per draw, ~24% over 7 draws. Worth harvesting, but it is
  not a route to 0.10; that still needs real solves.

### LESSON (added)
**Do not estimate variance from a single pair, and do not quote an expected value as a score.** One
observation set sigma=1 and drove a wrong recommendation twice; the leaderboard, which was public the
whole time, implies sigma~2 in one line of arithmetic. Check the population before trusting a sample of
two.

## CALIBRATED AGAINST THE #1 COMPETITOR: the 129-rate maps 1:1 to the LB, and our gap is 3.9x capability (2026-11-02)

Yurnero (1st, 0.29) posted: *"I ran all 129 tasks this weekend on the Kaggle side ... I was doing much
better on the 129 than I thought because I assumed I was only landing Rich tasks. But **landing about
30%ish across the whole board**."*

That is the independent (129-rate -> LB) calibration point this project never had. Testing three models
for how the LB relates to the 129:

| model | prediction from a 30% 129-rate | observed | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| **random subset of the 129 (dead tasks included)** | **17.4/58 = 0.29** | **17/58 = 0.29** | **0.4 tasks** |
| filtered to the 59 truly-solvable | 38.0/58 = 0.65 | 17/58 | **21.0 tasks** |
| filtered to the 95 live | 23.6/58 = 0.41 | 17/58 | **6.6 tasks** |

**Only the random-subset model reproduces the leader's score.** The filtered models - including the one
built on my own "59 solvable" inventory - over-predict by 21 and 6.6 tasks.

Consequence: **the 129-task rate is a direct estimator of the LB score**, `expected = 129-rate x 58`.
That is the single most useful measurement relationship in the project, and it means every local and
Kaggle 129-run we have is directly comparable to the board.

### The real gap
| | 129-rate | predicted LB | observed LB |
|---|---|---|---|
| **leader (#1)** | **39/129 = 30.2%** | 17.5/58 = 0.31 | **17/58 = 0.29** |
| us, Kaggle side (n=1) | **10/129 = 7.8%** | 4.5/58 = 0.06 | **2/58 = 0.03** |
| us, local ca5 | 11/129 = 8.5% | 4.9/58 = 0.08 | - |

- **The gap to #1 is 3.9x in solve rate**, not a measurement artifact, not a variance opportunity and
  not a prompt-wording problem.
- Our 0.03 is **2.5 tasks below** the 4.5/58 our own Kaggle run predicts - a low draw, consistent with
  sigma~2, and it will drift toward 0.06 with harvesting.
- **To reach the 0.24 cluster we need ~31/129. To match 0.29 we need ~39/129.** We are at 10.

### Independent corroboration from the thread
- **Nir Aberman (171st), 163 runs:** *"the gold file is opened by call 2-3 in ~84% of runs, but the
  first edit lands at ~106 s in solved runs vs ~183 s in failed ones ... **Prompt rules to edit earlier
  were mostly ignored.**"* That is an outside team independently reproducing our compliance finding
  (we measured 0/7 repo-wide execution of a definition rule).
- **Yurnero:** *"Gold patches are not working for all public tasks, but all private gold patches are
  correct, since hosts have properly verified them."* Confirms the public-task breakage is real and
  confined to the public set.
- **Nir asks the key question:** whether Yurnero's jump past 0.24 came from *"config/tooling rather
  than prompt wording"*. The leader's own framing points the same way our data does.

### What this closes and what it opens
**Closes:** the theory that the board is filtered and our practice rate under-predicts. It does not
under-predict; it maps 1:1. Our 0.03 is our 7.8% with a bad draw, nothing more.
**Closes:** resubmission as a strategy. With the 1:1 map, harvesting moves 2/58 toward 4.5/58 = 0.06.
It cannot approach 0.24 without the solve rate moving first.
**Opens:** the only question that matters is how to get from 10/129 to 31/129. Prompt wording is
excluded by three independent lines of evidence (our empty-prompt baseline, our 0/7 compliance
measurement, and Nir's 163-run observation). Config and tooling are not excluded, and the leader's
attribution points there.

### LESSON (added)
**Calibrate against a competitor's published rate before theorising about the leaderboard.** One
sentence from the #1 team resolved in a minute what this project argued about for two weeks - and
falsified the filtered-board model that all of my inventory arithmetic was built on. The public
discussion thread was available the whole time.

### FRESH-RETRY ARMS (LoopAgent [fixer, verifier], max 3; gate undoes rejected attempts, restores best on the last) — NULL on total (2026-11-01)

Builder: `local_eval/parity_rig/_build_retry.py`.
- `retry` = fixer sees the full history, including the gate failure.
- `retry2` = fixer `include_contents: none`, with the task re-injected via `{problem_description}` and only a RETRY
  line. A truly fresh attempt.
Same 8 rich tasks, 3 reps each, caps 28/8/120. Ungated reference = 7 existing ca5 129-task runs on the same tasks.

| arm | wins | rate |
|---|---|---|
| ungated (7 runs) | 29/56 | 0.52 |
| gated (verifier repairs) | 8/16 | 0.50 |
| retry (history) | 13/24 | 0.54 |
| retry2 (fresh) | 13/24 | 0.54 |

**Per task** (all 3 gated arms pooled vs ungated):
- rich_3067: 7/8 vs 3/7. Two wins came after an R -> retry -> A, so the retry mechanism converted here.
- rich_3894: **1/8 vs 2/7**. The gate rejects every wrong attempt (R,R,R in 6/8 runs). E4B's retries stay in the
  same wrong family (variants of `__qualname__` / `__name__` fallbacks), and the right fix never appears.
- rich_3518 2/8 vs 2/7; rich_3882 1/8 vs 1/7; rich_4077 1/8 vs 1/7.
  - Retried attempts there were *accepted* by the gate but still wrong: existing tests do not cover the new contract.
- Stable tasks unchanged (3006 8/8, 3454 8/8, 3905 7/8).

**Mechanism verdict.** The gate detects wrong patches (offline: 0 false rejections, 64% of wrong rich patches
rejected). Retry converts only when E4B's attempt distribution actually contains the right fix (3067). It cannot
manufacture a fix E4B does not produce (3894), and cannot see wrong fixes the existing tests do not cover
(3518/3882/4077). Retries also cost wall time: 8-task batches took 344-547 s vs ~400 s for ungated r0. **No free
gate is justified on this evidence.** Total effect is +0.02 on n=24 per arm, inside noise.

**Cheapest remaining levers on this axis:**
- (a) Higher temperature on retry attempts, to diversify the attempt family.
- (b) An issue-derived repro check (fail on base, pass on patch) to cover the false-ACCEPT cases.
- Otherwise the binding constraint is E4B's attempt quality, which points to the capability lever (LoRA from
  31B trajectories).

### E4B good_test_rate (Konwinski-style F2P repro tests): 3/17 = 18% per single sample (2026-11-01, local)

Setup:
- Bundle `agent_ctrl_e4b_testwriter` (`_build_testwriter.py`): one LlmAgent. It locates the code, calls the
  `test-context` skill (deterministic: module signatures, plus imports / test names / one example test from the
  matching test file), writes `repro_issue.py` in the Konwinski print format, runs it, fixes it once, submits.
  It never edits source.
- Scorer `_score_repro.py` runs the extracted test (a) on the original snapshot, (b) with the gold patch, and
  (c) for good tests, on every recorded wrong E4B patch.

Results:

| measure | count |
|---|---|
| tasks | 17 (+2 pilot) |
| wrote a test | 19/19 |
| imports the real package | 16/19; 3 mocked the classes themselves, which is useless |
| prints "Issue reproduced" on the original | 7/17 |
| prints "Issue resolved" with gold | 9/17 |
| **GOOD (both)** | **3/17**: rich_3518, fastapi_14616, fastapi_14786 |
| wrong patches caught by the GOOD tests | **6/6** |

- The existing-test gate caught 3/4 on rich_3518 and **0/2** on fastapi_14616. A good repro test is strictly more
  discriminative there.
- **Hazard:** 4/7 base-reproducing tests ALSO reproduce on gold (fastapi_14873, fastapi_9425, rich_3894, rich_3518
  pilot). Used as a hard gate, a test like that rejects a CORRECT fix. Runtime cannot tell good from bad tests
  (gold is unknown). Konwinski handled this with 5-10 tests and an "any test flips" rule on a 32B model.
- **Budget:** `run_skill_script` DOES count toward max_tool_calls (traces: read+edit+skill = 3 calls). One test
  costs ~7-10 calls, so the 28-call cap fits about 1 test + 1 fix.
- The earlier budget-raise null (L13180, plain agent; L10362) does not cover a structured pipeline. A pipeline
  needs room it will actually use. The total scoring wall is a constraint: v6w took 31B ~7.8h for 129 tasks; Kaggle
  E4B ran 129 tasks in ~75 min.

**Verdict:**
- At 1 sample, the repro-gate is not viable. P(good test) = 0.18, while P(test that would falsely reject a correct
  fix) is about 0.24.
- Viable only if test quality rises: anti-mock enforcement, a scaffold generated by the script, and validation
  feedback. Test sample count also has to rise, which needs a budget raise in eval_config.
- Next measurable step: raise good_test_rate with script-enforced structure, then re-measure on the same 17 tasks.

  the task survives only as a summary, and re-reads rise from 4% to 13%).

  - 64/67 solves used <=15 calls.
- Side effect: below 20 max_tool_calls, the harness stops appending "call submit_patch soon" (tools/base.py:53).

(B9AEAA9A53CE). Run caps 15/8/120, concurrency 3 (same as m1_capped), full 129, same rig/llama-server.

7, 9, 11, 11, 12 (mean 10.0).
- WIN: genuine >= 13, which is above every reference run.
- NULL: 7-12.
- LOSS: <= 6.
- Also report: solves lost among the 3 reference solves that used >15 calls, new solves, and the per-run
  tool-call distribution.

**Known fidelity gap (recorded, not fixed by this arm).** The local rig and our E4B Kaggle kernels run with NO
events_compaction_config. The scorer uses EventsCompactionConfig (interval 15, token_threshold 14,336, retention 5,
per comp_official/HARNESS_README.md:571-574). Next arm: a compaction-faithful driver.

### RESULT — E4B CAP-15, full 129 local (`m1_skilltest/cap15_r0`): 9 genuine -> NULL (pre-registered band 7-12)
