## PRE-REGISTERED: COMPACTION-FAITHFUL E4B runs, 28 vs 15 calls, full 129 local (2026-11-01)

**Fidelity finding (MEASURED).**
- Every E4B number in this project ran with NO context compaction: the local rig, plus both Kaggle E4B kernels.
  `swegemma eval` passes events_compaction_config=None (cli.py:245-266; agent_runner.py:694); the E4B kernel never
  sets it.
- The scorer uses EventsCompactionConfig(interval 15, overlap 2, token_threshold 14,336, retention 5)
  (comp_official/HARNESS_README.md:571-574; official getting-started notebook).
- In capped r0, **70/129 runs crossed 14,336 prompt tokens** (max 30,174), so the grader would compact more than
  half of our tasks mid-run.
- Driver `_compact_main.py` injects the scorer's config into the stock CLI. Smoke test on rich_3518: prompt
  tokens went 14,560 -> 6,100 on the next call, so compaction fired.

**Arms (sequential, same rig, conc 3, caps x/8/120):**
- `cmp28` = agent_ctrl_e4b (ca5, 28 calls) + compaction.
- `cmp15` = agent_ctrl_e4b_cap15 + compaction.

**Bars (genuine; noise reference = identical local pairs differed by 2 and 5, so single-run power is low):**
- Q1, does compaction hurt E4B? Reference: no-compaction 28-call local runs 7/9/11/11/12 (mean 10.0).
  - cmp28 <= 6: compaction hurts (a candidate for the board gap).
  - 7-12: no detectable effect.
  - >= 13: helps.
- Q2, does the cap protect under compaction?
  - cmp15 - cmp28 >= +3: the cap helps under compaction, and a 2nd replicate is required before any gate.
  - within +/-2: null.
  - <= -3: the cap hurts.

### RESULT — COMPACTION-FAITHFUL runs (`m1_skilltest/cmp28_r0`, `cmp15_r0`), full 129, local

| run | compaction | max calls | genuine | mean calls | at cap | errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ref ca5 x5 | off | 28 | 12, 7, 9, 11, 11 (mean 10.0) | - | - | - |
| cap15_r0 | off | 15 | 9 | 7.7 | 16 | 4 |
| **cmp28_r0** | **on** | 28 | **12** | 8.9 | 1 | 1 |
| **cmp15_r0** | **on** | 15 | **13** | 8.1 | 19 | 6 |

- **Q1 (does compaction hurt E4B?): NO.** cmp28 = 12 is inside the pre-registered 7-12 "no detectable effect" band,
  at its top. Compaction does not explain the 2/58 board score. If anything, the two compaction-on runs (12, 13)
  sit above the no-compaction mean (10.0). That is n=1 each and not claimed.
- **Q2 (does the 15 cap help under compaction?): NULL.** cmp15 - cmp28 = +1, inside +/-2. cmp15 = 13 is the
  highest single local E4B genuine count recorded, but the pre-registered comparison is vs cmp28.
- **New solves never seen in the 7 prior ca5 runs:** fastapi_15589 and rich_3506 (cmp28); rich_3944 (cmp15);
  rich_2725 (cmp15; previously only the no-prompt run). Compaction changes trajectories enough to reach tasks the
  uncompacted runs never solved. The E4B reachable union grows from 17 to 21.
- Not done (by the pre-registered rule): a 2nd replicate. It is warranted only to test the incidental "compaction-on
  runs score higher" pattern, not as a gate for cap-15.

## MEASUREMENT REPAIR: provenance-aware failure classes, the 14 src/ tasks, and why the board never lost them (2026-11-02)

This entry records a measurement repair plus two retractions. Net effect on the E4B inventory: **genuine 9 -> 13**.
No new model runs, no GPU, no submission quota - every result below comes from re-verifying patches we had already
produced.

### 1. The naive failure classifier was wrong 12 times, all in fastapi

`local_eval/classify_test_failures.py` mines the `results/test_outputs/*.log` of a finished 129-run and separates
sandbox failures from agent failures by text pattern. On `out_e4b` (126 test_outputs) it reported:

| class | n | rule |
|---|---|---|
| REAL | 64 | assertion / FAILED |
| ENV | 44 | collection error, NameError, ModuleNotFoundError, ... |
| UNKNOWN | 17 | no signal |
| MIXED | 1 | both |

**That ENV count is inflated.** `local_eval/provenance_verdicts.py` adds the missing check - is the file named in the
traceback actually one the agent patched? Corrected:

| verdict | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| REAL | 54 | assertion failed |
| **ENV** | **36** | test never ran; agent did not touch the erroring file -> **unverifiable** |
| **AGENT** | **17** | the agent's own edit appears in the traceback |
| UNKNOWN | 19 | no signal |

The clean example is `fastapi_11194`. The collection error was
`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:999: NameError: name 'FastAPIError' is not defined`, and line 999 is the agent's own
line - it wrote `raise FastAPIError(..., status_code=422)` with no import. Pattern-matching `NameError` called that
an environment failure; provenance calls it an agent bug. **A symptom class is not a cause class.**

ENV by repo: fastapi 34, httpx 1, rich 1, requests 0. Half of fastapi was unmeasurable.

### 2. The 14 src/ tasks: both models stuck at 1/13

14 of 129 tasks have **every gold file under `src/`** - exactly requests (13) + httpx (1).

| cohort | n | solved | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| root-level (fastapi, rich) | 115 | 35 | **30.4%** |
| src-layout (requests, httpx) | 14 | 1 | **7%** |

31B is 3.5x better than E4B overall (35/129 vs 10/129), yet per repo it is `requests 1/13` and E4B is also
`requests 1/13` (L13942, L14237). A 3.5x capability gap cannot vanish on one repo - so the cause is structural.
The single solve is `requests_6644`, which this log already excludes as degenerate, so genuinely **0/14**.

The agent is not at fault: `local_eval/src_layout_check.py` shows the agent patched the correct `src/requests/*.py`
path on **13 of 14** tasks (the 14th edited `setup.py`).

### 3. Root cause: the subprocess backend skips the editable install

`harness_src/x/swegemma/harness/container_setup.py:506`:

```python
def install_editable_package(docker, container_id):
    if type(docker).__name__ in {'SubprocessManager', 'SubprocessSandbox'}:
        return
    docker.exec(container_id,
        'pip install --no-index --find-links=/wheels --no-build-isolation --no-deps -e /workspace 2>/dev/null || true')
```

| backend | editable install | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **docker** (grader default, HARNESS_README:247) | runs | src/ tasks graded correctly |
| **subprocess** (Kaggle notebooks) | **skipped entirely** | `import requests` resolves to site-packages; every `src/` edit is invisible to tests |

Root-level packages (`fastapi/`, `rich/`) import straight from cwd, which is why only src-layout repos were affected.
Our local `gemma-parity-rig` is docker but had **no `/wheels` and no build backends** (`pdm-backend`, `poetry-core`,
`hatchling`, `flit-core`, `editables`, `wheel` all absent), so the install failed there too and `|| true` hid it.
Both of our instruments were blind on the same 14 tasks; the grader was not.

### 4. Re-verification in a correct sandbox

Built `local_eval/Dockerfile.verify` (+ `Dockerfile.fastapi`): python 3.13, pytest, the real build backends, an
actual `/wheels`, and the test packages. `local_eval/reverify_src_layout.py` replays existing patches under
`install` / `path` / `broken` modes, with `+shim` and `-noagent` variants.

**src-layout cohort (14 tasks, E4B):**

| outcome | n | tasks |
|---|---|---|
| **new genuine solves** | **4** | `requests_7309, 7315, 7433, 7502` |
| already excluded as degenerate | 1 | `requests_6644` |
| real agent bugs | 2 | `requests_7205` (`continue` outside loop), `requests_7427` (`host_with_port` used before assignment) |
| env-blocked (baseline fails identically) | 4 | `httpx_3672, requests_6757, 7328, 7505` |
| inconclusive | 3 | `requests_6589, 6592, 6629` |

Two of the four conversions (`7433`, `7502`) were previously killed by a **`httpbin` fixture setup error** - test
dependencies, not the patch. `7309`/`7315` had been written off as **phantoms** (rig importing site-packages); in a
correct sandbox they genuinely pass. The phantoms were real solves masked by a broken rig.

**Fastapi cohort (the 5 fastapi solves among the 10 recorded):**

| task | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| `fastapi_14301, 14463, 14077, 14786` | **PASS** | confirmed genuine |
| `fastapi_14851` | env-blocked | fails on 2 lifespan `DeprecationWarning`s **identically with no patch** |

`fastapi_14786` passing again contradicts our earlier "gold-invalid" call and agrees with the outside review (M1)
that the official grader resolves it.

Getting fastapi to collect at all required period-correct pins: anyio `>=4.2,<4.7` (4.x emits a `BlockingPortal`
`DeprecationWarning` that fastapi's `filterwarnings = error` converts into a collection failure) and `-p no:asyncio`
(the plugin's own `PytestDeprecationWarning` does the same on `pytest_configure`). Same class as the original
`fastapi_11194` skew - dependency versions, not patches.

**Rich cohort:** 4/4 recorded solves re-confirmed (`rich_3006, 3454, 3894, 3905`).

**Corrected E4B inventory:** 9 genuine -> **13** (12 verified in-sandbox, `fastapi_14851` unverifiable locally).
The baseline cap15 bar "genuine >= 12 = WIN" therefore sits below the true pool rate and should be read against 13.

### 5. RETRACTED: the conftest shim as a board lever

A root `conftest.py` doing `sys.path.insert(0, "src")` was proved to rescue src-layout tasks locally (2x2:
`broken` FAIL, `broken+shim` PASS, `install` PASS) and to **not** rescue broken patches (`7205` NO_JUNIT,
`7427` FAIL, `7328` FAIL). That part stands and is useful for local evaluation only.

**It cannot ship.** `verification.py:62` + `strip_protected_files_from_patch` deletes from the agent patch, before
grading, every diff section touching: `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `tox.ini`, `setup.cfg`,
`.pytest.ini`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py`, `_swegemma_stubs.py`, `*.pth`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`,
and anything under `tests/`. The harness additionally writes its own `/workspace/conftest.py`
(`container_setup.py:868`, "Hermetic test discovery hook for SWE-gemma"). There is **no agent-side way to influence
import resolution.**

Two further retractions follow:

- **"The shim is worth 0.20 -> 0.24 on the board."** Wrong. The grader is docker, so it installs editable properly
  and **already credits src-layout work**. There was never board upside.
- **"The 4.3-task board anomaly is the 4 src-layout tasks."** Wrong direction. Those tasks were always *in* the
  board and *missing* from our measurement, not the reverse. Predicted board from the corrected rate is
  13 x 58/129 = 5.85/58; observed 2/58. The ~3.9-task deficit is **not** src-layout and remains open
  (`P(K<=10) = 0.026` under a uniform-subset assumption points back at "the public 58 is harder than random").

### 6. What this buys and what it does not

- **Buys:** a verifier that agrees with the grader's backend instead of silently skipping the install. Every
  notebook-measured arm had the same 14-task blind spot, so arm comparisons were ranking configs on a 115-task
  instrument. That is now fixable locally.
- **Does not buy:** board points. The src/ cohort is a measurement defect, not a scoring one.
- **Still open:** the fastapi half of the benchmark needs the published wheels (`/wheels` + pre-installed
  site-packages) before it can be measured faithfully; our image now collects it but only with hand-pinned versions.

Tooling added this session: `local_eval/classify_test_failures.py`, `env_false_negatives.py`,
`provenance_verdicts.py`, `src_layout_check.py`, `reverify_src_layout.py`, `fastapi_deps_probe.py`,
`Dockerfile.verify`, `Dockerfile.fastapi`.

## VERIFY-FIX SKILL BUNDLE BUILT (edit -> verify -> repair-once -> submit) — zero-GPU, STATIC-VALIDATED, gate PENDING on GPU machine (2026-11-02)

Direction chosen (user): work the SKILLS lever from the laptop (no GPU needed to build; the gate run
needs the GPU machine). Rationale set in the prior session: prompt-wording and budget-cap axes are both
measured-null; sub-agents are closed; skills + LoRA are the only live levers. Skills are laptop-friendly.

### THE DESIGN — attacks the measured failure class with the user's cap insight
- Measured failure (outside-review 6): **46 of 52 E4B misses on reachable tasks were WRONG PATCHES
  SUBMITTED UNTESTED.** The fix is structural (verify before submit), not more prose.
- User's cap insight (cap-15 null, L16854/L16944): 64/67 E4B solves used <=15 calls, so localize+edit
  fits in ~13. That frees the back half of the 28-call budget for ONE verify->repair cycle.
- The earlier skill cost problem (testwriter: `run_skill_script` ~7-10 calls because the MODEL drives a
  multi-call probe) is fixed by making verify a **single deterministic call**: the skill script
  py_compiles the edited file AND runs the ONE most-relevant existing test for that module, printing a
  terse `VERIFY: PASS` / `VERIFY: FAIL <first failure line>` / `VERIFY: NO_TEST`. One tool call, not a probe.

### BUNDLE: `local_eval/parity_rig/agent_ctrl_e4b_verify` (builder `_build_verify.py`)
- HELD CONSTANT vs ca5 (`agent_ctrl_e4b`): model (E4B w4a16), sampling (temp 0.2 / thinking 4096), and
  the ENTIRE localization+edit+contract prompt. eval_config cap stays 28 (the back half IS the reserve).
- ADDED: `skills/verify-fix` (SKILL.md + scripts/verify.py) + two prompt sections inserted before
  "Hard rules": VERIFY-BEFORE-SUBMIT (run the skill once after the edit lands, read PASS/FAIL/NO_TEST,
  at most ONE repair, do NOT verify twice) and the reserve split (locate+edit in ~13, verify in the rest;
  skip verify if already in the <=7-call danger zone — COMMIT-BY-REMAINING still wins there).
- verify.py is defensive: SyntaxError -> FAIL fast; no mapped test -> NO_TEST (never a false hard-fail);
  collection error / timeout -> NO_TEST; picks the narrowest existing test (exact test_<stem>.py, then
  prefix, then import-grep fallback). NEVER runs bare pytest (-x -q, single target file, 110s cap).

### VALIDATION DONE ON THIS LAPTOP (no docker/GPU here):
- `_validate_verify_static.py`: SKILL.md has NO BOM + starts with `---` (the L16451 compile-killer),
  agent.yaml model + every !include + skills/<dir> resolve, scripts compile, ca5 core prompt retained,
  VERIFY section present exactly once. -> STATIC OK.
- `_test_verify_logic.py` + isolated parser test: find_test_file exact/prefix/underscore-strip selection
  = 3/3; first_failure_line parsing = 3/3. (import-grep fallback only exercised in the Linux rig.)

### NOT DONE (blocked on this laptop — Docker Desktop not running, no GPU, no snapshots):
- `compile_check.py` (real adk_submission compiler) — needs the `gemma-parity-rig` container.
- The E4B rig gate run — needs llama-server :8081 (GPU) + snapshots.

### PRE-REGISTERED GATE (run on the GPU machine, rule 2): `_skilltest.py verify agent_ctrl_e4b_verify`
on the reachable rich cohort, gold-scored via the rp-4 offline scorer; compare to the ca5 E4B baseline.
- Reference: local ca5 E4B genuine ~10/129 (draws 7-12); the corrected reachable pool is 13.
- WIN: genuine > ca5 baseline on the SAME cohort AND traces show verify firing (VERIFY: lines) and >=1
  repair converting a would-be wrong submit into a resolve.
- NULL: within +/-2 of baseline, or verify fires but never converts (wrong patches that pass the narrow
  existing test anyway — the known Type-B "self-test passes, hidden test fails" hazard).
- LOSS: verify eats budget and drops genuine below baseline (watch mean calls/task; if the reserve
  pushes edits past the budget, that is the cap-15 lesson re-firing).
Also measure: calls spent on the skill (should be ~1-2/task), NO_TEST rate (how often no existing test
maps — those tasks get no verify benefit), and whether compaction interacts (run compaction-faithful too).

## VERIFY-FIX SKILL — FIRST KAGGLE BATCH (6 tasks, E4B): mechanism FIRES, no regression, ONE bug found (2026-11-02)

Kernel `comfyops/e4b-verify-batch` (ca5 E4B + verify-fix skill, edit->verify->repair->submit), 6-task
batch, caps 28/8, tp=1 single-GPU. Result 4/6.

| task | role | resolved | calls | patch | test_rc |
|------|------|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| fastapi_14301 | stable win | T | 5 | 620 | 0 |
| fastapi_14463 | stable win | T | 5 | 873 | 0 |
| rich_3905 | stable win | T | 8 | 521 | 0 |
| rich_3006 | stable win | T | 3 | 558 | 0 |
| rich_4077 | near-miss | F | 10 | 585 | 1 |
| rich_3894 | near-miss | F | 3 | 683 | 1 |

### WHAT PASSED (the real risk — does a verify loop break known wins?): NO REGRESSION.
All 4 stable wins stayed green. Call counts low (3-10). The SINGLE-CALL verify design did NOT repeat the
testwriter's 7-10-call blowup: skill cost ~1 call/task. The bundle is safe to run at scale.

### MECHANISM CONFIRMED: the skill FIRED on all 6 tasks (grep VERIFY:/run_skill_script in logs).
The agent localizes, edits, then calls `run_skill_script verify-fix` exactly as designed, reads the
result, then submits. The structural edit->verify->submit loop executes on the real harness.

### THE BUG (decisive, cheap to fix): the skill received `--` as its path argument, not the file.
Every task's verify output was `VERIFY: FAIL edited file not found: --`. The agent passed
`positional_args: ["rich/repr.py"]` CORRECTLY, but the ADK delivers skill positional args after a `--`
separator, so `sys.argv[1] == "--"`. verify.py read argv[1] directly -> garbage. So verify produced ZERO
real signal on any task; the 4 wins passed DESPITE verify failing (the agent correctly ignored the
nonsense FAIL and submitted — the safe fallback working as intended). The 2 near-misses' `test_rc=1` is
the HARNESS grading, not our skill.

### SECOND FACT ESTABLISHED (from harness source, settles an old open question):
`enable_sandbox_testing` DEFAULTS TRUE (config.py:123; agent_runner.py:588 "Test runners are re-enabled
in sandbox"). pytest/unittest are MASKED only if explicitly set False (agent_runner.py:402 prompt). So
the scoring sandbox DOES allow pytest by default -> a verify skill that runs a targeted test is viable;
it was NOT the blocker. The `--` arg bug was the only blocker.

### FIX APPLIED: verify.py now has `_argpath()` that skips a leading `--`/flag token and takes the first
real path (unit-tested: ['v','--','p']->'p', ['v','p']->'p', ['v','--']->''). The NO_TEST branch now
prints argv so the next run reveals the exact shape if `--` is not the whole story.

### NEXT RUN (pushed): `comfyops/e4b-verify-par` — the 4x-PARALLEL harness + the arg fix, SAME 6 tasks.
This is the user's parallelism lever baked in as the standard dev harness: 4 independent tp=1 E4B servers
(one per L4, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned, ports 8000-8003), tasks round-robin sharded, 4 concurrent
`swegemma eval` subprocesses each pinned to its server URL. Builder `kaggle_pkg/_build_parallel_kernel.py`.
It answers BOTH: (a) do the 2 near-misses CONVERT now that verify returns real PASS/FAIL, and (b) does the
4x harness work + cut wall time ~3-4x. Pre-registered: WIN if >=1 near-miss converts with VERIFY firing
real output AND 0 regressions; NULL if verify now gives real signal but still converts nothing (the
Type-B "wrong patch passes the narrow test" hazard); the parallel harness itself is a keep regardless if
it runs clean (reusable for all future dev batches). Serve cell uses CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set before each
VllmServer.start() (build_env does os.environ.copy(), so the device sticks per server).

## VERIFY-FIX NULL INVESTIGATION — the arg fix WORKED; the 2 near-misses are TWO DIFFERENT walls (2026-11-02)

Ran `comfyops/e4b-verify-par` (4x-parallel harness + the `_argpath` fix), same 6 tasks. Result 4/6 again,
but now verify returns REAL PASS/FAIL (the `--` arg bug is gone). Investigated WHY the 2 near-misses
(rich_4077, rich_3894) still failed by reading patches + hidden test_outputs + gold + problem statements.
They are NOT the same null.

### HARNESS-TIMING WIN (bonus): the 4x PARALLEL harness works.
Eval phase 174s for 6 tasks across 4 GPUs (shards 2/2/1/1), "ALL SHARDS DONE in 174s". The waste was the
SEQUENTIAL server BOOT (gpu0 up @295s, gpu1 @+142s, ... ~11 min before eval). FIXED in
`_build_parallel_kernel.py`: servers now boot CONCURRENTLY in threads with a per-server build_env()
override for CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (no shared-env race), so 4 boots overlap to ~300s total. N_GPU is now a
knob (use 1 for <=8-task batches — one boot beats four; 4 for the full 129). CONCURRENT-SESSION CAP is 2
(logged earlier: double-push -> 409), and the weekly unlock is HOURS not SLOTS, so "4 simultaneous 129
kernels" is not possible; the parallelism is WITHIN one kernel (4-GPU shard) across at most 2 kernels.

### NULL #1 — rich_4077: FALSE GREEN. verify is structurally blind to the hidden regression test.
- Agent fix: `def isatty(self): return os.isatty(self.__file.fileno())`.
- Hidden test (injected, NOT in the base-commit test file): builds a `TTYFile` with `isatty()` but NO
  `fileno()`, asserts `file_proxy.isatty()` is True. Agent fix raises
  `AttributeError: 'TTYFile' object has no attribute 'fileno'`. Gold = `return self.__file.isatty()`.
- verify ran `tests/test_file_proxy.py` AT THE BASE COMMIT and got PASS — because the `test_isatty`
  regression test is part of the HIDDEN test_patch, applied only at grading. So verify literally cannot
  see the test it is graded on. Problem statement is 2 words ("proxy isatty") -> a behaviour-verify built
  from the issue ALSO can't recover the fileno-less-TTYFile scenario. This null is UNADDRESSABLE by any
  verifier: the signal is not present at agent time.

### NULL #2 — rich_3894: TRUE FAIL verify caught, but the model OVER-EDITED and regressed a PASS_TO_PASS.
- Gold: KEEP `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)`, ADD a guard only for when qualname
  is NOT a str (the "unusual __qualname__" the issue names).
- Agent: REPLACED the line with `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", getattr(obj,"__name__",name))` -> changed
  the normal path from bare `name` to dotted `__qualname__`, so `def method` became `def Foo.method` and
  BROKE the previously-passing `test_render` (the hidden test_output `++` markers show the exact extra
  `Foo.`). This is a PASS_TO_PASS REGRESSION from over-editing.
- Here verify WORKED: it ran `tests/test_inspect.py` (which DOES cover this) and correctly said FAIL. The
  agent then made 4 repair edits, fought `old_string not found` (edit-mechanics), re-verified (still
  FAIL), and submitted a still-wrong patch. So the wall is (a) fix-CONTENT: the model can't produce the
  surgical guard-only gold edit, and (b) edit-MECHANICS: it couldn't land clean repair edits.

### WHAT THE NULLS ESTABLISH (decomposition, not defeat):
1. When the existing test COVERS the behaviour, verify is ACCURATE (caught rich_3894's wrong patch). The
   verify mechanism is sound where signal exists.
2. When the regression test is HIDDEN (rich_4077), verify gives a FALSE GREEN and NO verifier helps —
   the discriminating test does not exist at agent time. This is the real ceiling on the verify lever and
   it is STRUCTURAL, not a design flaw.
3. The residual failure even WITH a correct FAIL signal (rich_3894) is fix-CONTENT + edit-MECHANICS — the
   model knows it failed and still can't emit the surgical gold edit. That is the weights-level wall the
   log has hit repeatedly; a verifier cannot cross it.

### CONSEQUENCE / NEXT (pre-register before spending more GPU):
- The verify skill is a KEEP for the "existing test covers it" subset and a GUARDRAIL against over-edit
  regressions (rich_3894-class: if verify FAILs, do NOT submit a patch that regresses — prefer reverting
  to a smaller diff). That is a measurable, addressable slice.
- Verify CANNOT convert the hidden-regression-test subset (rich_4077-class). Stop expecting it to.
- The highest-value cheap experiment is NOT a stronger verifier. It is: on a verify-FAIL, does a
  "REVERT-AND-MINIMIZE" instruction (shrink the diff toward gold-minimal / restore the regressed line)
  beat "repair"? rich_3894 over-edited; the gold is SMALLER than the agent's patch. Test whether the
  guardrail "verify FAIL -> make the SMALLEST change, do not rewrite the line" recovers the
  PASS_TO_PASS. Cheap: 1 GPU, the ~3 rich tasks whose existing test covers the behaviour.
- The rich_4077-class (hidden-test false green) routes to the LoRA/content lever, not skills.

User point: rich_4077 HAS resolved on E4B before, so it is not intrinsically unsolvable; the loss was a
specific wrong CHOICE. Both near-misses share a shape the null investigation exposed:
- rich_4077: wrote `os.isatty(self.__file.fileno())` when the sibling `fileno()` directly above is
  `return self.__file.fileno()` -> the conform fix is `return self.__file.isatty()` (delegate, not
  reconstruct).

  is SMALLER than the agent's.

### THE ARM: `agent_ctrl_e4b_verify_guard` (prompt-only delta vs agent_ctrl_e4b_verify)
Rewrites ONLY the verify-FAIL repair branch from free-form ("fix the deviation") to a MINIMIZE rule:
  (1) MIRROR THE SIBLING directly above/below — same shape; delegate like the neighbor, don't reconstruct
      via a lower-level API; (2) SMALLEST DIFF — prefer ADD-a-guard/one-delegating-line over REPLACE; if
      you replaced a line that worked, restore it and add the minimal change; (3) one smaller edit, submit.
Same skill (arg-fixed verify.py), same caps 28/8, same model/sampling. Kernel `comfyops/e4b-verify-guard`,
single-GPU, same 6-task batch -> clean A/B vs the plain-verify 4/6.

- WIN: >= 5/6, i.e. convert rich_4077 OR rich_3894 (ideally both) with the 4 stable wins held.
- NULL: 4/6 (no conversion) — the repair wording doesn't move content/mechanics; verify-as-guardrail is
  then only a regression-preventer, not a converter, and the content wall stands (-> LoRA lever).
- LOSS: < 4/6 — the minimize rule regressed a stable win (watch for over-constraining the good tasks).
Also read the traces: on a FAIL, did the agent actually MIRROR the sibling (rich_4077 -> self.__file.isatty())

rich_4077 flipped F->T, all 4 stable wins held. The sibling-mirror + smallest-diff repair rule works on

### MECHANISM CONFIRMED (read the trace, not just the count): it is the GOLD fix, produced on the FIRST edit.
Agent patch = `def isatty(self): return self.__file.isatty()` — IDENTICAL to gold, and it MIRRORS the
sibling `fileno()` (`return self.__file.fileno()`) right above it. Previous run wrote the reconstruct form
`os.isatty(self.__file.fileno())` (455ch, crashed on the fileno-less TTYFile). The guardrail steered the
delegate-not-reconstruct choice UP FRONT (3 calls, no repair cycle needed). So the win is the PROMPT RULE,
not a lucky resample.

verify still returned `VERIFY: PASS` on the base-commit test (the hidden test_isatty is not in it), so the
skill caught nothing here. The sibling-mirror rule is what produced the correct patch. => the ACTIVE LEVER
is the "mirror the adjacent sibling, smallest diff" prompt rule; the verify skill is riding along. This is
cheaper and more general than the skill: it needs no sandbox test, so it applies to the hidden-test-false-
green class (rich_4077) that verify provably cannot help.

### rich_3894 did NOT convert — and that bounds the lever honestly.
Its miss is subtler than delegate-vs-reconstruct: gold ADDS a `if not isinstance(qualname, str)` guard
while KEEPING `qualname = name or getattr(obj,"__qualname__",name)`; the agent replaced the line with a
`__qualname__`-first form (dotted names, regressed PASS_TO_PASS). The sibling-mirror rule did not fix the
content CHOICE of which name attribute to use. So the guardrail converts the "conform to the obvious
adjacent sibling" shape, not arbitrary content errors. That residual is the weights/LoRA lever.

`comfyops/e4b-sibling` (prompt-only, NO skill, sibling-mirror rule as a PRE-EDIT principle): 4/6.

### FINDING 1 (solid): the sibling-mirror PROMPT RULE is the rich_4077 lever; the verify SKILL is not.
Prompt-only reproduced the exact gold fix (`return self.__file.isatty()`, 324ch, 4 calls) with no skill.
=> ATTRIBUTION: ship the prompt rule, the skill is optional. Confirms the earlier read that verify PASS'd
without catching anything; the win was always the prompt.

### FINDING 2 (the fastapi_14463 regression) — CONFOUNDED, do NOT over-read as strategy.
The patch contains a MALFORMED edit: `import copyfrom fastapi import routing` (the model mashed
`import copy` into the existing import line) -> SyntaxError -> pytest collection ERROR (test_rc=2). The
logic change (`additional_response.copy()` -> `copy.deepcopy(...)`) may be fine; the IMPORT insertion
corrupted the file. This is the edit_file-malformation wall (documented repeatedly), NOT evidence that the
Rich rule hurts FastAPI strategically. n=1, cause = mechanics. RETRACT any "sibling rule hurts fastapi"
claim from this run.

### THE REAL STATE OF "make the agent act differently on FastAPI vs Rich" (user's question):
- REFUTED (prior, L10115 + A25 board 0.13): a ROUTING AGENT / classify-then-dispatch. FastAPI is NOT a
  routing problem (7/12 fastapi already edit the exact gold file); its wall is COMMITMENT + CONTENT
  SYNTHESIS, which the prompt channel + 8 LoRA levers have not cracked. A per-repo SUB-AGENT is dead.
- NEWLY POSSIBLE (verified this session): the model SEES the repo name in line 1 of every task prompt
  (`...for repository Textualize/rich` / `fastapi/fastapi`, agent_runner build_agent_prompt). So
  REPO-CONDITIONAL TEXT inside system.md ("if rich: mirror the sibling / smallest diff; if fastapi:
  <contract-synthesis guidance>") is a real, UNTESTED lever distinct from the refuted routing agent.
- WHY it might matter: the sibling-mirror rule is a RICH-SHAPED lever (high-redundancy / plastic-surgery).
  It just converted a rich task. Whether it is NEUTRAL or HARMFUL on fastapi (low-redundancy, no sibling
  to mirror) is the open question — this run did NOT answer it (the one fastapi regression was a malformed
  import, not a strategy mismatch).

### PRE-REGISTERED NEXT (the actual FastAPI-vs-Rich experiment):
Build a BALANCED hard cohort: ~6 hard RICH + ~6 hard FastAPI (not already-solved stable wins). Run:
  arm A = plain ca5 (control)
  arm B = ca5 + GLOBAL sibling-mirror rule
  arm C = ca5 + REPO-CONDITIONAL rule (rich: sibling-mirror; fastapi: no sibling-mirror / contract-first)
Bar: does B beat A on rich WITHOUT losing fastapi? If B loses fastapi and C recovers it, repo-conditional
prompting is justified and becomes the shipping config. If B is neutral on fastapi, ship B globally (simpler)
and the repo-conditional complexity is unnecessary. Use the 4x-parallel harness (concurrent boot) + 1-2
session slots. This finally measures the user's question instead of inferring it from 2 already-solved
fastapi tasks.

### ALSO LOGGED (prompt-layer audit, user question "are we tuning the wrong prompt?"):
The model reads TWO authored layers we DON'T fully control: our system.md (system role) AND the harness
`build_agent_prompt` (user role: problem + budget + `## Instructions:` 0-5 + `## Code Intelligence Tools`
+ workspace tree). The harness block partly CONTRADICTS our system.md (its Instruction 2 "inspect
conventions and test files BEFORE editing" vs our "EDIT EARLY, don't explore"; and it advertises
search_similar_code as semantic search when the log proved it name-keyed). We author ONLY system.md; the
agent.yaml `description:` field is unset (low impact for a flat agent). We cannot edit the harness block,
only out-argue it -> sharp, ADDITIVE, non-conflicting system.md rules land (sibling-mirror did); vague or
harness-contradicting ones get drowned. This is a lens for future prompt edits, not a bug we introduced.

## E4B ca5 VARIANCE HARNESS — 3h, full-129 repeated on 8 servers (2 per L4) — RUNNING (2026-11-02)

Kernel `comfyops/e4b-variance-129`. Purpose: finally MEASURE E4B run-to-run variance instead of inferring
it (we've reasoned from n=1-2 draws all project; the 3-arm churn suggested ~1-task noise but unmeasured).

### DESIGN (user direction: use all 4 L4s, more than 4 instances):
- 8 tp=1 E4B servers = INSTANCES_PER_GPU=2 x 4 L4s. E4B QAT weights ~6.5GB (L13747), 23.7GB L4 fits 2 at
  gpu_memory_utilization~0.42 (~7GB KV each). Concurrent boot (threads, per-server CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
  override, no shared-env race). Ports 8000-8007, 2 pinned per GPU.
- TIME-BOXED: repeat the full 129 (8-way sharded) until 3h - 12min save-reserve. Each pass tagged run_N,
  variance.json rewritten after every pass (kill-safe). At ~35s/task E4B and 8 servers, a full pass is
  ~10-15 min wall -> expect ~10-16 passes in the window (vs the n=1-2 we had).
- Config = ca5 (agent_ctrl_e4b, the banked E4B baseline), caps 28/8, NO compaction (matches prior E4B
  Kaggle numbers for comparability). Best banked config, not a new arm — the point is variance, not a lever.

### OUTPUT: variance.json -> per-pass resolved sets + summary: k_mean / k_sd / k_min / k_max, STABLE core
### (solved every pass), FLAKY set (solved some), never-solved. This gives the real sigma to replace the
### single-pair sigma=1 and the inferred sigma~2 the log has argued over (L16238, L16649).

### WHY IT MATTERS: every arm comparison this session (verify 4/6, guard 5/6, sibling 4/6, 3-arm 4/5/4,
### 12-task 0-2 rich) was single-draw. If sigma is ~1-2 tasks on 129, the small-batch deltas we've been
### reading (e.g. B 5/12 vs A 4/12) may be inside noise. This run calibrates how much to trust them, and
### gives the stable-core / flaky decomposition that tells us which tasks are real targets vs coin-flips.

### Builder: kaggle_pkg/_build_variance_kernel.py. ~3h wall. Read variance.json summary when COMPLETE.

### VARIANCE HARNESS v1 FAILED (8-server boot) -> FIXED in v2 (2026-11-02)

v1: all 8 servers exited `ServerStartupError: code 1` on boot. CAUSE: 2 vLLM instances booting
SIMULTANEOUSLY on the same L4 each profile peak memory as if they OWN the card and each grab util*23.7GB
-> collective over-commit -> OOM at init. util=0.45 was also too high for 2/GPU.

FIX (v2): (1) UTIL lowered to ~0.42 for 2/GPU (20GB/instances / 23.7), 0.85 for 1/GPU. (2) STAGGERED
ROUND boot: boot one instance per GPU (round 1, concurrent), wait healthy, THEN the second instance per
GPU (round 2) — so the 2nd never races the 1st's memory profiler. (3) tolerant assert (>=NG): if round 2
still OOMs on some GPUs, proceed with whatever booted (>=4 servers) so the 3h run still happens.
LESSON: multiple vLLM instances per GPU must be booted SEQUENTIALLY (or with explicit memory caps), never
concurrently — the memory profiler assumes sole ownership. Kernel v2 running.

## PER-NODE VARIANCE KERNEL — what the user actually asked for (2026-11-03)

User intent: 4 complete 129-task passes running AT THE SAME TIME, one per node (GPU), each node looping its
own passes. The first variance kernel (`e4b-variance-129`) did NOT do that: it sharded ONE pass across the
4 servers (4 threads, ~32 tasks each) and ran passes sequentially, so each pass waited on its slowest shard.
I described that correctly but built it against the intent.

New kernel `comfyops/e4b-variance-pernode` (builder `kaggle_pkg/_build_variance_pernode.py`): reuses the
proven 1-server-per-GPU boot; each node loops full-129 passes against its own server (8 concurrent loops
per node), no cross-node barrier. A node starts another pass only if remaining time > 1.15x its longest
complete pass. After each pass the logs/traces/test_outputs dirs are deleted except for each node's first
pass, and every task row (resolved, calls, patch size, duration, rc) is stored in variance.json, so
variance.json alone supports the analysis (the first kernel's output was thousands of files and the CLI
download crawled). Summary adds k_by_node to check for a node effect. 3h eval budget after boot, 10 min
save reserve. Expect roughly 2 passes per node (~8 total) if a pass takes ~60-75 min at conc 8; that
estimate is unmeasured. Old kernel `e4b-variance-129` untouched (its download still in progress).

  live-task runs, consistent with the 35/129 full-pool (which includes dead tasks in the denominator).

User rejects accepting 0.20; notes E4B has room (board top 0.10 = 6/58; we are ~0.08-0.10). Pressure-tested

  search_similar_code/get_code_neighbors/get_code_subgraph are backed by non-existent Google-internal
  /cns/ sstables; they raise TypeError, no graph data ships. Non-functional for everyone. BUT its real
  residual = the definition-vs-reference localization lever (below).
- OPTION 2 (structural verify/budget): mostly exhausted (budget raise null, verify false-PASS, gate null,
  compaction null). The one structural idea the log named for the def-lever — wrap edit_file to refuse a
  reference-site path — is NOT BUILDABLE: tools come from a fixed pre-approved ToolRegistry (context.py);
  the declarative submission selects from it, cannot redefine/wrap edit_file. Harness-enforcement route closed.
- OPTION 3 (accept 0.20 / paper): defensible but rejected by user. E4B room is real and specific.

### DEFINITION-FINDER lever — rebuilt correctly, NOT the prior null:
The prior def-arm (agent_ctrl_e4b_def) was a PROMPT rule (`grep -rn 'def <symbol>'`), ran on its 7-task
cohort, got 2/7, zero conversions — because E4B follows the rule ~25% of the time AND fixed-localization
tasks then failed on content. The log's stated fix was ENFORCEMENT not prose. Tool-wrap enforcement is
impossible (fixed registry), so the viable form is a SKILL that does definition-finding DETERMINISTICALLY:
one `run_skill_script` call greps `def/class <symbol>` across the repo and returns the defining file, so
localization no longer depends on the model remembering-and-grepping-right.

### CEILING MEASURED (kaggle_pkg, gold-shape of the 7 targets): 4 LOC-ONLY, 3 content-hard.
LOC-ONLY (fix is small+mechanical once in the right file -> the skill can convert):
  rich_4077 (def isatty: return self.__file.isatty()), rich_3067 (one URL-regex line),
  rich_3480 (text._spans.copy x2), fastapi_14492 (one string "identifier": "Apache-2.0").
CONTENT-HARD (right file won't be enough): fastapi_14372, 14458, 9555 (dataclasses.replace / isclass guard
  / 13-line cached_property). So the lever's realistic ceiling is ~4 E4B conversions, named, not 7.

### WHY THIS IS WORTH A BUILD (vs everything closed): 4 new E4B solves is large on a 6/58-top board; the
4 tasks fail for ONE measured reason (grep hits a reference, never opens the definition); it is a SKILL
(deterministic, removes the 25%-compliance gap), not a prompt (nulled) / LoRA (closed) / graph tool (dead)
/ tool-wrap (impossible). Free to gate on E4B. HONEST CEILING: 4, and content-hard tasks are out of reach;
if the deterministic finder still converts 0, localization was not the true wall and the E4B prompt path

## CAP SIMULATION ON THE UNCAPPED v7 31B RUN: board caps explain the whole pool->board gap (2026-10-09 session)

Source: `comfyops/ca5-31b-full129-eval` output, re-pulled to `Outputs/v7_31b_full129/` (129 agent logs, 112
test_outputs). Script `Outputs/v7_31b_full129/_cap_sim.py`. Verdict rule = L13967 recovery rule
(>=1 passed, 0 failed/error/skipped) -> **35/129, matches the logged number exactly.** Call counting
calibrated against the harness's own `tool_calls_used` (get_status excluded from budget: 104/112 samples).
Confirmed uncapped: get_status reports `max_time_minutes: 60.0`. Prompt text still said "~28 calls / 8 min".

Each solve's commit point = call index + elapsed seconds of its final submit_patch (or last edit if never
submitted). A solve survives a cap (C calls, M min) if commit <= both.

| calls \ min | 8 | 10 | 12 | 15 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **28 (shipped)** | **24** | 27 | 28 | 28 | 29 |
| 32 | 25 | 28 | 29 | 29 | 31 |
| 36 | 26 | 29 | 30 | 30 | 32 |
| **40** | 27 | 30 | **31** | 31 | 34 |
| **50** | 28 | 31 | 32 | 32 | **35** |

### Calibration check (the important part)
At the shipped 28/8, **24/129 = 18.6% -> predicts 10.8/58 = 0.186. Observed board mean of the identical pack
= 10.6/58.** The capped 129-rate maps to the board; the uncapped one (0.27) did not. The 5-task gap is the cap.

### Where the lost solves are
- 11 of 35 solves land after call 28 or after 8 min. Time binds more than calls at 8 min (28 calls/10 min
  already gives 27).
- Late-by-time: rich_3521 (1042s, 14 calls), rich_3480 (902s), rich_3063 (660s), fastapi_14873/14419/15589
  (550-600s). Late-by-calls: fastapi_11194 (32), 14372 (34), 14616 (38), 14851 (40), rich_4070 (50).

### Caveats
- v7 ran CONC=4 on one tp=4 server; elapsed seconds include contention. Scorer concurrency unknown.
- A real cap changes get_status output (remaining budget), which the model reads. Prompt text identical.
- Scorer compute ceiling: ref 57276407 (100/60/500) threw. Sum of min(task_end, M) over 129: 12.3h at M=8
  (ships fine today), 13.8h at M=12 (+12%), 14.5h at M=20 (+18%). Relative cost is modest; absolute ceiling
  unknown.

### Recommendation
Same bytes as the board pack, change ONLY eval_config.yaml (keep system.md unchanged - the simulation is
valid precisely because the prompt said 28/8 in v7). Candidates: **40/12 -> 31/129 ~ 0.24**, **50/20 -> 35/129
~ 0.27**. 40/12 is the lower-risk first submission.

### CAP PACKS BUILT (CPU packager kernels, no GPU quota)
Builder `kaggle_pkg/_build_cap_packs.py` forks `comfyops/gemma-submit-mobile-ca5`; it first asserts the
packager's agent.yaml / sampling.yaml / system.md are byte-identical (sha256 6562a591393b / a49dbd3aab94 /
b9aeaa9a53ce) to the v7 run's `agent_ca5` files - PASSED - so the cap simulation applies to these bytes.
| kernel | eval_config | member sha1 (agent/sampling/system) | eval sha1 | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `comfyops/gemma-submit-ca5-cap40-12` | 40 calls / 12 min / 120 turns | b1663033e726 / 8f61024c4e81 / b08b32a2438d | 1657b93609c2 | 31/129 ~0.24 |
| `comfyops/gemma-submit-ca5-cap50-20` | 50 calls / 20 min / 120 turns | same | 4a060950efe6 | 35/129 ~0.27 |
Both COMPLETE, competition attached, zips pulled to `Outputs/gemma-submit-ca5-cap*/submission.zip`. Only
eval_config differs from the 0.20 pack (eval sha1 4a6b044ec65c). max_turns kept at 120 (does not bind:

Builder `kaggle_pkg/_build_31b_cap_ab.py` (forks push_129_off31 like the sibling A/B). Paired, one tp=4 31B

## RETRACTION: the cap simulation's 28/8 prediction was wrong - ENFORCED 28/8 already scores like uncapped (2026-10-09 session)

Chunk 1 of `ca5-31b-cap-ab` (10 tasks): A 40/12 = 6, B 50/20 = 6. Sim predicted 5 and 7; sim at 28/8 predicted 4.
But the data to check this was already on disk: `Outputs/ca5_31b_ab/ab31.json` = the 31B sibling A/B, which ran
the SAME ca5 bytes with caps ENFORCED at 28/8 on the same 85 live tasks:
| run | caps | round-1 on 85 live | chunk-1 tasks |
|---|---|---|---|
| v7 | none (60 min shown) | 34 | 7 |
| sibling A/B control | **28/8 enforced** | **34** (rich 15, fastapi 19) | **6** |
| sibling A/B sibling arm | 28/8 enforced | 33 | 6 |
| cap-sim prediction | 28/8 | 23 | 4 |
| cap A/B arm A / B | 40/12 / 50/20 | (running) | 6 / 6 |

**The simulation assumed a run's trajectory is the same with or without a cap and just gets truncated. False.**
Under an enforced countdown, get_status shows real remaining budget and the commit-by-remaining rules fire;
the model compresses its work and lands the same solves inside 28/8. Truncating uncapped traces measures
nothing about the capped regime. (This was the caveat I flagged and then did not check against ab31.json.)

### Consequences
- **Retracted:** "board caps explain the pool->board gap" and "40/12 -> ~0.24, 50/20 -> ~0.27".
- **The cap lever is probably null on the 31B** (34 at 28/8 vs 34 uncapped; chunk 1 6=6=6). Cap A/B still running.
- **The pool->board gap is UNEXPLAINED again:** capped 31B ~27% of the 129 predicts ~15.7/58; board mean 10.6/58.
  Remaining candidates: board tasks harder than the public 129; scorer environment (hardware/concurrency making
  the 8-min wall bite harder than on our 4xL4 at conc 4); or both.
- The two cap submission packs were NOT submitted. Good.

### LESSON
**Before trusting a counterfactual simulation, check whether the counterfactual was already measured directly.**
The enforced-28/8 run existed; one query would have refuted the sim before two kernels and two packs were built.

### Scorer-speed hypothesis, measured on the ENFORCED 28/8 traces (ab31.json A_control round 1, 34 solves)
Yesterday's timing analysis used the UNCAPPED v7 traces (the basis just retracted); this uses enforced 28/8.
Solve duration median 250s, max 540s (duration_seconds includes harness overhead beyond the 480s agent cap).
Solves after 300s: 12; after 420s: 5. If the scorer ran X times slower than our 4xL4/conc-4 rig, solves lost to
the 8-min wall: 1.25x -> 6/34, **1.5x -> 10/34**, 2x -> 17/34.
A 1.5x-slower scorer turns 27% of the 129 (15.7/58) into ~11.1/58, close to the board mean 10.6. That is a fit with one
free parameter, NOT evidence: scorer hardware/concurrency is unknown. Testable only on the board or from host docs.

### `ca5-31b-cap-ab` KILLED by user after chunk 1 - data pulled (`Outputs/ca5_31b_cap_ab/`, `_compare.py`)
10 tasks x 2 arms, chunk complete. Same 10 tasks vs enforced 28/8 (ab31 A_control r1) and uncapped v7:
| | v7 uncapped | 28/8 enforced | 40/12 | 50/20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| solved | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| median calls | - | 17 | 19 | 22 |
- 50/20 converted rich_3521 (9 calls, 902s - a pure time-bound solve, as v7 had at 1042s) but LOST fastapi_15589
  (solved in the 3 other regimes). Net 0. 40/12 = identical solve set to 28/8.
- Max calls in any arm 32 (of 40/50 allowed): the call cap is not binding on the 31B; only time binds, on ~1 task.
- Swaps of +1/-1 per 10 tasks are inside 31B per-task flip noise.
VERDICT (n=10, consistent with the full-85 28/8-vs-uncapped equality 34=34): **cap lever NULL on the 31B.**
Do not submit the cap packs. E4B companion (`e4b-cap-ab`) still running.

## E4B RETRY A/B WITH A REPRO-TEST GATE — `comfyops/e4b-repro-ab` PUSHED (2026-10-09 session)

Premise (user): E4B is far from the 12h scoring ceiling (129 tasks ~75 min on Kaggle), so budget-hungry
architectures shelved at 28/8 are now affordable. This finishes the agent investigation's open items
(L16777 fresh-retry null "needs an issue-derived repro check"; L16820 test-writer "needs samples + budget").

Bundles (`local_eval/parity_rig/_build_repro_retry.py`), both from LF ca5 (fixer.md sha1 dc742f9bb676), 80/30/200:
- **ARM F `agent_e4b_retry_fresh`** = retry2 design: LoopAgent(3)[fixer (include_contents none), verifier];
  gate = existing tests; rejected attempts undone; out of attempts -> restore best.
- **ARM R `agent_e4b_retry_repro`** = ARM F + a `tester` sub-agent (Konwinski repro_issue.py via the test-context
  skill, runs once, SKIP RULE on later iterations) + a repro block in check.py: the repro script is moved OUT of the
  workspace (never in the patch), run on the original code once (cached) and on the patch; it counts only if the
  original prints "Issue reproduced"; then a patch that does not print "Issue resolved" -> REJECTED REPRO_FAIL.
- Shared changes vs retry2: best-restore ties -> EARLIEST attempt (a bad repro test degrades to ungated attempt 1).

### BUG FOUND AND FIXED: stale bytecode in the gate (affects the earlier retry2 / gated results)
Offline gate test `_test_repro_gate.sh` (WSL, 15 checks) failed on "correct fix": the gate reverts the edit, runs
tests, re-applies within the same second; Python's .pyc check is source mtime (1 s) + size, so a SAME-SIZE edit
(`a - b` -> `a + b`) ran the ORIGINAL bytecode and a correct fix was judged as the original. The retry2/gated
check.py has the same base-vs-patch comparison -> some of the L16777 rejections may have been false. Fixed with
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for gate subprocesses + __pycache__ purge before every pytest/repro run. After fix: 15/15.

### Kernel (`kaggle_pkg/_build_e4b_repro_ab.py`)
Forks push_e4b_cap_ab (per-node, 1 E4B/L4, conc 8). node0,1 = F; node2,3 = R. Task set = **39 ever-solved** of the
85 live (`Outputs/_solvable85.json`) - the never-solved 46 cannot convert by retry. 4h budget. 1-task smoke per arm
(fastapi_14786) before the main loop. Rows now carry dur / llm calls / error (scorer-time feasibility).
Control = `e4b-cap-ab` plain ca5 LF passes restricted to the same 39 ids (caps 40/12 & 50/20, measured null vs
each other, so pooled).
### Pre-registered reads
- R >= control + 2 per pass (on 39) AND R > F -> the repro gate is the lever; check scorer time from `dur`.
- F ~ R > control -> fresh retries help, the test adds nothing.
- R < control -> false rejects / time cost dominate; inspect gate outputs in pass-1 logs.

### `e4b-cap-ab` FINAL (17 complete passes; pulled via `kaggle_pkg/_pull_slow.py` - 2,317 output files)
| arm (85 live) | passes | k per pass | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40/12 | 8 | 9,8,10,10,8,12,10,10 | 9.62 | 1.22 |
| 50/20 | 9 | 10,14,12,10,11,6,12,9,9 | 10.33 | 2.16 |
| 28/8 ref (CRLF, older) | 5 | 10,8,11,9,11 | 9.8 | 1.17 |
**VERDICT: cap lever NULL on E4B** (+0.7, inside noise). With the 31B null, the cap axis is CLOSED on both models.
Why it is null: **median E4B run uses 7 tool calls** of the 40-50 allowed - E4B stops on its own long before any cap.
Control for the repro A/B (39 ever-solved ids; every solve lies inside the 39): 17 passes, **mean 9.82, sd 1.69**.
Pass wall time drifts 37.6 -> 41.6 min mean by pass 4 on all 4 nodes (solves unaffected) - telemetry pending.
Tooling: kaggle CLI 2.2.4 -> 2.2.5. `kernels output` recurses pages with no delay -> 429 on big outputs; use
`_pull_slow.py <owner/slug> <dest> <regex> [name]` (page 100, 4 s pause, 429 backoff).

## `e4b-repro-ab` RESULT: FRESH RETRY WINS (+1.7, t=3.2); REPRO GATE LOSES (2026-10-10)

39 ever-solved live ids, E4B, per-node. Control = plain ca5 LF passes from `e4b-cap-ab` on the same ids.
| arm | passes | k on 39 | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| control plain ca5 | 17 | 9,8,10,14,12,10,10,10,11,8,10,6,11,10,10,9,9 | 9.82 | 1.69 |
| **F fresh retry** (LoopAgent[fixer,verifier], gate=existing tests, 80/30) | 16 | 12,12,12,11,12,9,12,14,12,12,13,10,10,12,11,10 | **11.50** | **1.22** |
| R repro gate (+tester, repro check) | 8 | 8,10,9,8,8,11,8,9 | 8.88 | 1.05 |
**F vs control: +1.68/pass, Welch t = 3.18** (~p 0.003) - and LOWER variance. First positive architecture result
for E4B in the project. Since the only design change vs the L16777 null (retry2, +0.02) is the stale-bytecode gate
fix + earliest-attempt tie-break, **the earlier null was largely the gate falsely rejecting correct same-size fixes.**
Per task: F gains fastapi_14077 0.29->0.88, rich_3067 0.59->1.00; loses fastapi_9555 0.76->0.44.

### Why R loses
- **Context overflow in 32% of runs** (101/312; 0 of them solved, though 71 had a patch) vs 10% in F.
- 2x the time (mean 520 s vs 259 s; 14/71 solves after 8 min) and median 23 calls vs 10.
The tester's turns accumulate in the shared LoopAgent history -> overflow kills the session's patch. CLOSED as
built; a repro gate would need context isolation (tester include_contents none + its output passed via state).

### Timing (scorer feasibility) for F
mean 259 s, median 209 s, p90 487 s, max 1066 s on the 39. Solves after 12 min: 1/184; after 15 min: 0/184.
Unsolved runs average 306 s (retries happen on failures), so the full-129 mean will be higher than on the 39.

### Remaining defect in F: 10% context overflow (64/624, all lost; 43 had a patch)
Likely the verifier (include_contents default = sees the whole history, grows across 3 iterations). Fix candidate:
verifier `include_contents: none` (it only runs the gate + submit). Untested -> next A/B, not in the ship pack.
